name: Price above its moving average (price-to-MA ratio), long or cash
summary: Hold the coin while the daily close is above its n-day simple moving average (published crypto variants n = 5 to 100 days; Faber's equity rule uses the 10-month average checked at month-end), otherwise hold cash.
data_note: Daily closes only; exchange public candles (Coinbase/Kraken/Binance) are enough. No trade or order-book data needed.

sources.citation: Detzel, Liu, Strauss, Zhou, Zhu (2021), Learning and predictability via technical analysis: evidence from bitcoin and stocks with hard-to-value fundamentals, Financial Management 50(1)
sources.finding: [A] Ratios of prices to their moving averages forecast daily Bitcoin returns in and out of sample. Working-paper break-even switching frictions of 1.1% (5-day MA) to 4.5% (100-day MA) are reported only via CXO in A-research-report.md [S].

sources.citation: Grobys, Ahmed, Sapkota (2020), Technical trading rules in the cryptocurrency market, Finance Research Letters 32
sources.finding: [A, via A-research-report.md] Price against its 20-day average, daily, on crypto; reused as a published rule definition.

sources.citation: Wei, Kyriakou, Sermpinis, Stasinakis (2024), Cryptocurrencies and lucky factors: the value of technical and fundamental analysis, International Journal of Finance & Economics 29
sources.finding: [FT, via A-research-report.md] 12 coins 2015-2022, 7,846 rules: only a short-term log price-to-MA ratio and a hashrate index show genuine in- and out-of-sample profitability after SPA and Lucky-Factors correction.

sources.citation: Levine, Pedersen (2016), Which trend is your friend?, Financial Analysts Journal 72(3)
sources.finding: [FT, via A-research-report.md] Time-series momentum and moving-average rules are equivalent representations in their general forms, so this rule is a member of the TSMOM family.

sources.citation: CXO Advisory (n.d.), 10-month SMA timing signals over the long run
sources.finding: [S, search snippet] On the S&P Composite Dec 1871 - Dec 2012, 10-month SMA timing performed similarly to buy-and-hold (0.75% vs 0.79% average monthly return). Faber's 2013 figures are in A-research-report.md section 6 [S].

sources.citation: Hudson, Urquhart (2021), Technical trading and cryptocurrencies, Annals of Operations Research 297
sources.finding: [A, via A-research-report.md] About 15,000 rules incl. moving averages: break-even costs above typical crypto costs, but no predictability for Bitcoin in the out-of-sample period.

crypto_evidence_note: Detzel (OOS) and Wei (survives data-snooping correction) are positive for short-to-medium MA ratios on daily data; Hudson & Urquhart find no BTC predictability out of sample. Profits concentrate in bull/bubble periods (Svogun & Bazan-Palomino 2022).
expected_trades_per_coin_year: About 3-10 round trips at 50-200-day averages, 15-40 at 5-20 days (estimate: whipsaw count rises as n falls; Detzel break-even frictions rise with n, consistent with fewer switches).
fee_sensitivity: At 1.10% a round trip: 100-200-day average about 3-11% a year of drag; 5-20-day average 16-44% a year. Only the slow averages leave a margin (Detzel 100-day break-even 4.5% per switch > 1.10%).
long_only_note: Natively long or cash; the published rules are long/cash.
limitations: Equivalent to TSMOM (STRAT-005) in general form; adds little unless the MA weighting differs materially
Losses at sharp V-shaped reversals; crypto samples are bull-market dominated
Choice of n is a free parameter: count every n tried as a trial
priority_reason: Daily, long/cash, few trades, two crypto studies with OOS or data-snooping-corrected support; trivial OHLCV data; tests STRAT-005's family with a different smoother.

name: Two moving-average crossover (SMA/EMA; golden cross 50/200; EMA 20/50)
summary: Long when the fast average (e.g. EMA 20 or SMA 50) is above the slow average (EMA 50 or SMA 200), cash otherwise; published crypto tests also use EMA pairs scaled by volatility.
data_note: OHLCV closes only.

sources.citation: Rozario, Holt, West, Ng (2020), A decade of evidence of trend following investing in cryptocurrencies, arXiv:2009.12155
sources.finding: [A] SMA/EMA/DEMA trend rules on BTCUSD (hourly): 255% walk-forward annualised returns; the paper assumes negligible fees, spread and slippage; authors affiliated with a crypto-derivatives exchange.

sources.citation: Rohrbach, Suremann, Osterrieder (2017), Momentum and trend following trading strategies for currencies revisited, SSRN (summary by CXO Advisory)
sources.finding: [S] Seven cryptos Mar 2015 - Mar 2017, three EMA-pair signals scaled by volatility: time-series portfolio gross average return 299%, SD 185%, Sharpe 1.62, max drawdown about -40%. CXO: returns gross, daily reformation, short and snooping-prone sample.

sources.citation: Corbet, Eraslan, Lucey, Sensoy (2019), The effectiveness of technical trading rules in cryptocurrency markets, Finance Research Letters 31
sources.finding: [FT preprint, via A-research-report.md] Variable-length MA and breakout rules on 1-minute Bitcoin; breakout rules weak (1 significant of 20).

sources.citation: Coinpaprika (2026), Which crypto indicators actually work? Testing the popular ones
sources.finding: [FT] 8 Binance USDT pairs, 23,602 daily bars from Aug 2017, no costs: 50/200 golden cross 70 fires, 7-day mean +2.26%, hit rate 48.5%, vs base +1.65%/49.9%; death cross 7-day mean +3.26%, hit 65.7%. Crossovers carried no reliable short-horizon edge.

sources.citation: Deprez, Frommel (2024), Are simple technical trading rules profitable in bitcoin markets?, International Review of Economics & Finance 93
sources.finding: [A, via A-research-report.md] 75,360 rules incl. MA classes, selected after costs with a multiple-testing procedure; out-of-sample portfolios can beat buy-and-hold, especially risk-adjusted. Cost level not in abstract.

crypto_evidence_note: Positive headline results are gross or near-zero cost and short-sample; repository result: STRAT-000 EMA 20/50 on 1h lost money net of 0.55% a side (2021-2025, 9 coins).

reference_implementations.name: bittrends (Globe Research code for Rozario et al.)

expected_trades_per_coin_year: 1h EMA 20/50: tens to 100+ round trips (repo STRAT-000 history); daily 50/200: about 1-3 (Coinpaprika: 70 golden crosses across 8 coins over ~9 years).
fee_sensitivity: Hourly versions: 30-100+ round trips = 33-110%+ a year of drag, fatal (repo confirms). Daily 50/200: about 1-3% a year, negligible.
long_only_note: Long when fast > slow, else cash. Rohrbach's portfolio weights can be negative; use the long side only.
limitations: Hourly variant already failed net of fees in the repo
Daily slow crossover lags badly at turns and is near-equivalent to price-above-MA and TSMOM
Headline crypto results are gross of costs

high_return_claim.claim: 255% walk-forward annualised (Rozario et al.); 299% gross average annual, Sharpe 1.62 (Rohrbach et al. TS portfolio); both assume no or negligible costs
high_return_claim.drawdown: about -40% (Rohrbach TS); not verified for Rozario
high_return_claim.leverage: Rohrbach weights scaled by volatility, long and short; Rozario unverified
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: Rozario reports walk-forward; neither shown to survive realistic costs or post-publication

priority_reason: Daily slow crossover is cheap to run and moderately evidenced, but it is close to STRAT-005/price-above-MA; the hourly version (STRAT-000) is fee-destroyed and should not be retested.

name: Multi-timeframe confirmation (higher-timeframe trend filter)
summary: Take lower-timeframe entries only when a higher-timeframe trend is up, e.g. hourly MACD longs only while the daily MACD is above its signal line (Elder triple-screen style).
data_note: OHLCV at two timeframes (resampled from the same feed).

sources.citation: Quantpedia (2025), How to design a simple multi-timeframe trend strategy on Bitcoin
sources.finding: [FT] BTC/USD Dec 2018 - Nov 2025, no costs stated: adding a daily MACD filter to hourly MACD longs cut trades from 2,262 to about 1,000; return 4.6% -> 6.6% a year, Sharpe 0.33 -> 0.80, max DD -23.9% -> -12.4%.

crypto_evidence_note: One practitioner BTC test shows the filter improves risk-adjusted gross results by cutting trades, but the base strategy stays hourly and fee-dominated.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Filter only; in the Quantpedia case ~140 trades a year remained at 1h.
fee_sensitivity: Halves an hourly strategy's drag but leaves it far above 1.10% x trades; useful only on daily entries with a weekly filter.
long_only_note: Veto filter on long entries.
limitations: Evidence is one gross practitioner backtest
Adds a parameter set per timeframe
Cannot rescue a fee-destroyed base rule
priority_reason: Cheap gate that only removes trades, but evidence is anecdotal; worth a variant inside the regime-gate test (weekly trend gating daily entries).

name: ADX trend-strength filter (Wilder)
summary: Take trend entries only when ADX(14) exceeds a threshold (rule of thumb 20-25; sometimes skip when ADX > ~50).
data_note: OHLCV highs/lows/closes.

sources.citation: Oxford Capital Strategies (n.d.), ADX filter test on a Donchian trend-following model
sources.finding: [FT] 42 futures, 1980-2014, Donchian 5-200 entry, ADX threshold 0-60: no value added; rated D on the vendor's A-D scale.

crypto_evidence_note: No crypto study of an ADX filter found; the repo uses it inside STRAT-001, which lost money at 1h.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Removes entries only; no trades of its own.
fee_sensitivity: Can only reduce turnover; harmless on cost, but may remove the best early-trend entries.
long_only_note: A veto filter; direction-neutral.
limitations: Lagging measure of trend strength
Threshold is a free parameter
Only evidence found is a vendor simulation, negative
priority_reason: No crypto evidence and the only systematic test found says it adds nothing; cheap to include as one variant of a gate test, not as its own study.

name: DEMA/TEMA crossover with ADX trend-strength filter
summary: Long when a double/triple exponential average crosses above a slower one and ADX(14) is above a threshold (commonly 20-25); exit on the reverse cross.
data_note: OHLCV; ADX needs highs and lows.

sources.citation: Rozario, Holt, West, Ng (2020), A decade of evidence of trend following investing in cryptocurrencies, arXiv:2009.12155
sources.finding: [A] Includes double-exponential MA rules on hourly BTCUSD; headline 255% walk-forward annualised assumes negligible costs.

sources.citation: Oxford Capital Strategies (n.d.), ADX filter test on a Donchian trend-following model, 42 futures 1980-2014
sources.finding: [FT] ADX(14) threshold swept 0-60 on a Donchian base model, with $0 and $100 round-turn costs: 'The Average Directional Index (ADX) does not add value to the base case trend-following model.' Results shown only as charts.

crypto_evidence_note: Repository: STRAT-001 at 1h made 6,825 trades on 11 coins 2021-2025 at 0.50% and lost $5,191 of $10,000; it also lost out of sample at 0.10% + 0.05% (A-research-report.md section 2). No independent crypto test of DEMA/TEMA + ADX found.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: About 60 round trips at 1h (repo: 6,825 trades / 11 coins / 4.3 years ~ 144 fills); a daily version perhaps 5-15 (estimate).
fee_sensitivity: At 1h, ~60+ round trips = ~66%+ a year: fatal, as observed. A daily version would cost ~5-17% a year.
long_only_note: Long/cash version is what the repo runs.
limitations: Faster smoothers raise turnover without evidence of extra edge
ADX filter showed no value in a 34-year futures test
Already falsified at 1h in this repo
priority_reason: Repo evidence negative at 1h; no independent evidence that DEMA/TEMA or ADX adds anything over a plain daily MA rule. Keep only as a control.

name: MACD (12/26/9) signal-line crossover
summary: Long when MACD (EMA12 - EMA26) crosses above its 9-period signal line, flat when it crosses below.
data_note: Closes only.

sources.citation: Biondo, Pluchino, Rapisarda, Helbing (2013), Are random trading strategies more successful than technical ones?, PLOS ONE 8(7)
sources.finding: [FT, via A-research-report.md] RSI, MACD and momentum rules perform on average no better than a purely random strategy on four equity indices, before costs.

sources.citation: Coinpaprika (2026), Which crypto indicators actually work? Testing the popular ones
sources.finding: [FT] 8 coins, daily, no costs: MACD bullish crossover 825 fires, 7-day mean +1.40%, hit 49.1%, below the +1.65%/49.9% base rate; the article says it stayed below base in every cut.

sources.citation: Quantpedia (2025), How to design a simple multi-timeframe trend strategy on Bitcoin
sources.finding: [FT] Long-only MACD 12/26/9 on 1h BTC/USD (Gemini), Dec 2018 - Nov 2025, 2,262 trades, no costs stated: 4.6% a year, Sharpe 0.33, max DD -23.9%.

crypto_evidence_note: Crypto tests found are community/practitioner and gross: MACD crossovers at or below the base rate; hourly MACD earned 4.6% a year before costs on 2,262 trades, which 0.55%/side fees would wipe out many times over.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: About 320 round trips at 1h (Quantpedia: 2,262 over ~7 years); daily perhaps 10-20 (estimate from Coinpaprika: 825 bullish crosses over 8 coins x ~9 years ~ 11 per coin-year).
fee_sensitivity: 1h: ~350% a year of drag, fatal. Daily: ~12-22% a year, larger than any edge reported.
long_only_note: Long/flat as tested by Quantpedia.
limitations: Fast signal, many whipsaws
Below base rate in the only multi-coin crypto tally found
No cost-inclusive crypto study found
priority_reason: Negative/weak crypto evidence and turnover the fees destroy; at most a falsification control.

name: Parabolic SAR and Ichimoku cloud
summary: PSAR (Wilder, step 0.02, max 0.20) trails price and flips on a cross; Ichimoku (9/26/52) is long when price is above the cloud and the conversion line is above the base line.
data_note: OHLCV.

sources.citation: Cohen, Qadan (2022), The complexity of cryptocurrencies algorithmic trading, Mathematics 10(12) 2037
sources.finding: [A] ML systems trading BTC, ETH, BNB and SOL with Ichimoku and other indicators, daily and minute bars: 'more indicators do not necessarily mean better trading performance'; one or two indicators did best for daily swing trades.

crypto_evidence_note: One small peer-reviewed crypto study (Ichimoku), no cost or OOS detail in the abstract; PSAR evidence found was a student thesis and vendor blogs (not verified).
expected_trades_per_coin_year: PSAR flips often: 15-40 round trips daily (estimate); Ichimoku daily 4-10 (estimate).
fee_sensitivity: PSAR ~17-44% a year of drag; Ichimoku ~4-11%.
long_only_note: Long/flat variants straightforward.
limitations: Many parameters and line definitions
Evidence thin and mostly in-sample
Ichimoku cloud is another MA/channel trend rule
priority_reason: Weak evidence; redundant with MA and Donchian trend rules already in the catalogue.

name: Supertrend (ATR band trailing trend)
summary: Trend line at (high+low)/2 +/- multiplier x ATR(period), commonly ATR 10 and multiplier 3; long while the close is above the lower band, flat on a close below it.
data_note: OHLCV.

sources.citation: Quantified Strategies (n.d.), The Supertrend indicator backtested (search summary)
sources.finding: [S, search snippet] Weekly S&P 500 from 1960 suggested it can add value as a trend tool; no crypto test, no figures read.

crypto_evidence_note: No peer-reviewed crypto study found. Repository: STRAT-002 (4h) lost out of sample even at 0.10% + 0.05% (A-research-report.md section 2, BACKTEST-REPORT-batch-1).
expected_trades_per_coin_year: About 20-40 round trips at 4h (estimate); 5-12 daily (estimate).
fee_sensitivity: 4h: ~22-44% a year of drag; daily: ~6-13%. Daily variant is functionally an ATR trailing exit, already covered by OVL-ATR + STRAT-004.
long_only_note: Long/flat.
limitations: No academic evidence
Repo result negative at 4h
Overlaps OVL-ATR and the Donchian exit
priority_reason: Anecdotal evidence, negative repo result; the useful part (ATR trailing exit) already exists as OVL-ATR.

name: Donchian channel breakout (Turtle System 1 20/10 and System 2 55/20)
summary: Enter long on a close/break above the n-day high (20 for S1, 55 for S2); exit on a break below the m-day low (10 or 20); Turtles added 2 x ATR(20) stops and unit pyramiding.
data_note: Daily highs, lows, closes; ATR for stops/sizing.

sources.citation: Gerritsen, Bouri, Ramezanifar, Roubaud (2020), The profitability of technical trading rules in the Bitcoin market, Finance Research Letters 34
sources.finding: [A, via A-research-report.md] Daily Bitcoin 2010-2019: the trading-range breakout rule has significant forecasting power and outperforms in strongly trending markets.

sources.citation: Garner (2010), Tuning up the turtle, Active Trader (citing C. Faith, The Original Turtle Trading Rules)
sources.finding: [FT, via A-research-report.md; third-party PDF copy located 2026-11-11] System 1 backtest 72% a year with a 66% drawdown, essentially unprofitable since the early 1990s; slower variants held up better.

sources.citation: TurtleTrader.com (n.d.), The Original Turtle Trading Rules
sources.finding: [S, search snippet] System 1: 20-day breakout entry (skipped after a winning S1 trade), 10-day opposite-extreme exit; System 2: 55-day entry, 20-day exit, all breakouts taken.

sources.citation: Corbet, Eraslan, Lucey, Sensoy (2019), The effectiveness of technical trading rules in cryptocurrency markets, Finance Research Letters 31
sources.finding: [FT preprint, via A-research-report.md] On 1-minute Bitcoin, trading-range breakouts were weak: 1 significant result of 20.

sources.citation: Wei, Kyriakou, Sermpinis, Stasinakis (2024), Cryptocurrencies and lucky factors, International Journal of Finance & Economics 29
sources.finding: [FT, via A-research-report.md] Short channel-breakout rules strong in-sample but not consistently out of sample.

crypto_evidence_note: Daily breakouts positive on BTC (Gerritsen) and in long-only portfolios (Zarattini 2025, WP); intraday breakouts weak. Repository: STRAT-004 (55/20) netted +23.6% over 4.3 years on 9 coins at 0.55%/side and beat random entries, but stayed below buy-and-hold (+27%).
expected_trades_per_coin_year: S2 55/20: about 2.7-4 round trips; S1 20/10: about 7-8 (Zarattini Bitcoin counts: 78 trades at 20 days and 28 at 60 days over Jan 2015 - Mar 2025).
fee_sensitivity: S2: ~3-4% a year of drag, survivable; S1: ~8-9% a year, marginal.
long_only_note: Long breakouts only; exit to cash.
limitations: Below buy-and-hold in the repo's bull-dominated sample
Turtle S1 decayed after publication
Few trades per coin: low statistical power per coin

high_return_claim.claim: Turtle System 1 backtest 72% a year (Garner 2010, practitioner, futures)
high_return_claim.period: Original Turtle era, futures (exact span in Garner)
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: Essentially unprofitable since the early 1990s per Garner: did not survive

priority_reason: Best repository result so far, daily, few trades, long-only native, positive crypto evidence; continue paper observation and compare with the ensemble variant.

name: Long-only Donchian ensemble with ratcheting midline stop and volatility sizing (Zarattini, Pagani, Barbon 2025)
summary: Long when the close is the highest close of the last n days, for n from 5 to 360 averaged into an ensemble; exit at the first close below a trailing stop that starts at the channel midline and never moves down; size min(25%/sigma_90d, 200%).
data_note: Daily OHLCV for each coin; 90-day volatility.

sources.citation: Zarattini, Pagani, Barbon (2025), Catching crypto trends: a tactical approach for Bitcoin and altcoins, Swiss Finance Institute RP 25-80 / SSRN 5209907
sources.finding: [FT, via A-research-report.md] 10-coin long-only book net of 10 bp: Sharpe 1.50, max DD 12%; long-short 1.18. At 50 bp the 5-day model's CAGR falls from 34% to 18% while longer lookbacks are less affected. Survivorship-free universe (C-evidence.md); settings chosen after exploration, no multiple-testing correction.

sources.citation: CXO Advisory (2025), Crypto-asset trend following strategies (summary of Zarattini et al.)
sources.finding: [S, via C-evidence.md] About 18% net CAGR and about 11% a year net alpha versus BTC at 10 bp.

sources.citation: Concretum Group / Pagani (2025), Seasonality in Bitcoin intraday trend trading
sources.finding: [FT] Same group: a volatility-targeted long-only BTC portfolio at 20% target volatility had Sharpe just below 0.8 (2018-2025), the comparison point for their trend models.

crypto_evidence_note: The closest published design to this app (long-only, daily, crypto, survivorship-free), but a practitioner-led working paper; account costs (55 bp) are above the highest level tested (50 bp).
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Per lookback (BTC, Jan 2015 - Mar 2025): 5d 292, 10d 156, 20d 78, 30d 49, 60d 28, 90d 20, 150d 15, 250d 9, 360d 5 trades; i.e. ~0.5-29 a year. An ensemble restricted to n >= 20 averages ~2-8 a year.
fee_sensitivity: Drop n < 20: the 5-10-day members cost 15-30%+ a year at 1.10% a round trip. Volatility re-sizing adds turnover unless a no-trade band (Zarattini used 20%) is applied.
long_only_note: Published as long-only; cap sizing at 100% on spot (no leverage).
limitations: Working paper, practitioner authors, no multiple-testing correction
Headline at 10 bp; 55 bp untested
Up to 200% sizing in the paper is not available on spot

high_return_claim.claim: 10-coin long-only portfolio Sharpe 1.50, about 18% net CAGR, about 11% a year net alpha vs BTC, at 10 bp costs
high_return_claim.leverage: Position size up to 200% of allocation (min(25%/sigma, 200%))
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: No formal holdout reported; working paper of April 2025, no post-publication evidence yet

priority_reason: Best-matched published evidence for long-only daily crypto; extends STRAT-004 with the ratchet stop (OVL-RATCHET exists) and multi-lookback ensemble; OHLCV only.

name: Nearness to 52-week / all-time high (George-Hwang anchoring)
summary: Rank or gate coins by close / max(close over 252 or 365 days); hold coins near their 52-week high (George & Hwang sort stocks on this ratio); the single-coin form is a 250-360-day Donchian entry.
data_note: Daily closes; needs 1 year of history (HYPE only from late 2024).

sources.citation: George, Hwang (2004), The 52-week high and momentum investing, Journal of Finance 59(5)
sources.finding: [A, search snippet] Nearness to the 52-week high forecasts returns better than past returns, and its forecasts do not reverse in the long run (US equities).

sources.citation: Li, Urquhart, Wang, Zhang (2021), MAX momentum in cryptocurrency markets, International Review of Financial Analysis 77
sources.finding: [A] Coins with higher maximum daily returns earn higher subsequent returns ('MAX momentum'), the reverse of equities; varies with market state and sentiment. Cross-sectional, related evidence of continuation after extremes.

sources.citation: Zarattini, Pagani, Barbon (2025), Catching crypto trends, SSRN 5209907
sources.finding: [FT, via A-research-report.md] The 250- and 360-day highest-close entries produced 9 and 5 BTC trades over Jan 2015 - Mar 2025.

crypto_evidence_note: No direct crypto test of 52-week-high proximity found; related crypto evidence (MAX momentum, long Donchian lookbacks) points to continuation.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: As a single-coin entry: 0.5-1 round trips (Zarattini 250-360d counts); as a weekly ranking: depends on band rule.
fee_sensitivity: Negligible as an entry rule (<1.5% a year); a weekly ranking without a band could reach 20%+ a year.
long_only_note: Long the names nearest their highs; cash otherwise.
limitations: Equity evidence; crypto evidence only indirect
HYPE lacks a full year of history until late 2025
Very few trades: weak per-coin statistics
priority_reason: Plausible and cheap, but no direct crypto evidence; best tested as the long-lookback member of the Donchian ensemble rather than separately.

name: Intraday / opening-range breakout and intraday trend
summary: Trade intraday breakouts of an opening range or short intraday channel, closing by day end; Concretum's version is an ensemble of high-frequency trend models, volatility-targeted to 20%.
data_note: Intraday OHLCV (1-minute to 1-hour); free from exchange APIs but long minute histories need bulk downloads.

sources.citation: Concretum Group / Pagani (2025), Seasonality in Bitcoin intraday trend trading
sources.finding: [FT] Long-short ensemble of high-frequency trend models on BTC 2018-2025, volatility-targeted: gross-of-fees Sharpe about 1.6; no cost figure given.

sources.citation: Corbet, Eraslan, Lucey, Sensoy (2019), The effectiveness of technical trading rules in cryptocurrency markets, Finance Research Letters 31
sources.finding: [FT preprint, via A-research-report.md] 1-minute Bitcoin trading-range breakouts: 1 significant result of 20.

crypto_evidence_note: Gross practitioner results are positive for a long-short intraday ensemble; the academic minute-bar breakout test is weak; nothing net of retail fees.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: 100-365+ round trips (one or more per day).
fee_sensitivity: ~110-400%+ a year of drag at 1.10% a round trip: fatal.
long_only_note: Long side can be run alone, but the published edge is long-short and gross.
limitations: Turnover far beyond what 0.55%/side allows
Published edge is long-short and gross
Needs intraday execution reliability
priority_reason: Fee-destroyed at this account's costs; keep only as a documented negative.

name: Time-series momentum (sign of past 1-12-month return), decided weekly or monthly
summary: Long if the past lookback return (published: 12 months; Hurst et al. average of 1, 3 and 12 months; STRAT-005 uses 30/90/365 days) is positive, cash otherwise, volatility-scaled in the futures literature.
data_note: Daily closes; 365-day lookback needs a year of history (HYPE short).

sources.citation: Moskowitz, Ooi, Pedersen (2012), Time series momentum, Journal of Financial Economics 104(2)
sources.finding: [FT, via A-research-report.md] Significant TSMOM in all 58 liquid futures; persists 1-12 months, partially reverses later; returns before costs.

sources.citation: Hurst, Ooi, Pedersen (2017), A century of evidence on trend-following investing, Journal of Portfolio Management 44(1)
sources.finding: [FT, via A-research-report.md] 67 markets 1880-2016, positive in every decade after estimated costs and fees.

sources.citation: Huang, Li, Wang, Zhou (2020), Time series momentum: is it there?, Journal of Financial Economics 135(3)
sources.finding: [A, via A-research-report.md] Asset-by-asset tests show little evidence of TSMOM in- or out-of-sample.

sources.citation: Liu, Tsyvinski (2021), Risks and returns of cryptocurrency, Review of Financial Studies 34(6)
sources.finding: [A/FT WP, via A-research-report.md] Strong time-series momentum: weekly returns predict the next one to four weeks; mostly in-sample predictive regressions.

sources.citation: Borgards (2021), Dynamic time series momentum of cryptocurrencies, North American Journal of Economics and Finance 57
sources.finding: [A, via A-research-report.md] Crypto TSMOM benchmarked against buy-and-hold.

crypto_evidence_note: Strong long-history evidence outside crypto; crypto evidence positive but short-sample and mostly in-sample or gross (Liu & Tsyvinski); asset-by-asset critiques (Huang et al.; Kim, Tse, Wald 2016 on volatility scaling) apply.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: About 2-6 round trips with weekly decisions on 30-365-day lookbacks (A report: a few switches a year at 3-12-month horizons).
fee_sensitivity: ~2-7% a year of drag; survivable. Volatility re-scaling must use a wide no-trade band.
long_only_note: Long/cash; NBIM (2014) finds most futures TSMOM return from the long signals.
limitations: Without volatility scaling, TSMOM and buy-and-hold had similar cumulative returns (Kim, Tse, Wald 2016)
Loses at sharp trend reversals
Lookback choice is a trial
priority_reason: Strongest general evidence of any rule here, weekly decisions, few trades, long/cash; already implemented, so the priority is evaluation, not building.

name: Dual momentum (absolute + relative; Antonacci-style rotation with cash)
summary: Each week hold the asset with the higher X-week return among candidates (e.g. BTC vs gold, or BTC vs ETH) only if that return is above 0, otherwise cash; Quantpedia's BTC/gold version uses 4/8/12 weeks, rebalanced Wednesdays.
data_note: Weekly closes of each candidate asset; a non-crypto asset (gold) would need another data source and is not tradable on these exchanges, so the spot-crypto form compares coins or coin vs cash.

sources.citation: Quantpedia (2026), Dual momentum allocation between physical gold and Bitcoin (digital gold)
sources.finding: [FT] Dec 2018 - Apr 2026, weekly: 8-week pure variant 79.91% a year, Sharpe 1.64, max DD -43.94%; vol-capped composite 12.01%, Sharpe 1.37, max DD -12.27%. No transaction costs stated; lookbacks chosen on the full sample; no out-of-sample test.

crypto_evidence_note: One practitioner backtest, gross and in-sample; no peer-reviewed crypto test of dual momentum found.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: About 4-12 switches a year with weekly decisions on 4-12-week lookbacks (estimate; not reported by the source).
fee_sensitivity: ~4-13% a year of drag (each switch between two coins is 2 fills = 1.10%); survivable only with the slower lookbacks.
long_only_note: Natively long-only with cash; on these exchanges the candidate set is coins (e.g. BTC vs ETH) plus cash.
limitations: Single practitioner backtest, in-sample, gross
Gold not tradable on the app's exchanges
Concentrated: one asset at a time

high_return_claim.claim: 79.91% a year, Sharpe 1.64 (8-week BTC/gold variant), no costs
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: No; lookbacks chosen on the full sample

priority_reason: Long-only by design, weekly, low turnover, OHLCV only, and a natural extension of STRAT-005 to a BTC/ETH/cash choice; evidence is only anecdotal.

name: Intraday time-series momentum (early-day return predicts late-day return)
summary: Take the sign of the first part of the day's Bitcoin return as the signal for the last part of the day (Shen, Urquhart, Wang); close by end of day.
data_note: Intraday OHLCV.

sources.citation: Shen, Urquhart, Wang (2022), Bitcoin intraday time series momentum, Financial Review 57(2)
sources.finding: [A, via A-research-report.md and C-evidence.md] Economic gains in market timing, strongest in downturns; linked to liquidity provision and high-volume, high-volatility periods. Not net of retail fees.

crypto_evidence_note: Effect documented on Bitcoin, but the gains are intraday-sized and strongest in downturns (where long-only cannot short).
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Up to ~365 round trips (one decision a day).
fee_sensitivity: ~400% a year of drag at 1.10% per round trip if every signal is traded: fatal.
long_only_note: Only the up-signal days are tradable; the paper's best periods are downturns.
limitations: Daily round trips
Strongest on the short side
Single coin
priority_reason: Real effect but per-trade size cannot clear 1.10% a round trip; falsification at most.

name: Cross-sectional momentum factor (winners minus losers)
summary: Each week sort coins on the past 1-4-week return; long the top quantile and short the bottom quantile, hold one week (Liu, Tsyvinski, Wu); Dobrynskaya finds momentum up to 2-4 weeks and reversal beyond one month.
data_note: Synchronised daily closes for every coin in the universe; published universes are hundreds to thousands of coins.

sources.citation: Liu, Tsyvinski, Wu (2022), Common risk factors in cryptocurrency, Journal of Finance 77(2)
sources.finding: [A; NBER WP FT pp.1-4, via A-research-report.md] Weekly quintile sorts 2014-2018, coins above $1m cap, long-short: weekly excess returns 2.7%-4.1% before costs.

sources.citation: Fieberg, Liedtke, Zaremba (2024), Cryptocurrency anomalies and economic constraints, International Review of Financial Analysis 94
sources.finding: [A, via A-research-report.md] Momentum prevails in larger coins but incurs substantial trading costs and extracts alpha largely from short positions; fades over time.

sources.citation: Dobrynskaya (2023), Cryptocurrency momentum and reversal, Journal of Alternative Investments 26(1)
sources.finding: [A] ~2,000 largest coins 2014-2020: momentum at horizons up to 2-4 weeks, significant reversal beyond one month, reversal driven by past losers; costs not mentioned in the abstract.

sources.citation: Grobys, Sapkota (2019), Cryptocurrencies and momentum, Economics Letters 180
sources.finding: [A, via A-research-report.md] 143 coins: no evidence of significant momentum payoffs.

sources.citation: Rohrbach, Suremann, Osterrieder (2017), via CXO Advisory
sources.finding: [S] Seven cryptos, daily long top-3 / short bottom-3: gross average annual return 359%, Sharpe 1.48, max DD about -70% (Mar 2015 - Mar 2017); costs excluded.

crypto_evidence_note: Positive in broad, small-coin-heavy universes before costs; among large coins the alpha is mostly from shorts and eaten by costs (Fieberg); one study finds none (Grobys & Sapkota).
expected_trades_per_coin_year: 52 rebalances a year; with 9 coins and k=3, about 17 round trips per coin-slot a year if one name changes weekly (A report estimate).
fee_sensitivity: About 19% a year of drag at k=3 with one swap a week (A report); the short leg is impossible on spot.
long_only_note: The factor needs shorting; see relative_strength.top-k-rotation for the long-only form.
limitations: Short leg not available on spot
Published alpha concentrated in small illiquid coins
Momentum crashes in rebounds (Daniel & Moskowitz 2016)

high_return_claim.claim: Weekly long-short excess returns 2.7%-4.1% before costs (Liu, Tsyvinski, Wu); 359% gross annual (Rohrbach et al.)
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: Fieberg et al. (2024): effect fades over time and is mostly from shorts after costs

priority_reason: Requires shorting; the long-only remnant is catalogued separately.

name: BTC/ETH leadership as a timing input (lagged BTC return predicts altcoins)
summary: Use BTC's (or ETH's) lagged return or trend as a gate or feature for altcoin entries; Guo et al. predict each coin from other coins' lagged returns with adaptive LASSO.
data_note: OHLCV of all coins at aligned timestamps (Coinbase, Kraken, Binance Vision).

sources.citation: Sifat, Mohamad, Shariff (2019), Lead-lag relationship between Bitcoin and Ethereum: evidence from hourly and daily data, Research in International Business and Finance 50
sources.finding: [A] Aug 2017 - Sep 2018, VECM/Granger/wavelets: mostly bi-directional causality; intraday traders can hardly exploit BTC-ETH price discovery at hourly or daily frequency.

sources.citation: Guo, Sang, Tu, Wang (2024), Cross-cryptocurrency return predictability, Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control 163
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence.md] Other coins' lagged returns predict a coin's return out of sample; working-paper long-short 2.16% a day after costs, which C-evidence.md flags as implausible.

sources.citation: Guo, L., Sang, B., Tu, J., Wang, Y. (2024), Cross-cryptocurrency return predictability, Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control 163
sources.finding: [A, reused from C-evidence] Other coins' lagged returns predict a coin's return (slow information diffusion); the working paper reports a long-short 2.16% a day out of sample after costs - size implausible, treat with caution.

sources.citation: Sifat, I.M., Mohamad, A., Mohamed Shariff, M.S. (2019), Lead-lag relationship between Bitcoin and Ethereum: evidence from hourly and daily data, Research in International Business and Finance 50, 306-321
sources.finding: [A] Aug 2017 to Sep 2018 hourly and daily data: largely bi-directional causality between BTC and ETH; intraday traders 'can barely exploit' the price-discovery process.

crypto_evidence_note: Predictability reported, but BTC-ETH leadership is bi-directional and hard to exploit; the large published profits are long-short.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: As a gate: removes trades only. As a daily signal: tens to hundreds (estimate).
fee_sensitivity: Only usable as a slow gate/feature; as a daily signal the per-trade effect is far below 1.10%.
long_only_note: Usable as a veto on long altcoin entries when BTC is weak.
limitations: Lead-lag is short-lived and bi-directional
Large published profits require shorting
Overlaps the BTC 200-day regime gate
Main positive result is long-short and cross-sectional
Effect likely shrank as markets became more efficient
Overlaps fork 1's relative-strength candidates and the OVL-REGIME BTC gate

high_return_claim.claim: Long-short 2.16% a day out of sample after costs (Guo et al. working paper)
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: Reported OOS; size flagged implausible in C-evidence.md

priority_reason: Already a signal_fusion input; evidence says the timing value is small for a long-only daily trader. (Merged with momentum.cross-coin-lead-lag.)

name: Coin/BTC ratio trend (relative-strength line)
summary: Hold an altcoin only while its price in BTC (coin/BTC) is above its n-day average or has a positive n-day return; otherwise hold BTC or cash.
data_note: Coin/USD and BTC/USD closes (or coin/BTC pairs).

sources.citation: Dobrynskaya (2023), Cryptocurrency momentum and reversal, Journal of Alternative Investments 26(1)
sources.finding: [A] Relative (cross-sectional) momentum to 2-4 weeks and reversal beyond a month: relative-strength persistence is short-lived.

sources.citation: Liu, Tsyvinski, Wu (2022), Common risk factors in cryptocurrency, Journal of Finance 77(2)
sources.finding: [A, via A-research-report.md] A crypto market factor plus size and momentum explain the cross-section: coin returns share a strong common component.

crypto_evidence_note: No direct test of a coin/BTC ratio trend rule found; inferred from cross-sectional momentum evidence.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: About 4-12 switches a year at 50-100-day ratio averages (estimate).
fee_sensitivity: Switching coin->BTC costs 2 fills (1.10%); ~4-13% a year of drag.
long_only_note: Long the stronger of coin/BTC, or cash.
limitations: No direct evidence
Correlated coins: ratio trends are noisy
Doubles fills per switch
priority_reason: Cheap OHLCV test that targets the 'below buy-and-hold' problem, but no direct evidence.

name: Long-only top-k rotation among the traded coins
summary: Weekly, rank the 9 coins on past 1-4-week (or 30-90-day) return and hold the top k equal-weighted, moving to cash when the leaders' own trend is negative; swap only if a new coin leads by a margin (rank band).
data_note: Synchronised daily closes for all 9 coins; HYPE has a short history.

sources.citation: Fieberg, Liedtke, Zaremba (2024), Cryptocurrency anomalies and economic constraints, International Review of Financial Analysis 94
sources.finding: [A, via A-research-report.md] Momentum in larger coins earns mostly from short positions and incurs substantial trading costs; long-only forgoes most of the alpha.

sources.citation: Tzouvanas, Kizys, Tsend-Ayush (2020), Momentum trading in cryptocurrencies: short-term returns and diversification benefits, Economics Letters 191
sources.finding: [A, via A-research-report.md] Twelve coins: short-term momentum that fades at longer horizons.

sources.citation: Dobrynskaya (2023), Cryptocurrency momentum and reversal, Journal of Alternative Investments 26(1)
sources.finding: [A] Momentum to 2-4 weeks, reversal beyond one month: lookbacks above a month may pick future laggards.

crypto_evidence_note: Evidence is long-short and small-coin heavy; with 9 large coins sharing one strong common factor, the long-only top-k benefit is unproven.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Up to 52 rebalances; with a rank band, perhaps 10-25 swaps a year across the book (estimate).
fee_sensitivity: About 19% a year of drag at k = 3 with one swap a week (A report); a rank band and minimum hold are mandatory.
long_only_note: Long-only by construction; the benchmark is equal-weighted buy-and-hold of the same coins.
limitations: Needs a strategy interface that sees all coins at once (not in the app)
Few coins: quintiles of 2
Weekly turnover vs 1.10% round trip
priority_reason: Plausible but evidence is mostly long-short and cost-sensitive; needs a portfolio interface before testing.

name: Bollinger Bands (20, 2) reversion
summary: Buy when the close falls below the lower band (20-period SMA - 2 SD), exit at the middle band or upper band.
data_note: Closes.

sources.citation: Lento, Gradojevic, Wright (2007), Investment information content in Bollinger Bands?, Applied Financial Economics Letters 3(4)
sources.finding: [A, via A-research-report.md] After transaction costs, Bollinger Bands are consistently unable to beat buy-and-hold.

sources.citation: Day, Cheng, Huang, Ni (2023), Bollinger Bands trading on Bitcoin futures, Applied Economics Letters 30(11)
sources.finding: [A, search snippet] Bitcoin futures: average holding-period return over 20% with the 20-day MA and above 50% with a 60-day MA; futures margin; costs and drawdown not seen.

sources.citation: Coinpaprika (2026), Which crypto indicators actually work? Testing the popular ones
sources.finding: [FT] 8 coins daily, no costs: close below lower band 7-day mean +1.20% (below the +1.65% base), close above upper band +5.27% (30-day +18.09%): band breaks upward behaved as momentum.

crypto_evidence_note: One futures study positive (leveraged, cost detail unseen); multi-coin daily tally shows the lower-band buy underperforming the base rate and upper-band breaks continuing.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Daily: about 15 lower-band touches a coin a year before de-clustering (Coinpaprika 1,211 / 8 coins / ~9 years); hourly far more.
fee_sensitivity: ~5-17% a year of drag daily; per-trade gross edge found is below the base rate, so negative net.
long_only_note: Long-only buy-the-lower-band is possible; the squeeze/upper-band breakout variant belongs to the volatility family.
limitations: Reversion against a trending asset class
Day et al. is futures with margin
Original source of the 20/2 convention not verified

high_return_claim.claim: Average holding-period return >20% (20-day MA) and >50% (60-day MA) on Bitcoin futures (Day et al. 2023)
high_return_claim.leverage: Futures margin; authors note returns on margin would be higher
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: Not verified

priority_reason: Reversion evidence weak or negative for large coins; keep as a falsification control.

name: Candlestick patterns (engulfing, harami, hammer, doji, stars, etc.)
summary: Enter on classical one- to three-bar reversal or continuation patterns (e.g. bullish engulfing after a decline), hold for a fixed horizon or until an opposite pattern.
data_note: OHLC of each bar; pattern definitions need a trend context.

sources.citation: Ho, Chan, Pan, Li (2022), Do candlestick patterns work in cryptocurrency trading?, 2021 IEEE International Conference on Big Data
sources.finding: [A] 68 common patterns on daily OHLC of the top 23 coins: patterns are 'of little use in cryptocurrency trading'; more patterns show low than high accuracy.

sources.citation: Cohen (2021), Optimizing candlesticks patterns for Bitcoin's trading systems, Review of Quantitative Finance and Accounting 57(3)
sources.finding: [A] BTC 2012 - Jul 2020: of three classical patterns only Engulfing was useful (profit factor 3.54); reversed Harami and reversed Kicker (74.36% winners, PF 6.92) profitable after the author modified the patterns: an in-sample optimisation.

crypto_evidence_note: The broad multi-coin test is negative; the positive BTC study optimised and reversed patterns in-sample. Equity evidence (Marshall, Young, Rose 2006) is reported negative but was not read here.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Daily: 10-50 pattern signals a year depending on the set (estimate).
fee_sensitivity: ~11-55% a year of drag for daily pattern trading with short holds.
long_only_note: Bullish patterns only.
limitations: Pattern definitions vary; many trials
Positive results are in-sample optimisations
Short holds vs 1.10% round trip
priority_reason: Negative broad evidence; FDS-SIG-003 already frames them as candidates to be falsified, not strategies.

name: Chart patterns (head-and-shoulders, double tops/bottoms, triangles) by kernel smoothing
summary: Detect geometric patterns on kernel-smoothed prices (Lo, Mamaysky, Wang) and trade the conditional return distribution after each pattern.
data_note: Daily closes.

sources.citation: Lo, Mamaysky, Wang (2000), Foundations of technical analysis: computational algorithms, statistical inference, and empirical implementation, Journal of Finance 55(4)
sources.finding: [A] Automated kernel-regression pattern recognition on US stocks 1962-1996: several technical patterns provide incremental information about the return distribution and may have some practical value; not a trading-profit test.

crypto_evidence_note: No crypto study of systematic chart-pattern trading found.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: A few to ~10 patterns a coin a year (estimate).
fee_sensitivity: Low turnover, but the published effect is a distributional shift, not a cost-covering edge.
long_only_note: Bullish completions only.
limitations: Pattern detection has many free parameters
Evidence is distributional, equities, pre-2000
Rare events: little statistical power on 9 coins
priority_reason: No crypto evidence and many free parameters for few events.

name: RSI(14) oversold/overbought (buy below 30, sell above 70)
summary: Buy when RSI(14) falls below 30, sell when it rises above 70 (Wilder's conventional thresholds).
data_note: Closes only.

sources.citation: Coinpaprika (2026), Which crypto indicators actually work? Testing the popular ones
sources.finding: [FT] 8 coins daily from Aug 2017, no costs: RSI < 30 (889 fires, 158 independent episodes) 7-day mean +2.46%, hit 59.7% vs base +1.65%/49.9%, but 30-day mean +7.37% below the +8.65% base; RSI > 70 was more bullish (7-day +6.26%, 30-day +21.13%): overbought behaved as momentum, not reversal.

sources.citation: Biondo, Pluchino, Rapisarda, Helbing (2013), Are random trading strategies more successful than technical ones?, PLOS ONE 8(7)
sources.finding: [FT, via A-research-report.md] RSI rules no better than random on four equity indices, before costs.

crypto_evidence_note: The only multi-coin crypto tally found is gross and suggests 'sell above 70' is wrong-way for these coins; large coins show daily/weekly continuation (Zaremba 2021; Ficura 2023 in A report).
expected_trades_per_coin_year: About 2-4 independent oversold episodes a year daily (Coinpaprika: 158 episodes over 8 coins x ~9 years); hourly, dozens.
fee_sensitivity: Daily: ~2-5% a year of drag but the 30-day edge is negative; hourly versions fatal.
long_only_note: Buy oversold, exit overbought: long-only possible, but the exit rule cuts winners in trends.
limitations: Thresholds 30/70 have no verified original source (A report)
Exit at 70 conflicts with observed momentum
Gross, single community test
priority_reason: Evidence negative for these coins at useful horizons; keep as a falsification control.

name: RSI(2) pullback in an uptrend (Connors and Alvarez)
summary: Buy when the close is above the 200-day SMA and RSI(2) is 5 or lower (looser: below 10), entering near the close; exit on a close above the 5-day SMA; Connors advocates no stop-loss.
data_note: Daily closes.

sources.citation: StockCharts ChartSchool (n.d.), RSI(2) strategy
sources.finding: [FT] Rules as above (long: above 200-day SMA, RSI(2) <= 5; exit above 5-day SMA; short mirror at 95 below the 200-day). Warns against curve fitting; no statistical results.

sources.citation: CXO Advisory (n.d.), A few notes on Short Term Trading Strategies That Work (Connors)
sources.finding: [FT] Book tests mostly daily US stocks and the S&P 500, 1995-2007; CXO: no data-snooping control, no out-of-sample or subperiod tests, no friction sensitivity.

crypto_evidence_note: No crypto test found. Large coins show short-horizon continuation rather than reversal (A report), which works against the rule.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: About 5-15 round trips a year with holds of a few days (estimate from equity use; not reported for crypto).
fee_sensitivity: ~6-17% a year of drag; average equity wins reported by blogs are around 1%, below the 1.10% round-trip cost.
long_only_note: Long side only; the 200-day filter suits long-only.
limitations: Equity-derived, no crypto evidence
No stop: large losses possible in crashes
Small average gain per trade vs 1.10% cost
priority_reason: No crypto evidence, per-trade edge in equities is below this account's round-trip cost, and large coins trend rather than revert.

name: Short-term reversal / buy the dip after an overreaction
summary: Buy after an abnormally large one-day fall (e.g. beyond a multiple of the average absolute daily change) or after the worst weekly return, exit after a fixed hold or rebound.
data_note: OHLCV.

sources.citation: Caporale, Plastun (2018), Price overreactions in the cryptocurrency market, CESifo Working Paper 6861 (journal version 2019)
sources.finding: [A, search snippet] BTC, LTC, XRP, DASH daily 28.04.2013-31.12.2017: next-day moves after overreactions are larger; a counter-movement strategy is not profitable, while an inertia strategy appears profitable but is not statistically different from random.

sources.citation: Zaremba, Bilgin, Long, Mercik, Szczygielski (2021), Up or down? Short-term reversal, momentum, and liquidity effects in cryptocurrency markets, International Review of Financial Analysis 78
sources.finding: [A, via A-research-report.md] Daily reversal comes from illiquid coins; the largest, most tradeable coins exhibit daily momentum instead.

sources.citation: Kitron, Wengrowicz (2026), Short-horizon mean reversion in cryptocurrency markets, arXiv:2608.21888
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence.md] 15-minute reversal in about 90% of 183 Binance pairs, but the gross edge is about 1.3 bp a trade, too small to clear costs.

sources.citation: Dobrynskaya (2023), Cryptocurrency momentum and reversal, Journal of Alternative Investments 26(1)
sources.finding: [A] Cross-sectional reversal appears beyond one month and is driven by past losers (long-short).

crypto_evidence_note: For large coins at daily/weekly horizons the evidence shows continuation; reversal exists intraday but at ~1.3 bp gross, ~85x below this account's round-trip cost.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Daily overreaction rule: about 5-20 (estimate); 15-minute: thousands.
fee_sensitivity: Daily: ~5-22% a year of drag against an edge not distinguishable from random; intraday fatal.
long_only_note: Buying dips is long-only; the legacy DCA ladder is a form of it.
limitations: Large coins continue rather than revert at these horizons
Averaging down concentrates risk in falling assets
Intraday effect too small for fees
priority_reason: Evidence negative for these coins and horizons; useful only as a falsification test and as a check on the legacy DCA logic.

name: Stochastic oscillator (%K 14, %D 3) and Williams %R (14)
summary: Buy when %K (or %R) is in the oversold zone (stochastic below 20; %R below -80) and turns up; sell in the overbought zone (above 80; %R above -20).
data_note: OHLCV highs/lows/closes.

sources.citation: KuCoin Learn (n.d.), What is Williams %R and how to use it in crypto trading
sources.finding: [S, search snippet] Definition only: %R near 0 when closing near the high, near -100 near the low; -80/-20 zones; no performance statistics.

crypto_evidence_note: No peer-reviewed or systematic crypto test of either oscillator was found.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Daily: 10-25 signals a year (estimate; fast oscillators).
fee_sensitivity: ~11-28% a year of drag daily; hourly fatal.
long_only_note: Long-only oversold buys possible.
limitations: No evidence found
Same reversal logic as RSI, which the crypto evidence contradicts for large coins
priority_reason: No evidence; redundant with RSI reversion; falsification at most.

name: Long-only spread rotation (hold the cheap leg of a pair, or cash)
summary: Spot-only remnant of pairs trading: when a cointegrated pair's spread is extreme, switch an existing holding from the rich coin to the cheap coin (or from cash into the cheap coin), switching back at convergence.
data_note: Synchronised OHLCV of both coins.

sources.citation: Fil, Kristoufek (2020), Pairs trading in cryptocurrency markets, IEEE Access 8
sources.finding: [A, search snippet] Daily distance pairs earn -0.07% a month; mean reversion is an intraday phenomenon.

sources.citation: Sifat, Mohamad, Shariff (2019), Lead-lag relationship between Bitcoin and Ethereum, Research in International Business and Finance 50
sources.finding: [A] BTC-ETH price discovery is hard to exploit at hourly or daily frequency.

crypto_evidence_note: No direct test of the long-only form found; [R] it keeps only half of the spread return and adds full directional exposure to the cheap leg, while each switch costs 1.10%.

reference_implementations.name: statsmodels (cointegration tests) - not confirmed on the page read

expected_trades_per_coin_year: Daily: perhaps 4-12 switches a pair a year (estimate); intraday: hundreds.
fee_sensitivity: Each switch is 2 fills (1.10%); daily spread moves found do not exceed that.
long_only_note: Feasible mechanically on spot when the account already holds one leg; economically doubtful (see note).
limitations: Daily spreads do not revert reliably
Directional exposure dominates the spread signal
Doubles fills per decision
priority_reason: Feasible only in a degraded form whose evidence (daily pairs) is negative; record as assessed, do not build.

name: Cash-and-carry / funding capture (long spot, short perpetual or dated future)
summary: Hold spot and short an equal amount of perpetual (or dated future) to collect positive funding/basis while staying delta-neutral.
data_note: Data is free (funding archives); execution needs a derivatives account.

sources.citation: Borri, Liu, Tsyvinski, Wu (2025, rev. 2026), arXiv 2510.14435
sources.finding: [FT, partial] Carry strategy annualised Sharpe 6.45 over 1 Aug 2020 to 31 May 2025; 4.06 from 2024; negative in 2025. Funding averaged about 8% a year with about 0.8% volatility.

sources.citation: Schmeling, Schrimpf, Todorov (2023, rev. 2025), Crypto carry, BIS WP 1087
sources.finding: [A] Carry up to 60% p.a. and averaging above 10% a year (page summary); cash-and-carry is risky because of margin spikes and liquidations in drawdowns.

crypto_evidence_note: Strong historical carry, but compressed since 2024 and negative in 2025 (Borri et al.) - a clear post-publication / crowding decay.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Continuous position; rebalancing frequency set by margin needs.
fee_sensitivity: Two legs at 0.55% each way: about 2.2% to open and close both legs; recent funding (Borri: negative Sharpe in 2025) would not cover it.
long_only_note: Needs a short derivatives leg: outside a long-only spot app, and crypto derivatives are banned for UK retail (FCA PS20/10).
limitations: Requires shorting derivatives
UK retail derivatives ban
Counterparty and exchange risk on two venues
Premium decayed sharply after 2024

high_return_claim.claim: Crypto carry up to 60% p.a., average above 10% a year (BIS); carry strategy Sharpe 6.45 (Borri et al.). Costs not stated in what was read; delta-neutral.
high_return_claim.period: Borri et al.: 2020-08-01 to 2025-05-31; BIS sample period not read
high_return_claim.drawdown: Not given in the parts read
high_return_claim.leverage: Delta-neutral, margin on the short leg
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: Decayed after publication/crowding: Sharpe 4.06 from 2024, negative in 2025 (Borri et al.)

priority_reason: Needs short derivatives (banned for UK retail and outside the app's scope); documented decay. Listed for completeness and the high-return section.

name: Pairs trading / cointegration statistical arbitrage (distance, Engle-Granger, Johansen, copula)
summary: Find cointegrated or close-distance coin pairs; when the spread diverges by about 2 SD, short the rich leg and buy the cheap leg, closing at convergence.
data_note: Synchronised OHLCV for both legs; the profitable published frequency (5-minute) needs intraday history.

sources.citation: Fil, Kristoufek (2020), Pairs trading in cryptocurrency markets, IEEE Access 8
sources.finding: [A, search snippet] The daily distance method returns -0.07% monthly, rising to 11.61% monthly at 5-minute frequency; intraday prices mean-revert, daily ones do not; cointegration and distance methods differ by sub-period.

sources.citation: Leung, Nguyen (2019), Constructing cointegrated cryptocurrency portfolios for statistical arbitrage, Studies in Economics and Finance
sources.finding: [A, search snippet] Johansen and Engle-Granger portfolios of BTC, ETH, BCH, LTC; strategies profitable under several configurations, with and without stop-loss.

sources.citation: Tadi, Witzany (2025), Copula-based trading of cointegrated cryptocurrency pairs, Financial Innovation (arXiv:2305.06961)
sources.finding: [A] Linear/non-linear cointegration selection and copula signals; reported to outperform buy-and-hold on profitability and risk-adjusted return; costs, frequency and short mechanics not in the abstract.

sources.citation: Fischer, Krauss, Deinert (2019), Statistical arbitrage in cryptocurrency markets, Journal of Risk and Financial Management 12
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence.md] Random forest on lagged returns of 40 coins, 120-minute horizon, long-short: 7.1 bp a day after costs (about 29% a year), 18 Jun - 17 Sep 2018 only.

crypto_evidence_note: Profitable intraday and long-short; daily distance pairs lose; samples short.

reference_implementations.name: statsmodels (Engle-Granger coint, Johansen) - functions not confirmed on the page read

expected_trades_per_coin_year: Intraday: hundreds of round trips per pair a year (5-minute signals).
fee_sensitivity: Each pair trade is 4 fills (2.20%) per round trip; at intraday frequency fatal.
long_only_note: Needs a short leg (margin or perpetuals), which this app does not have. See stat_arb.long-only-leg-rotation for the spot-only remnant.
limitations: Requires shorting
Profitable only intraday
Cointegration among crypto pairs is unstable across sub-periods

high_return_claim.claim: 11.61% a month at 5-minute frequency (Fil & Kristoufek); about 29% a year after costs (Fischer et al.)
high_return_claim.period: Fischer: 18 Jun - 17 Sep 2018; Fil & Kristoufek: not verified
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: Fischer OOS only 3 months; Fil & Kristoufek not verified

priority_reason: Not feasible: needs shorting and intraday turnover far above what 0.55%/side allows.

name: Trend regime gate: BTC (or the coin) above its 200-day SMA / 10-month average
summary: Allow new long entries only while BTC's daily close (or the coin's own) is above its 200-day SMA (Faber: 10-month SMA at month-end); used as a veto, not a forced exit.
data_note: Daily BTC closes (and the coin's).

sources.citation: Detzel, Liu, Strauss, Zhou, Zhu (2021), Financial Management 50(1)
sources.finding: [A] Price-to-MA ratios forecast daily Bitcoin returns in and out of sample; A report [S]: even with an MA filter Bitcoin drawdowns stayed -66% to -70% vs -89.5% buy-and-hold (2010-2017, before costs).

sources.citation: CXO Advisory (n.d.), 10-month SMA timing signals over the long run
sources.finding: [S, search snippet] S&P Composite 1871-2012: 10-month SMA timing similar to buy-and-hold in average monthly return (0.75% vs 0.79%); Faber's drawdown reduction is in A-research-report.md.

sources.citation: Hurst, Ooi, Pedersen (2017), A century of evidence on trend-following investing
sources.finding: [FT, via A-research-report.md] Panel B with lagged, tradable indicators shows the apparent difficulty of improving trend strategies via timing decisions.

sources.citation: Coinpaprika (2026), Which crypto indicators actually work?
sources.finding: [FT] 50/200 death crosses were followed by higher 7-day returns (+3.26%, hit 65.7%) than golden crosses (+2.26%), a caution that a slow MA state carries little short-horizon information.

crypto_evidence_note: Drawdown reduction is the documented benefit; return improvement is not. No verified crypto study of a 200-day BTC gate with costs (A report).
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Veto only: removes entries, adds none.
fee_sensitivity: Can only reduce fees as a veto; as a forced exit it would add 1-4 round trips a year.
long_only_note: Long or cash: the natural long-only control.
limitations: 200-day length is a choice (count it as a trial)
Altcoins may need their own gate, not BTC's
Benefit is mainly drawdown, which few-trade samples measure poorly
priority_reason: Already built, only removes trades, natural for long-only; evaluate on STRAT-004/005 with time-in-state reported.

name: Leverage / carry veto (perpetual funding rate or futures basis too high: no new entries)
summary: Veto new spot entries while perpetual funding (or the annualised futures-spot basis) on the coin, or on BTC, is in its top band, on the reading that high carry marks crowded leveraged longs and raises crash risk. No published default threshold; the BIS paper documents carry up to 60% p.a.
data_note: Funding history free: Binance Vision USD-M fundingRate monthly files from 2020-01 (BTCUSDT); Hyperliquid info API fundingHistory (HYPE and others); Bybit archives. Binance Vision data is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and limited to personal non-production research. Not OHLCV of the traded spot pair: needs derivatives market data (no derivatives position is taken).

sources.citation: Schmeling, M., Schrimpf, A., Todorov, K. (2023, rev. 2025), Crypto carry, BIS Working Paper 1087
sources.finding: [A] The carry of crypto futures 'can become very large (up to 60% p.a.) and varies strongly over time'; the page's findings section states 'a high crypto carry predicts future price crashes', driven by trend-chasing small investors and scarce arbitrage capital. Not a trading-rule test.

sources.citation: Borri, N., Liu, Y., Tsyvinski, A., Wu, X. (2025, rev. 2026), Cryptocurrency as an investable asset class: coming of age, arXiv 2510.14435
sources.finding: [FT, partial] Stylised fact 6: carry 'used to be highly profitable, but profitability has compressed sharply since 2024'; profit 'mostly driven by the funding rate', which averaged about 8% a year (Aug 2020 to May 2025).

sources.citation: He, S., Manela, A., Ross, O., von Wachter, V. (2022, rev. 2026), Fundamentals of perpetual futures, arXiv 2212.06888
sources.finding: [A] Deviations of perpetual prices from their no-arbitrage values are larger than in traditional currency markets, co-move across currencies and diminish over time.

crypto_evidence_note: Carry predicting crashes is a working-paper finding read only at abstract level; no study found tests it as a long-only entry veto net of costs. The carry premium itself has decayed since 2024 (Borri et al.).
expected_trades_per_coin_year: 0 added; a veto only removes entries from the host strategy (share of time vetoed unknown until measured).
fee_sensitivity: Cannot add fees as a pure entry veto; it can only cut round trips (1.10% each). Used as a forced exit it would add round trips.
long_only_note: Uses derivatives data as information only. Holding crypto derivatives is banned for UK retail clients (FCA PS20/10), and the app is spot only.
limitations: Funding/basis history only from about 2019-2020; covers the 2021-2025 development window but few bear phases
Thresholds must be fixed before testing (multiple-testing risk)
Binance Vision licence is non-commercial, personal non-production research
Carry regime may have shifted after spot ETFs and the 2024 compression
priority_reason: Free data, cheap to add as a gate that only removes trades, economically motivated (leverage crowding), but evidence is a working paper on crash prediction, not a tested veto.

name: Drawdown-from-high filter (distance below the running or 52-week high)
summary: Gate entries on the coin's drawdown from its running high: momentum form allows entries only within x% of the high; contrarian form buys only after a drawdown beyond y%.
data_note: Daily closes; full history for all-time highs.

sources.citation: George, Hwang (2004), The 52-week high and momentum investing, Journal of Finance 59(5)
sources.finding: [A, search snippet] Stocks near their 52-week high outperform; forecasts do not reverse (supports the momentum form).

sources.citation: Caporale, Plastun (2018), Price overreactions in the cryptocurrency market, CESifo WP 6861
sources.finding: [A, search snippet] Buying counter to overreactions was not profitable in BTC, LTC, XRP, DASH 2013-2017 (against the contrarian form).

crypto_evidence_note: No direct crypto test of a drawdown gate found; indirect evidence favours the momentum form.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Gate only.
fee_sensitivity: Veto reduces trades.
long_only_note: Long-only gate.
limitations: No direct crypto evidence
Thresholds are trials
All-time highs depend on listing date (HYPE)
priority_reason: Cheap OHLCV gate with indirect support for the momentum form; untested in crypto.

name: Crypto Fear & Greed Index as contrarian entry or regime gate
summary: Use alternative.me's daily 0-100 index (volatility 25%, momentum/volume 25%, social 15%, surveys 15% (paused), dominance 10%, trends 10%) either as a contrarian buy in 'extreme fear' or as a veto in 'extreme greed'.
data_note: Free API (api.alternative.me/fng, limit=0 returns full history) from 2018-02-01, daily. Commercial use allowed with attribution next to the displayed data; must not impersonate the service. Market-wide (BTC-centric), not per coin.

sources.citation: Cavalheiro, E.A., Vieira, K.M., Thue, P.S. (2024), The impact of investor greed and fear on cryptocurrency returns: a Granger causality analysis of Bitcoin and Ethereum, Review of Behavioral Finance 16(5), 819-835
sources.finding: [A] Weekly data July 2022 to June 2023: the index Granger-predicts BTC and ETH returns, with feedback; nonlinear causality not supported. No trading test.

sources.citation: Shelton, A. (2024), Bitcoin return prediction: is it possible via stock-to-flow, Metcalfe's law, technical analysis, or market sentiment? Journal of Risk and Financial Management 17(10), 443
sources.finding: [A] Market-sentiment and technical measures are 'generally unrelated to returns in-sample' and poor out-of-sample predictors; a blended out-of-sample timing strategy did well (details unread).

sources.citation: alternative.me (2026), Crypto Fear & Greed Index and API terms
sources.finding: [FT] Component weights as in the summary; attribution required; commercial use allowed with attribution beside the data.

crypto_evidence_note: One short-sample Granger study positive; a broader out-of-sample study finds sentiment measures poor predictors. The index is partly built from price momentum and volatility, so it overlaps trend filters.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: As a gate: none added. As contrarian 'extreme fear' buys: perhaps 2-6 entries a year market-wide (inference).
fee_sensitivity: Low turnover, so drag of a few percent a year at most; the question is edge, not cost.
long_only_note: Natural long-or-cash use.
limitations: History from 2018-02 only; methodology changed (surveys paused)
One index for all coins
Mechanically overlaps momentum and volatility inputs
Vendor could change or withdraw the API
priority_reason: Free, daily, easy, low turnover; evidence weak and overlapping with trend filters - test only as a pre-declared gate.

name: Hidden Markov / Markov-switching / statistical jump-model regime filter
summary: Fit a 2-5 state hidden Markov (or Markov-switching, or statistical jump) model to daily returns and volatility on an expanding window; hold the coin only in states with positive expected return, otherwise cash. Shu, Yu and Mulvey add a jump penalty that makes regimes persistent.
data_note: Daily closes (BTC or each coin). OHLCV only.

sources.citation: Koki, C., Leonardos, S., Piliouras, G. (2022), Exploring the predictability of cryptocurrencies via Bayesian hidden Markov models, Research in International Business and Finance 59
sources.finding: [A] On BTC, ETH and XRP returns a four-state non-homogeneous HMM gave the best one-step-ahead forecasts among 2-5 state models; it identified bull, bear and calm regimes for BTC. Forecasts only, no trading after costs.

sources.citation: Ardia, D., Bluteau, K., Ruede, M. (2019), Regime changes in Bitcoin GARCH volatility dynamics, Finance Research Letters 29, 266-271
sources.finding: [A] Strong evidence of regime changes in Bitcoin's GARCH volatility; Markov-switching GARCH beats single-regime models in Value-at-Risk forecasts.

sources.citation: Shu, Y., Yu, C., Mulvey, J.M. (2024), Downside risk reduction using regime-switching signals: a statistical jump model approach, arXiv 2402.05272
sources.finding: [A] US, German and Japanese equity indices 1990-2023 out of sample, with transaction costs and trading delay: the jump-model regime strategy beat both an HMM-guided strategy and buy-and-hold on volatility, maximum drawdown and Sharpe ratio, attributed to more persistent regimes.

crypto_evidence_note: Crypto papers show regimes exist and help forecasts or VaR; no crypto long/cash regime-trading test with costs was found (also A report §6).
expected_trades_per_coin_year: 2-6 switches a year if regimes are persistent (jump penalty) [R]; an unpenalised HMM can flip far more often.
fee_sensitivity: Acceptable at a few switches a year (2-7% drag); a forced exit on every flip of a jittery HMM would add many round trips. Use as an entry veto first.
long_only_note: Naturally long or cash.
limitations: State labels can switch between refits (label switching)
In-sample regime fits look far better than real-time ones
Must beat the simpler BTC 200-day SMA gate already implemented
priority_reason: Fits long/cash and could only remove trades as a veto, but needs to beat the existing 200-day SMA gate and has no crypto trading evidence.

name: Network activity and hashrate (new/active addresses, hashrate trend)
summary: Use growth in network adoption (new addresses) or a hashrate index as a slow fundamental regime input; Wei et al. found a Hashrate Index among the only factors with genuine out-of-sample profitability.
data_note: Coin Metrics Community API (CC BY-NC 4.0), blockchain.com charts and Blockchair carry addresses and hashrate for BTC; hashrate applies only to proof-of-work coins (BTC, DOGE, ZEC, DASH), not ETH (post-merge), XRP, BNB, SOL or HYPE.

sources.citation: Wei, M., Kyriakou, I., Sermpinis, G., Stasinakis, C. (2024), Cryptocurrencies and lucky factors: the value of technical and fundamental analysis, International Journal of Finance & Economics 29
sources.finding: [FT, reused from A report] 12 coins 2015-2022, 7,846 rules and 59 fundamental factors: only a short-term price-to-average ratio and a hashrate index show genuine profitability after SPA and lucky-factor tests.

sources.citation: Borri, Liu, Tsyvinski, Wu (2025, rev. 2026), arXiv 2510.14435
sources.finding: [FT, partial] Review of Liu, Tsyvinski and Wu (2021): on-chain user adoption (new addresses) accounts for about 8% of return variation, over 10% for the largest coins in time series; the price-to-new-address ratio negatively predicts returns.

crypto_evidence_note: Hashrate survives a strict data-snooping test (Wei et al.); adoption explains returns, but much of it is contemporaneous variation, not tested as a long-only rule.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Slow regime input: 1-4 changes a year (inference).
fee_sensitivity: Low turnover; fees small.
long_only_note: Gate or slow allocation input.
limitations: Hashrate only for PoW coins in the list
Address counts are inflated by exchange and spam activity
Licence of free source is non-commercial (CC BY-NC)
Exact factor construction in Wei et al. not re-read here
priority_reason: One of few fundamentals with snooping-robust evidence and free data, but applies to only 4 of 9 coins and is untested as a long-only gate.

name: Volatility-regime filter (avoid entries in high realised-volatility states)
summary: Veto new entries when realised volatility (e.g. 20-30-day) is above a long-run percentile, or scale exposure down; equity literature frames it as volatility-managed portfolios.
data_note: Daily returns.

sources.citation: Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang, Yan (2020), On the performance of volatility-managed portfolios, Journal of Financial Economics 138(1)
sources.finding: [A, via A-research-report.md] Across 103 equity strategies, volatility-managed portfolios do not systematically outperform; real-time versions earn less.

sources.citation: Harvey, Hoyle, Korgaonkar, Rattray, Sargaison, Van Hemert (2018), The impact of volatility targeting, Journal of Portfolio Management 45(1)
sources.finding: [FT, via A-research-report.md] Volatility scaling raises Sharpe ratios for risk assets via the leverage effect and reduces extreme returns.

sources.citation: Bouri, Azzi, Dyhrberg (2017), On the return-volatility relationship in the Bitcoin market around the price crash of 2013, Economics E-Journal 11
sources.finding: [A, via A-research-report.md] Before the 2013 crash Bitcoin's volatility rose more after positive shocks (inverse of equities); no significant relation afterwards.

sources.citation: Almeida, C., Grith, M., Miftachov, R., Wang, Z. (2024), Risk premia in the Bitcoin market, arXiv 2410.15195
sources.finding: [A] Clustering option-implied densities reveals two Bitcoin volatility regimes. In the low-volatility regime more of the premium comes from positive returns and the variance risk premium is high; in the high-volatility regime the premium is split more evenly. Descriptive; no trading test.

sources.citation: Cederburg, S. et al. (2020), On the performance of volatility-managed portfolios, Journal of Financial Economics 138(1)
sources.finding: [A] (from A-research-report) Volatility timing does not systematically outperform out of sample in equities.

crypto_evidence_note: No crypto study of a volatility-state entry gate with costs found; Bitcoin's return-volatility asymmetry differed from equities, so the equity rationale may not transfer. Option-implied data show two Bitcoin volatility regimes (Almeida et al. 2024), but no trading test of a volatility gate was found.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Veto only.
fee_sensitivity: Veto reduces trades; re-sizing would add turnover unless banded.
long_only_note: Long or reduced/cash.
limitations: High-volatility states include the biggest crypto up-moves
Equity evidence contested
Threshold is a trial
Threshold choice is a free parameter (overfitting risk)
Trend strategies earn much of their return in high-volatility trends, which a calm-only filter would cut
Overlaps the BTC 200-day regime gate
priority_reason: Cheap veto but no crypto evidence and plausible harm (vetoes the strongest up-trends); the sizing form (volatility shrink) is covered by the volatility family. (Merged with volatility.regime-filter.)

name: Bubble-state dependence (trade trend rules only in dated bubble regimes)
summary: Svogun and Bazan-Palomino tie technical-rule excess returns to formally dated bubbles; a regime candidate would condition trend entries on a real-time explosive-price test (e.g. right-tailed unit-root tests).
data_note: Daily closes.

sources.citation: Svogun, Bazan-Palomino (2022), Technical analysis in cryptocurrency markets: do transaction costs and bubbles matter?, Journal of International Financial Markets, Institutions and Money 79
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence.md] 69 MA and breakout rules 2016-2021, daily and 1-minute, with and without costs: excess returns over buy-and-hold are statistically tied to formally dated bubbles.

crypto_evidence_note: Explains where trend profits came from; no study found showing real-time bubble dating improves a trading rule.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Gate only.
fee_sensitivity: Veto reduces trades.
long_only_note: Long-only gate.
limitations: Bubble dating is ex post; real-time tests lag
Few bubble episodes in sample
Mainly a caution on interpreting trend results
priority_reason: Valuable as an interpretation caution for every trend result, weak as a tradable gate.

name: Calendar effects: day-of-week (Monday), weekend, turn-of-the-month
summary: Hold only on historically strong days (e.g. Monday for BTC) or in the turn-of-month window (last day plus first three days, or searched four-day windows).
data_note: Daily (UTC) closes; definition of 'day' matters for a 24/7 market.

sources.citation: Caporale, Plastun (2019), The day of the week effect in the cryptocurrency market, Finance Research Letters 31
sources.finding: [A] Only Bitcoin shows an anomaly: Monday returns significantly higher; LTC, XRP, DASH show none; the trading simulation's results are mostly not different from random.

sources.citation: Baur, Cahill, Godfrey, Liu (2019), Bitcoin time-of-day, day-of-week and month-of-year effects in returns and trading volume, Finance Research Letters 31
sources.finding: [A, search snippet] 15m+ observations from seven exchanges: time-specific return anomalies do not persist over time; volume patterns (lower evenings and weekends) do.

sources.citation: Kumar (2022), Turn-of-the-month effect in cryptocurrencies, Managerial Finance
sources.finding: [A, search snippet] Aug 2015 - Aug 2021: BTC, ETH, LTC turn-of-month returns positive and significantly higher than other days; a TOM strategy beat buy-and-hold for Bitcoin.

sources.citation: Vasileiou (2023), turn-of-the-month in Bitcoin and Ethereum, International Journal of Banking, Accounting and Finance 13(3)
sources.finding: [A, search snippet] TOM windows cluster around month-end, but a TOM strategy does not always beat buy-and-hold on profit; better return-to-risk.

crypto_evidence_note: Effects reported in some samples, not persistent (Baur) or not different from random (Caporale & Plastun); TOM evidence conflicting.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Monday-only: 52 round trips; turn-of-month: 12.
fee_sensitivity: Monday: ~57% a year of drag, fatal. TOM: ~13% a year, larger than any effect size verified.
long_only_note: Long in the window, cash otherwise.
limitations: Non-persistent anomalies
Many possible windows: severe data-snooping
Fixed calendar turnover
priority_reason: Weak, non-persistent evidence and calendar turnover the fees destroy; at most a tilt on the timing of otherwise-planned trades.

name: Bitcoin halving-cycle timing
summary: Be long in the 12-18 months after each Bitcoin block-reward halving and reduce exposure late in the four-year cycle.
data_note: Halving dates are public; daily prices.

sources.citation: Virtonen (2025), Estimating the impact of the Bitcoin halving on its price using synthetic control, arXiv:2511.05512
sources.finding: [A] Synthetic control: positive effect of the 2024 halving about three months later (roughly one-fifth of the April 2023 - July 2024 price change); no statistically significant robust effect for 2020.

crypto_evidence_note: Four halvings in total: no statistical power; the only causal study finds an effect for one of two halvings tested.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: About 0.25-0.5 (one cycle decision every 2-4 years).
fee_sensitivity: Negligible.
long_only_note: Long/cash by cycle phase.
limitations: n = 4 events
Widely known, so likely priced
