Altcoins only loosely tied
priority_reason: Untestable statistically with four events; narrative rather than evidence.

name: Hour-of-day seasonality (e.g. long BTC 21:00-23:00 UTC)
summary: Hold Bitcoin only during historically strong hours; Quantpedia's rule buys at 21:00 UTC and sells at 23:00 UTC daily.
data_note: Hourly OHLCV.

sources.citation: Quantpedia (2023), Are there seasonal intraday or overnight anomalies in Bitcoin?
sources.finding: [FT] Gemini hourly BTC 9 Oct 2015 - 3 Feb 2022: 22:00-23:00 UTC strongest; 21:00-23:00 rule 33% a year, vol 20.93%, max DD -22.45%, in-sample, no costs.

sources.citation: Baur, Cahill, Godfrey, Liu (2019), Finance Research Letters 31
sources.finding: [A, search snippet] Time-of-day return anomalies did not persist over time.

crypto_evidence_note: Gross in-sample practitioner result; the peer-reviewed study finds time-of-day return anomalies non-persistent.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: 365 round trips (one per day).
fee_sensitivity: ~400% a year of drag at 1.10% a round trip vs 33% gross: fatal.
long_only_note: Long-only by construction.
limitations: Daily round trips
In-sample, gross
Non-persistent per peer-reviewed evidence

high_return_claim.claim: 33% a year (21:00-23:00 UTC BTC rule), no costs
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: No; in-sample, and non-persistent per Baur et al.

priority_reason: Impossible at 0.55%/side (365 round trips); documented as a negative.

name: News coverage and tone (GDELT, news APIs)
summary: Count and score news articles about crypto/each coin per day (e.g. GDELT tone, article volume) and use abnormal coverage as a regime or bubble indicator.
data_note: GDELT is free for any use with citation, updated every 15 minutes (2.0), history back to 2013-2015 depending on product; topic filtering for small coins is noisy. NewsAPI free plan is development-only (24h delay, 1 month back). CryptoPanic has a free tier (rate-limited; history depth not confirmed).

sources.citation: Li, Y., Zhang, W., Urquhart, A., Zhang, P. (2022), The role of media coverage in bubble formation: evidence from the Bitcoin market, Journal of International Financial Markets, Institutions and Money 80, 101629
sources.finding: [A] Media coverage, regardless of tone, increases next-day Bitcoin returns in bubble periods but not otherwise; returns also predict future coverage.

sources.citation: The GDELT Project (2026), About / Data pages
sources.finding: [FT] All datasets free for academic, commercial or governmental use without fee; redistribution allowed with citation and link; GDELT 2.0 events and GKG update every 15 minutes.

crypto_evidence_note: Only a regime-dependent, next-day effect in bubbles; no trading test with costs found.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Next-day effect implies daily turnover (inference); as a bubble-regime gate, few.
fee_sensitivity: A next-day effect cannot plausibly clear 1.10% a round trip; only a slow gate is viable.
long_only_note: Long-or-cash.
limitations: Large data volumes (GDELT)
Effect only in bubble periods
Look-ahead risk from article timestamps and later revisions
priority_reason: Weak, regime-dependent evidence with a horizon too short for the fees.

name: On-chain valuation ratios (MVRV, NVT, SOPR, realised price, stock-to-flow, Metcalfe)
summary: Buy when on-chain valuation is low (e.g. MVRV near or below 1, short-term-holder SOPR below 1) and reduce when stretched; vendor and community rules, no single published default.
data_note: Coin Metrics Community API (free, no key, CC BY-NC 4.0, 10 requests per 6 s) carries some network/valuation series; Glassnode/CryptoQuant on-chain series are paid; Santiment free tier cuts the last 30 days. Mainly BTC (UTXO metrics); ETH partially; XRP/BNB/SOL/HYPE poorly covered.

sources.citation: Shelton, A. (2024), Bitcoin return prediction: is it possible via stock-to-flow, Metcalfe's law, technical analysis, or market sentiment? JRFM 17(10), 443
sources.finding: [A] Stock-to-flow and Metcalfe's law explain returns in-sample but have 'limited to no ability' out of sample; a blended out-of-sample timing strategy beat buy-and-hold risk-adjusted (method unread).

sources.citation: Glassnode Research (n.d.), The predictive power of Glassnode data
sources.finding: [FT] Vendor ML model; STH-SOPR and percentage of entities in profit were 'the most promising indicators' for longs; no periods, returns or costs disclosed.

crypto_evidence_note: Peer-reviewed out-of-sample test finds valuation models fail to predict; vendor claims are undisclosed.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Cycle-level signals: about 1-3 a year (inference).
fee_sensitivity: Very low turnover; fees negligible.
long_only_note: Long-or-cash accumulation timing.
limitations: Few independent cycles (2-3) in the data
Coverage limited to BTC/ETH
Best data is paid
Vendor definitions change
priority_reason: Negative out-of-sample evidence, few cycles, BTC-only coverage, best data paid.

name: Search attention (Google Trends, Wikipedia page views)
summary: Use abnormal search or page-view attention for a coin as a regime/feedback signal: rising attention above trend amplifies rallies, below trend amplifies falls (Kristoufek 2013).
data_note: Wikipedia Pageviews API: free, CC0 data, User-Agent header required (start date of per-article data not confirmed). Google Trends: relative (0-100) values only; official API is a closed alpha (July 2025); pytrends unofficial and archived 2025-04-17.

sources.citation: Kristoufek, L. (2013), BitCoin meets Google Trends and Wikipedia: quantifying the relationship between phenomena of the Internet era, Scientific Reports 3, 3415
sources.finding: [FT] May 2011 to June 2013: price correlations about 0.88 (Google Trends, weekly) and 0.83 (Wikipedia, daily); bidirectional link; interest pushes prices up when above trend and down when below. Not a trading test.

sources.citation: Urquhart, A. (2018), What causes the attention of Bitcoin? Economics Letters 166, 40-44
sources.finding: [A] Realised volatility and volume are significant drivers of next-day attention, i.e. attention follows the market.

sources.citation: Liu, Y., Tsyvinski, A. (2021), Risks and returns of cryptocurrency, Review of Financial Studies 34(6)
sources.finding: [A, reused from C-evidence] Investor-attention proxies forecast returns (mostly in-sample predictive regressions).

sources.citation: Yae, J., Tian, G.Z. (2022), Out-of-sample forecasting of cryptocurrency returns, Physica A 598
sources.finding: [A, reused from C-evidence] Popular in-sample predictors (attention, volume) fail out of sample.

crypto_evidence_note: Strong in-sample co-movement, but attention follows prices (Urquhart) and fails out of sample (Yae & Tian).
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Weekly regime flips: a few to a dozen (inference).
fee_sensitivity: Low to moderate turnover; drag a few to ~13% a year if used standalone.
long_only_note: Long-or-cash regime use.
limitations: Google Trends access unofficial/fragile and values are relative, re-scaled per query
Attention is coincident (follows volatility and volume)
Out-of-sample failure reported
priority_reason: Negative out-of-sample evidence and fragile data access.

name: Stablecoin issuance / Tether minting events
summary: Treat large stablecoin mints (USDT, USDC) as incoming buying power; enter or allow entries after large issuance, which tends to follow market downturns.
data_note: Mint events are public on-chain (Ethereum via Etherscan free 3 calls/s, Tron) and supply series appear in free community datasets; assembling a clean event history takes work.

sources.citation: Griffin, J.M., Shams, A. (2020), Is Bitcoin really untethered? Journal of Finance 75(4), 1913-1964
sources.finding: [A] Tether-funded purchases 'are timed following market downturns and result in sizable increases in Bitcoin prices' (2017 boom), consistent with unbacked supply inflating prices.

sources.citation: Ante, L., Fiedler, I., Strehle, E. (2021), The influence of stablecoin issuances on cryptocurrency markets, Finance Research Letters 41
sources.finding: [A] 565 issuances of $1m+ for seven stablecoins, Apr 2019 to Mar 2020: market downturns in the week before, positive abnormal returns in the 24 hours around issuance; insignificant for some stablecoins.

crypto_evidence_note: Event studies find short positive abnormal returns around issuance; the 24-hour window is shorter than a cost-viable hold, and the 2017-2020 samples predate today's larger, more institutional stablecoin market.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Many issuance events a year; as a daily gate, none added.
fee_sensitivity: A 24-hour abnormal return is unlikely to exceed 1.10% reliably; viable only as a slow liquidity regime input.
long_only_note: Buy-side or gate use.
limitations: Short event windows
Sample periods 2017-2020
Issuance partly reacts to prior moves (downturns)
priority_reason: Credible event-study evidence, but the horizon is too short for the fees and data assembly is non-trivial.

name: Exchange net flows and whale transfers
summary: Treat large on-chain deposits to exchanges (whale alerts, exchange inflow spikes) as selling pressure / volatility warnings and veto entries; outflows as accumulation.
data_note: Exchange-flow series need labelled exchange wallets: CryptoQuant includes on-chain data only from its Professional plan; Glassnode API needs paid credits; whale-alert feeds on X are paid to read.

sources.citation: Herremans, D., Low, K.W. (2022), Forecasting Bitcoin volatility spikes from whale transactions and CryptoQuant data using Synthesizer Transformer models, arXiv 2211.08281
sources.finding: [A] Whale-alert tweets plus CryptoQuant exchange/on-chain data forecast next-day volatility spikes better than baselines; backtests claim lower drawdown with 'steady profits' - no numbers in the abstract.

sources.citation: CryptoQuant (2026), Pricing
sources.finding: [FT] Free Basic plan: daily resolution, 3 years history, API for market data only; on-chain data via API from Professional plan.

crypto_evidence_note: Evidence is about volatility, not direction; directional claims are vendor commentary.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: As a veto: none added.
fee_sensitivity: As a veto it only removes trades.
long_only_note: Veto use.
limitations: Paid data
Exchange wallet labelling is proprietary and revised
Mostly BTC/ETH
priority_reason: Needs paid data; evidence concerns volatility not returns.

name: Social-media sentiment (Twitter/X, Reddit) as a signal
summary: Score posts about each coin (lexicon or model) into a daily sentiment or bullishness ratio and use it to time entries. LLM-based scoring is covered under the llm.* candidates.
data_note: X API is pay-per-use ($0.005 per post read, capped at 3 million reads a month) with no free read tier found; Reddit Data API free tier (100 queries/min per OAuth client from July 2023, per Reddit's announcement) excludes commercial use without a deal and has no historical archive. Bot share is material.

sources.citation: Kraaijeveld, O., De Smedt, J. (2020), The predictive power of public Twitter sentiment for forecasting cryptocurrency prices, Journal of International Financial Markets, Institutions and Money 65
sources.finding: [A] Nine largest coins incl. BTC, ETH, XRP: Twitter sentiment Granger-predicts returns for BTC, BCH and LTC; a bullishness ratio for EOS and TRON; at least 1-14% of tweets were from bots. No trading results.

sources.citation: X Developer Platform (2026), X API pricing
sources.finding: [FT] Pay-per-usage, no subscriptions; post reads $0.005 each; capped at 3 million post reads a month; Enterprise for more.

sources.citation: Reddit (2023), API update: enterprise level tier for large scale applications (r/redditdev announcement, read via mirror)
sources.finding: [S] Free tier 100 queries per minute per OAuth client id from 1 July 2023; apps that make money from Reddit data must pay.

crypto_evidence_note: Granger-causality only, coin-dependent, no trading tests with costs; bots contaminate the data.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Daily sentiment signals: likely dozens (inference).
fee_sensitivity: Daily turnover would cost tens of percent a year; only usable as a slow gate.
long_only_note: Long-or-cash.
limitations: No free historical source for X; Reddit terms restrict commercial and model-training use
Bots
No out-of-sample trading evidence
priority_reason: Data is paid or terms-restricted, with no historical archive; evidence is Granger-only.

name: CTREND: combined price-and-volume technical trend signal (cross-sectional)
summary: Many price and volume technical indicators (moving averages, oscillators, volume indicators) over several horizons, combined by a cross-sectional machine-learning regression (elastic net) into one return forecast. Published as a weekly long-short factor.
data_note: OHLCV for every coin at the same instant. The published universe is more than 3,000 coins, versus 9 here.

sources.citation: Fieberg, C., Liedtke, G., Poddig, T., Walker, T., Zaremba, A. (2025), A trend factor for the cross section of cryptocurrency returns, Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 60(7), 3116-3153
sources.finding: [A] Signal from price and volume indicators across horizons, by machine learning, on more than 3,000 coins. It 'reliably predicts cryptocurrency returns', is not subsumed by known factors, survives transaction costs and persists in large, liquid coins. The return figures were not read.

crypto_evidence_note: Positive as a cross-sectional long-short factor, net of the authors' cost assumption. Whether it works long-only across 9 large coins is untested. The repo's volume research reports (from the full text, not re-read here) that volume indicators are weak alone and excluding them barely matters.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Weekly rebalancing gives up to 52 rebalances a year. With 9 coins and top-k holdings, an estimated 10-30 position changes per coin a year, unverified.
fee_sensitivity: Weekly rotation is expensive. The A-research-report estimates about 19% a year of drag for a k = 3 book with one swap a week. A rank band and a minimum hold are required.
long_only_note: Published long-short. A long-only top-k version keeps only part of the spread, and needs a portfolio-level interface that sees every coin, which the app lacks.
limitations: Cross-sectional and long-short as published
The universe of 9 coins is too small for quintile sorts
ML fitting adds overfitting risk
Needs a portfolio interface
priority_reason: Peer-reviewed and cost-aware, but cross-sectional, long-short and built on thousands of coins. It needs portfolio infrastructure, and the volume part adds little.

name: Relative volume, volume shocks and volume acceleration (confirmation or veto)
summary: Volume divided by a baseline: Bianchi et al. use log volume minus the log of its 30-day mean, standardised. The rule requires high relative volume to confirm an entry, or vetoes entries after abnormal volume. Volume acceleration is the change in that ratio.
data_note: OHLCV only. Intraday baselines must be taken against the same hour of the day, because volume has strong daily, hourly and within-hour periodicity on Coinbase and Binance (Hansen, Kim and Kimbrough 2021).

sources.citation: Bianchi, D., Babiak, M., Dickerson, A. (2022), Trading volume and liquidity provision in cryptocurrency markets, Journal of Banking & Finance 142, 106547
sources.finding: [A] USD pairs on several centralised exchanges, Mar 2017 to Mar 2022. Returns to liquidity provision, proxied by short-term reversal, are larger in smaller, more volatile and less liquid pairs. In panel regressions, the interaction of lagged returns and volume predicts returns.

sources.citation: Garfinkel, J.A., Hsiao, L., Hu, D. (2025), Disagreement and returns: the case of cryptocurrencies, Financial Management 54(3), 633-672
sources.finding: [A] Abnormal volume, read as disagreement, is negatively related to future returns in the cross-section when short-sale constraints bind. The effect disappears once margin trading is enabled for a coin. This is the opposite sign to the equity high-volume premium.

sources.citation: Bouri, E., Lau, C.K.M., Lucey, B., Roubaud, D. (2019), Trading volume and the predictability of return and volatility in the cryptocurrency market, Finance Research Letters 29, 340-346
sources.finding: [A] Daily data for seven coins (including BTC, XRP, ETH, DASH): volume Granger-causes extreme negative and positive returns for all seven. It causes volatility only for LTC, NEM and DASH at low volatility. The test is in-sample causality, not a trading test.

sources.citation: Balcilar, M., Bouri, E., Gupta, R., Roubaud, D. (2017), Can volume predict Bitcoin returns and volatility? A quantiles-based approach, Economic Modelling 64, 74-81
sources.finding: [A] Daily BTC, 19 Dec 2011 to 25 Apr 2016: volume predicts returns except in bear and bull regimes (the tails). It does not predict volatility, and linear causality tests find nothing.

sources.citation: Hansen, P.R., Kim, C., Kimbrough, W. (2021), Periodicity in cryptocurrency volatility and liquidity, arXiv 2109.12142
sources.finding: [A] BTC and ETH on Coinbase Pro, Binance and Uniswap V2 show 'systematic patterns in both volatility and volume' by weekday, hour and within the hour, strengthening over time. A raw rolling baseline therefore partly measures the clock.

sources.citation: Cong, L.W., Li, X., Tang, K., Yang, Y. (2023), Crypto wash trading, Management Science 69(11), 6427-6454
sources.finding: [A] Across 29 centralised exchanges, regulated venues show normal trade-size and digit patterns; wash trading on unregulated exchanges averaged over 70% of reported volume. Volume from unregulated venues is unreliable as a signal input.

crypto_evidence_note: Volume carries information, but its sign depends on context: high abnormal volume precedes lower returns in short-constrained coins (Garfinkel et al.), while the return-by-volume interaction is positive in Bianchi et al. The repo's own test (docs/research/volume-module.md) found that relative volume above 1.5x the same-hour average lifted the STRAT-001 1h fee-adjusted hit rate from 15.6% to 21.2%, but those trades still lost 2.10% each at the app's fee. The gross effect was about +0.3% a trade.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: As a filter, a subset of the host strategy's trades: on STRAT-004, roughly 2-6 a year from 3-8. Stand-alone use is not proposed.
fee_sensitivity: As a veto it adds no fees. The repo found a gross lift of about +0.3% a trade at 1h, far below the 1.10% round trip, so it cannot rescue hourly strategies. Test it only on daily strategies whose gross edge already clears the fees.
long_only_note: Confirmation or veto of long entries. The disagreement result concerns coins that cannot be shorted, which is the situation of a spot-only trader's universe on most venues.
limitations: The sign of the effect is disputed
Main results are cross-sectional and in-sample
Volume is venue-specific and includes wash trading on unregulated venues (Cong et al. 2023: over 70% on average)
Intraday baselines must remove periodicity
Reported volume on unregulated exchanges is mostly wash trading (Cong et al. 2023); use regulated-venue volume only
priority_reason: Moderate evidence that volume is informative, but with a disputed sign. The repo already measured a gross effect too small for hourly fees. It is worth one pre-registered veto test on STRAT-004 daily entries.

name: Chaikin Money Flow (CMF-20) and accumulation/distribution
summary: CMF is the sum over n bars (n = 20 by convention) of the close-location value times volume, divided by the summed volume. Positive CMF is read as accumulation, negative as distribution, and it is used as a confirmation or veto for entries.
data_note: Computable from OHLCV (high, low, close, volume). Coinbase public candles are sufficient.

sources.citation: Fieberg, C., Liedtke, G., Poddig, T., Walker, T., Zaremba, A. (2025), A trend factor for the cross section of cryptocurrency returns, Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 60(7), 3116-3153
sources.finding: [A] Combines price and volume technical indicators over several horizons with machine learning, on more than 3,000 coins. The resulting signal 'reliably predicts' returns, survives transaction costs and persists in large, liquid coins (cross-sectional). The abstract does not isolate CMF.

sources.citation: Blume, L., Easley, D., O'Hara, M. (1994), Market statistics and technical analysis: the role of volume, Journal of Finance 49(1)
sources.finding: [A] Theoretical rationale: volume conveys information about signal quality.

crypto_evidence_note: No external CMF-only crypto test was read. The repo's own development run (docs/dev/SIG4-REPORT-dev.md, FDS-SIG-004 PV-1, 2021-01-01 to 2025-05-06) found no forecast improvement from price-and-volume features over price alone: Δ log loss +0.00033, p = 0.17. The repo's volume research (docs/research/volume-module.md) reports, from the CTREND full text, that Chaikin alone was not significant. That figure was not re-read here.

reference_implementations.name: TA-Lib AD / ADOSC (Chaikin A/D line and oscillator)

expected_trades_per_coin_year: As a veto on a host strategy, it removes some of the host's trades (STRAT-004: ~3-8 a year). As a stand-alone zero-cross rule on daily bars, it would flip often: an estimated 15-40 a year, unverified.
fee_sensitivity: Stand-alone: 15-40 round trips cost 16-44% a year, which no evidence suggests it can cover. As a veto: no added cost.
long_only_note: Used as a long-entry confirmation or veto.
limitations: Already tested in the repo with no forecast gain (development run only)
The close-location value is noisy on 24/7 markets with arbitrary daily cut-offs
Venue-specific volume
priority_reason: Already built and tested in signal_fusion with no improvement over price alone, and there is no external CMF-specific evidence. Keep it as a control, not a new candidate.

name: Money Flow Index (MFI)
summary: A volume-weighted RSI. Money flow is the typical price times volume; MFI(14) = 100 - 100/(1 + positive flow / negative flow). The convention reads 80 as overbought and 20 as oversold, and the standard rule buys on a cross back above 20.
data_note: Computable from OHLCV.

sources.citation: Blume, L., Easley, D., O'Hara, M. (1994), Market statistics and technical analysis: the role of volume, Journal of Finance 49(1)
sources.finding: [A] Theory only: volume is informative.

sources.citation: Zaremba, A., Bilgin, M.H., Long, H., Mercik, A., Szczygielski, J.J. (2021), Up or down? Short-term reversal, momentum, and liquidity effects in cryptocurrency markets, International Review of Financial Analysis 78, 101908
sources.finding: [A] (from A-research-report) Daily reversal comes from illiquid coins; the largest coins show daily momentum rather than reversal. This works against oversold-bounce rules such as MFI < 20 on large coins.

crypto_evidence_note: No MFI-specific crypto study was found. The oscillator logic is mean reversion, which the crypto evidence for large coins contradicts.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Estimated 5-15 oversold entries a year on daily bars, more on intraday bars. This is a guess from typical oscillator crossing rates and is unverified.
fee_sensitivity: Each trade must clear 1.10%. Short oscillator holds rarely earn that on large coins (A-research-report section 7).
long_only_note: The oversold-buy form is long-only.
limitations: No crypto evidence
Mean-reversion logic goes against the continuation found in large coins
Venue-specific volume
priority_reason: No evidence, a contrarian logic that the crypto literature contradicts for large coins, and short holds that the fees punish.

name: On-balance volume (OBV) and OBV moving-average crossovers
summary: Cumulative volume signed by the close-to-close direction (Granville). Typical rules buy when OBV crosses above its own moving average, or when OBV makes a new high that confirms a price high; Gerritsen et al. applied moving-average rules to OBV.
data_note: Computable from OHLCV. Coinbase public candles (Exchange API, max 300 per request; 60s to 1d) are enough. Exchange-reported volume differs by venue, and unregulated venues carry wash volume (Cong et al. 2023).

sources.citation: Gerritsen, D.F., Bouri, E., Ramezanifar, E., Roubaud, D. (2020), The profitability of technical trading rules in the Bitcoin market, Finance Research Letters 34, 101263
sources.finding: [A] (from A-research-report) Daily Bitcoin 2010-2019: the trading-range breakout rule has significant forecasting power. [S] A TradingView summary lists OBV (MA rules applied to OBV) among the seven rule families tested, but reports no OBV-specific result, and says the analysis does not account for transaction costs.

sources.citation: Gerritsen et al. (2020) summarised on TradingView, 'The profitability of TA trading rules in the Bitcoin market'
sources.finding: [S] Seven rule families tested on daily BTC, 17 Jul 2010 to 31 Dec 2018: MA, trading-range breakout, MACD, ROC, OBV, RSI, Bollinger. 'The study applied MA rules to the OBV'. No OBV result is given in the summary; RSI and Bollinger generally underperformed.

sources.citation: Blume, L., Easley, D., O'Hara, M. (1994), Market statistics and technical analysis: the role of volume, Journal of Finance 49(1), 153-181
sources.finding: [A] Theory: in an equilibrium model, volume carries information about signal quality that price alone does not, so traders who use market statistics do better. A rationale for volume indicators, not an empirical test of OBV.

crypto_evidence_note: No OBV-specific crypto result was found. Gerritsen et al. include OBV rules, but the reviewed summary reports results only for other rules, before costs.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: As a stand-alone OBV/MA crossover on daily bars, an estimated 6-20 round trips (similar to a price MA crossover of the same length). As a confirmation filter on STRAT-004, fewer than the host strategy's ~3-8.
fee_sensitivity: At 6-20 round trips, the drag is 7-22% a year at 1.10% a round trip. That is too much for an indicator with no shown edge. As a veto on an existing daily strategy, it can only cut costs.
long_only_note: Buy and exit signals map directly to long or cash.
limitations: No crypto evidence specific to OBV
Volume differs by exchange and includes wash trading on some venues
OBV level depends on the start date; only changes or crossovers are meaningful
priority_reason: Cheap to compute from OHLCV, but there is no verified crypto evidence. The repo's SIG-004 run found that volume features added no forecast value over price alone. Keep only as a falsification filter on STRAT-004.

name: Volume-price divergence and volume-confirmed breakouts
summary: A price breakout or new high counts only if volume (or OBV) also expands above its average; a price high on falling volume (bearish divergence) is a warning or exit. There are no canonical parameters; typical rules use volume above 1.5x its 20-day average on the breakout bar.
data_note: OHLCV only.

sources.citation: Blume, L., Easley, D., O'Hara, M. (1994), Market statistics and technical analysis: the role of volume, Journal of Finance 49(1)
sources.finding: [A] Theory: volume reveals the quality of information behind price moves, which is the rationale for confirmation rules.

sources.citation: Liu, Y., Tsyvinski, A., Wu, X. (2022), Common risk factors in cryptocurrency, Journal of Finance 77(2), 1133-1177 (NBER WP 25882)
sources.finding: [S] Volume-sorted portfolios: a long low-volume / short high-volume strategy earns about 3% weekly excess return (3.2% for dollar volume), gross. All such strategies are explained by the crypto three-factor model (market, size, momentum).

sources.citation: Bianchi, D., Babiak, M., Dickerson, A. (2022), Trading volume and liquidity provision in cryptocurrency markets, Journal of Banking & Finance 142
sources.finding: [A] The lagged return x volume interaction predicts returns. This is the nearest published analogue of 'volume-confirmed moves'.

crypto_evidence_note: No crypto study of divergence or volume-confirmed breakouts was found. The repo's volume research also lists volume-price divergence as unverified.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: A filter on STRAT-004 breakouts: fewer than ~3-8 a year.
fee_sensitivity: A filter only, so it cannot add fees. It may remove the few large trend trades that pay for everything, which is the main risk.
long_only_note: Entry confirmation and early-exit warning for long positions.
limitations: No crypto evidence
Breakouts on low volume during 24/7 weekend sessions are common, and seasonality confounds the test
Risk of filtering out the trend trades that carry the return
priority_reason: Untested idea with no crypto evidence. It is a cheap falsification test on STRAT-004, but it should not be prioritised over the price-only rules.

name: Volume profile: point of control and value area
summary: A histogram of traded volume by price over a window. The point of control (POC) is the price with the most volume; the value area is the band holding about 70% of volume. Rules buy re-entries into value from below or breakouts above the value-area high.
data_note: Needs volume at each price: trades, or at least 1-minute candles as an approximation. Coinbase public trades are paginated by trade id, so a full backfill is slow; Binance aggTrades bulk files exist, but their terms prohibit live-trading use (see data notes). Daily OHLCV alone gives only a crude approximation.

sources.citation: TradingView, Volume Profile indicators: basic concepts (wiki)
sources.finding: [S] Defines the POC and value area. The 70% value-area convention comes from Steidlmayer's Market Profile. Practitioner definitions only; no performance evidence.

crypto_evidence_note: No academic test of volume-profile levels in crypto (or elsewhere) was found. The sources found are vendor case studies without benchmarks.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Unknown; depends on the rule. Level-reaction rules typically trade often (more than 20 a year, estimated).
fee_sensitivity: Support and resistance reactions are small moves, usually below the 1.10% round trip. They are unlikely to survive.
long_only_note: Buy at the value-area low or POC, or on a breakout above the value-area high.
limitations: No evidence
Needs trade-level data for an exact profile
Highly discretionary parameters (window, bin size, 70%)
Wash volume distorts profiles on some venues
priority_reason: Anecdotal only, needs trade-level data, and suits short holds that the fees destroy.

name: VWAP and anchored-VWAP signals
summary: Go long when price is above the session VWAP (Zarattini and Aziz: long above VWAP, short below, intraday on QQQ). Anchored VWAP measures from a chosen event (a swing low or a listing) and is read as average cost basis, acting as support or resistance.
data_note: True VWAP needs trades (price x size), available from the Coinbase public trades endpoint (paginated by trade id) or Binance aggTrades. A bar approximation (typical price x bar volume) works from OHLCV; finer bars give a closer approximation. Crypto has no session open, so the 'session' must be defined (for example 00:00 UTC).

sources.citation: Zarattini, C., Aziz, A. (2023), Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP): the holy grail for day trading systems, SSRN 4631351 (Concretum Group summary)
sources.finding: [S] QQQ, 2 Jan 2018 to 28 Sep 2023, intraday long above and short below VWAP: $25,000 grew to $192,656 (671%), maximum drawdown 9.4%, Sharpe 2.1, against buy-and-hold at 126%, drawdown 37% and Sharpe 0.7. 'net of commissions', with the rate not stated. On 3x TQQQ: about 8,242%. One author runs a trading academy that promotes the paper.

sources.citation: Genet, R. (2025), Deep learning for VWAP execution in crypto markets: beyond the volume curve, arXiv 2502.13722
sources.finding: [A] VWAP as an execution objective in crypto (minimising slippage against VWAP), not as a trading signal. No performance numbers in the abstract.

crypto_evidence_note: No crypto study of VWAP as a signal was found. The only published backtest is an equity intraday long-short by practitioner authors.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: As published (intraday, one or more flips a day), more than 250 round trips a year. As a daily anchored-VWAP trend filter, perhaps 3-10, unverified.
fee_sensitivity: The intraday form would cost more than 275% a year at 1.10% a round trip, so it is destroyed. Only a slow daily filter variant could survive, and it has no evidence.
long_only_note: Published as intraday long-short. A long-only version (long above VWAP, else cash) halves the trades but keeps intraday turnover.
limitations: Equity-only, practitioner evidence with a conflict of interest
Independent replication reportedly much weaker (secondary claim, not verified)
Crypto session definition is arbitrary
Turnover incompatible with 0.55% a side

high_return_claim.claim: 671% total return on QQQ, Sharpe 2.1, intraday long-short, net of unspecified commissions; about 8,242% on 3x TQQQ (Concretum summary)
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: No out-of-sample period reported. A replication reportedly found Sharpe of about 0.7 (unverified secondary claim).

priority_reason: Intraday turnover cannot survive 0.55% a side. There is no crypto evidence, and the only headline evidence is promotional and equity-only.

name: Quoted spread and order-book depth as an execution and cost gate
summary: Before an entry or exit, read the best bid and ask and the depth at the order size. Skip or delay the trade (or use a limit order) when the spread or the estimated slippage exceeds a threshold. Log realised slippage against the 0.05% assumption.
data_note: Needs order-book snapshots. The Coinbase Exchange 'get product book' endpoint (levels 1-3) is public but returns only the current book, with no history. History must be recorded by the app from now on (or bought). Spreads cannot be backfilled from OHLCV.

sources.citation: Brauneis, A., Mestel, R., Riordan, R., Theissen, E. (2021), How to measure the liquidity of cryptocurrency markets?, Journal of Banking & Finance 124, 106041
sources.finding: [FT pp. 1, 5-6] (from A-research-report) Coinbase BTC-USD and ETH-USD spreads were about 1-2 basis points in 2017-2019, 25-50 times smaller than one 0.50% taker fee.

sources.citation: Dyhrberg, A.H., Foley, S., Svec, J. (2018), How investible is Bitcoin? Analyzing the liquidity and transaction costs of Bitcoin markets, Economics Letters 171, 140-143
sources.finding: [A] Intraday trade and quote data from three US exchanges: quoted and effective spreads are lower than on major equity exchanges, so Bitcoin is investible at retail trade sizes. Spreads are lowest, and activity highest, during US market hours.

sources.citation: Coinbase Developer Platform, Exchange API: Get product book
sources.finding: [FT] Level 1 is best bid and ask; level 2 is the full aggregated book; level 3 is the full non-aggregated book. 'The entire book is returned in one response'. Current snapshot only; WebSocket recommended for live updates. No authentication required.

crypto_evidence_note: This is evidence about costs, not alpha. Spreads on Coinbase majors are tiny compared with the fee. Thinner coins in this universe (ZEC, DASH, HYPE on Coinbase) were not measured in the studies, so the 0.05% slippage assumption is unverified for them.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: No new trades; it gates the host strategy's trades.
fee_sensitivity: It cannot reduce the 0.50% taker fee, but it protects the 0.05% slippage assumption on thin books. Using maker (limit) orders where available would change the fee tier, which needs the account's maker rate.
long_only_note: An execution policy; neutral to direction.
limitations: No free historical order-book data on Coinbase; must be recorded forward
Benefit is small relative to the fee
Delaying an order changes the fill price (timing risk)
priority_reason: Cheap infrastructure that validates the cost model every backtest relies on, especially for ZEC, DASH and HYPE. It needs only a forward-recorded public snapshot.

name: Execution timing by intraday liquidity periodicity
summary: Decide on the daily close, but place orders in historically liquid hours (for example, overlapping US market hours) and avoid thin periods and funding-time bursts. This lowers spread and slippage without changing the signal.
data_note: Hourly volume profiles come from OHLCV (free). Spread by hour needs order-book snapshots recorded forward.

sources.citation: Hansen, P.R., Kim, C., Kimbrough, W. (2021), Periodicity in cryptocurrency volatility and liquidity, arXiv 2109.12142
sources.finding: [A] Weekday, hour and within-hour patterns in volatility and volume of BTC and ETH on Coinbase Pro, Binance and Uniswap V2, intensifying over the years and linked to algorithmic trading and futures funding times.

sources.citation: Dyhrberg, A.H., Foley, S., Svec, J. (2018), How investible is Bitcoin?, Economics Letters 171
sources.finding: [A] Spreads lowest and trading activity highest during US market hours.

crypto_evidence_note: Periodicity in liquidity is documented. Its value for a retail order of £50 to £10,000 is a fraction of the 0.05% slippage budget, not of the 0.50% fee.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: No new trades.
fee_sensitivity: Can save part of the 0.05% slippage only. The 0.50% taker fee is unchanged.
long_only_note: Direction-neutral execution policy.
limitations: Small benefit
Delay between signal and fill adds price risk
Patterns shift over time
priority_reason: Well documented and cheap, but the economic value is small next to the taker fee. Do it after the strategy questions.

name: Amihud illiquidity, turnover and liquidity-volatility as return predictors
summary: Amihud ILLIQ = mean(|daily return| / dollar volume). The literature uses it in cross-sectional sorts (buy illiquid, sell liquid) and as a time-series predictor (returns after low liquidity, or after high volatility of liquidity).
data_note: OHLCV (dollar volume = close x volume). Venue-specific, and affected by wash trading on unregulated exchanges.

sources.citation: Zhang, W., Li, Y. (2023), Liquidity risk and expected cryptocurrency returns, International Journal of Finance & Economics 28(1), 472-492
sources.finding: [A] Using the Amihud measure, 'we document a negative relationship between liquidity and cryptocurrency returns', robust to other liquidity measures and size screens. There is no significant intertemporal (time-series) relation for three leading coins.

sources.citation: Leirvik, T. (2022), Cryptocurrency returns and the volatility of liquidity, Finance Research Letters 44, 102031
sources.finding: [A] For the five largest coins, the volatility of liquidity is generally positively related to returns, and the relation is 'highly time-varying'. Returns tend to be higher when liquidity is low.

sources.citation: Wei, W.C. (2018), Liquidity and market efficiency in cryptocurrencies, Economics Letters 168, 21-24
sources.finding: [A] Across 456 coins, return predictability diminishes as liquidity rises. Bitcoin shows signs of efficiency, while many illiquid coins show autocorrelation.

sources.citation: Liu, Y., Tsyvinski, A., Wu, X. (2022), Common risk factors in cryptocurrency, Journal of Finance 77(2) (NBER WP 25882)
sources.finding: [S] Long low-volume / short high-volume coins earns about 3% weekly excess (3.2% using dollar volume), gross. This is a size/liquidity effect, explained by the crypto three-factor model.

crypto_evidence_note: Cross-sectional liquidity effects exist but sit in small, illiquid coins and need shorting. The time-series relation for leading coins is insignificant (Zhang and Li) or time-varying (Leirvik).
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Cross-sectional sorts rebalance weekly (52 a year). Time-series timing on 9 coins: unknown.
fee_sensitivity: Weekly cross-sectional rebalancing is uneconomic at 1.10% a round trip. A time-series liquidity gate adds no trades if used only as a veto.
long_only_note: The published effects are long-short sorts. A long-only use is as a liquidity screen or veto (avoid entries when a coin's liquidity is thin), which serves risk control, not return.
limitations: Effects concentrated in micro-caps outside this universe
The direction of the time-series relation is unclear
Wash trading inflates the volume denominator on some venues
No out-of-sample trading test

high_return_claim.claim: About 3% weekly excess return for long low-volume / short high-volume coins (3.2% for dollar volume), gross of costs (Liu, Tsyvinski and Wu, as summarised)
high_return_claim.drawdown: Not reported in the summary read
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: No. In-sample factor sorts, explained by the three-factor model.

priority_reason: The return effects are cross-sectional, long-short and in micro-caps. For 9 large coins on long-only spot, liquidity is a risk screen, not a return source.

name: Short-term reversal as liquidity provision (low-volume reversal)
summary: Buy recent losers and sell recent winners, concentrated in low-volume or illiquid pairs, to earn the liquidity-provision premium. Bianchi and Dickerson double-sort on past return and abnormal volume, rebalancing every 12 hours.
data_note: OHLCV across many coins at the same time stamp. Published on aggregated multi-exchange data.

sources.citation: Bianchi, D., Babiak, M., Dickerson, A. (2022), Trading volume and liquidity provision in cryptocurrency markets, Journal of Banking & Finance 142, 106547
sources.finding: [A] Reversal (liquidity-provision) returns are concentrated in pairs with lower activity and are 'amplified in smaller, more volatile, and less liquid' pairs, Mar 2017 to Mar 2022.

sources.citation: Bianchi, D., Dickerson, A. (2018), Trading volume in cryptocurrency markets, working paper (CXO Advisory summary)
sources.finding: [S] 26 crypto-assets, 10-minute data, 1 Jan 2017 to 10 May 2018, returns in BTC. A long-short reversal on low-volume assets rebalanced every 12 hours has gross annualised Sharpe ratios 'as high as 2.96'. Outperformance is concentrated in the first months, and the summary notes reformation 'may be costly'.

sources.citation: Zaremba, A. et al. (2021), Up or down? Short-term reversal, momentum, and liquidity effects in cryptocurrency markets, IRFA 78, 101908
sources.finding: [A] (from A-research-report) Daily reversal comes from illiquidity; 'the handful of largest and most tradeable coins exhibit daily momentum rather than a reversal'.

crypto_evidence_note: Positive gross for illiquid coins in long-short form. Negative for large coins, which show continuation. Not shown net of retail fees.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Rebalancing every 12 hours to daily gives hundreds of position changes a year.
fee_sensitivity: At hundreds of round trips, the fees cost several hundred percent a year. Destroyed at 0.55% a side.
long_only_note: Published long-short. A long-only 'buy the low-volume loser' leg on large coins goes against the documented momentum.
limitations: Long-short
Lives in illiquid coins
Gross results only
Decays after the early sample
priority_reason: Real but small-coin, short-horizon and long-short. Fees and the large-coin momentum evidence rule it out; keep only as a falsification test.

name: Cross-exchange premium signal (Coinbase premium, Kimchi premium)
summary: Track the percentage gap between the same coin's price on two venues (e.g. Coinbase BTC-USD vs Binance BTC-USDT, or Korean won vs US price) as a demand/sentiment signal; arbitrage itself is a separate, infeasible trade.
data_note: Built from free public candles of two exchanges (Coinbase + Binance Vision/Kraken). Needs synchronised closes; USD vs USDT basis adds noise.

sources.citation: Makarov, I., Schoar, A. (2020), Trading and arbitrage in cryptocurrency markets, Journal of Financial Economics 135(2), 293-319
sources.finding: [A] 'Large, recurrent arbitrage opportunities across exchanges'; deviations are much larger across than within countries (capital controls), co-move, and widen when bitcoin appreciates sharply.

sources.citation: CoinDesk (2024), Bitcoin's bottom in price could be near or already in, the Coinbase Premium Index suggests
sources.finding: [S] Anecdotes: similar negative readings in Nov 2022 and Aug 2023 preceded local bottoms; notes ETF outflows and government sales may cause the discount mechanically.

crypto_evidence_note: Premia are well documented (Makarov & Schoar) and widen in rallies, i.e. coincident with returns; their power to predict future returns is only anecdotal.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Unknown; as a gate none added.
fee_sensitivity: As a signal, depends on the host rule. Arbitrage between venues would pay two takers per leg plus transfer costs - not viable at 0.55% a side.
long_only_note: Signal use only. Arbitrage needs inventory on both venues and fast transfers (and capital controls for KRW).
limitations: Coincident rather than leading in the published evidence
USD/USDT peg noise
Binance Vision licence is non-commercial
priority_reason: Free data but no predictive evidence; the arbitrage itself is infeasible for this app.

name: Funding-rate contrarian entry (buy after deeply negative funding)
summary: Enter spot long after perpetual funding turns strongly negative (shorts crowded), expecting a short squeeze or reversal; exit after a fixed hold or when funding normalises. No published parameterisation found.
data_note: Same funding sources as the carry veto (Binance Vision from 2020, Hyperliquid API, Bybit). Derivatives data, not spot OHLCV.

sources.citation: Brave New Coin (2023), Testing theory: is perpetual swap funding rate predictive?
sources.finding: [FT] BitMEX funding, 2 Nov 2022 to 22 Feb 2023, next 8-hour spot return: regression R-squared about 0.001, slope not significant; some reversal after the most extreme negative readings. Author calls the link 'loose'.

sources.citation: Schmeling, Schrimpf, Todorov (2023, rev. 2025), Crypto carry, BIS WP 1087
sources.finding: [A] High carry predicts crashes; says nothing about negative carry predicting rebounds.

crypto_evidence_note: Only a four-month practitioner regression (no predictive power overall) and anecdotes about extremes; no peer-reviewed test found.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Roughly 2-6 round trips if triggered only by extreme negative funding (inference; extremes are rare per the BNC sample).
fee_sensitivity: At 2-6 round trips the drag is about 2-7% a year; each trade needs a rebound above 1.10% to break even.
long_only_note: Buy-side only; derivatives used as data.
limitations: Very few extreme events per coin; statistically untestable per coin
Extremes cluster in crashes (FTX, Nov 2022), when spot can keep falling
No published rule to fix parameters from
priority_reason: Anecdotal evidence, few events, no published rule; keep as a falsification test after the carry veto.

name: Large trades and whale transfers as signals
summary: Flag unusually large exchange prints (for example, trades over 10 BTC) or large on-chain transfers to or from exchange addresses. Rules buy after large inflows from exchanges (accumulation) and avoid entries after large deposits to exchanges (potential selling).
data_note: Exchange prints need trade-level data (Coinbase public trades, slow backfill). On-chain transfers are public on the blockchain, but labelling exchange addresses usually needs a paid data vendor; free labels are partial.

sources.citation: Ante, L., Fiedler, I. (2021), Market reaction to large transfers on the Bitcoin blockchain: do size and motive matter?, Finance Research Letters 39, 101619
sources.finding: [A] 2,132 transfers of at least 500 BTC: results across all transfers are 'inconclusive'. Split by size and by presumed motive (known exchange addresses), significant price effects appear.

sources.citation: Makarov, I., Schoar, A. (2020), Trading and arbitrage in cryptocurrency markets, Journal of Financial Economics 135(2)
sources.finding: [A] Signed order flow explains most contemporaneous BTC returns (80% for the common component), so large prints move price at the time, not necessarily afterwards.

crypto_evidence_note: Event-study effects at minute horizons, conditional on motive labels. No cost-inclusive trading test was found.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Depends on thresholds; event-driven, possibly dozens a year.
fee_sensitivity: Minute-horizon effects will not cover 1.10%. Only a daily aggregate (net exchange flow) could, and that has no verified evidence here.
long_only_note: Usable as a long entry or veto.
limitations: Needs trades or labelled on-chain data
Inconclusive unconditional results
Short-horizon effects
priority_reason: Weak, short-horizon evidence and data that are hard to obtain for free (exchange labels). Overlaps the on-chain data-source work.

name: Liquidation-cascade rebound (buy after a long-liquidation flush)
summary: After a large long-liquidation spike (forced selling), buy spot expecting a partial rebound; exit after a fixed hold. Practitioner idea with no published parameters.
data_note: Binance Vision has liquidationSnapshot only for COIN-M futures (daily folder); USD-M liquidations history via Tardis.dev (paid, from 2020-01-07; free first day of each month) or Coinglass (paid). Exchange liquidation streams are live only. Event data, not OHLCV.

sources.citation: Cheng, Deng, Wang, Yu (2021), arXiv 2102.04591
sources.finding: [A] Liquidations are large relative to outstanding futures (3.51% long, 1.89% short, daily) on BitMEX; margin of 1% far too low.

sources.citation: Lim, B.C. (2026), study of the 10 October 2025 Hyperliquid liquidation cascade, Journal of Financial Data Analytics 1(2)
sources.finding: [S] Minute-level inside-market metrics for five Hyperliquid perpetuals around the cascade, from Hyperliquid's public L2 archive; market-quality study, not a trading rule. Status and title not confirmed.

crypto_evidence_note: No study found that tests rebound returns after liquidation spikes; commentary is split between 'flush marks a bottom' and 'cascade feeds further falls'.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Perhaps 2-8 large events a year (inference); per-coin samples tiny.
fee_sensitivity: Each rebound must exceed 1.10%; at a few trades a year the drag is small, but the edge is unmeasured.
long_only_note: Buy-only; derivatives used as data.
limitations: Free USD-M liquidation history not found
Few events
Catching a falling knife during multi-day cascades
priority_reason: No evidence and history mostly paid; revisit only if a free archive is confirmed.

name: Open-interest change signal (leverage build-up / flush)
summary: Use daily changes in futures open interest with price direction (rising OI with rising price = leveraged trend; falling OI after a drop = deleveraging) as an entry filter. Practitioner rule; no published parameters.
data_note: Binance Vision USD-M 'metrics' daily files (open interest, long/short ratios) from 2020-09-01 for BTCUSDT; Hyperliquid metaAndAssetCtxs gives current OI only (no history found); Coinglass history is paid. Derivatives data, not spot OHLCV.

sources.citation: Cheng, Z., Deng, J., Wang, T., Yu, M. (2021), Liquidation, leverage and optimal margin in Bitcoin futures markets, arXiv 2102.04591
sources.finding: [A] BitMEX perpetual: daily forced liquidations are 3.51% (long) and 1.89% (short) of outstanding futures; liquidated traders used about 60x average leverage. Risk study, not return prediction.

crypto_evidence_note: No peer-reviewed study found that OI changes predict spot returns; evidence is practitioner commentary.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Unknown; as a filter it adds none.
fee_sensitivity: As a filter: none added. As a standalone signal on daily OI swings: likely many trades and a drag above 10% a year.
long_only_note: Information only; no derivatives position.
limitations: Free OI history starts 2020-09 (Binance) and is one venue only
OI is fragmented across venues
No published rule
priority_reason: No return-prediction evidence; partial free history; consider only as a feature in a pooled model later.

name: 15-minute reversal after taker-driven moves
summary: After a 15-minute candle driven by aggressive taker flow, bet on partial reversal in the next 15 minutes (liquidity provision). Measured across 183 Binance pairs against matched US equities.
data_note: Needs taker flow (trades) and book depth to condition on; plain 15-minute candles give only the unconditional reversal.

sources.citation: Kitron, N.A., Wengrowicz, J.M. (2026), Short-horizon mean reversion in cryptocurrency markets: a matched cross-market measurement, arXiv 2608.21888
sources.finding: [A] About 90% of 183 Binance pairs show significant 15-minute reversal, against 2.7% of 187 US stocks and ETFs. The gross edge peaks near 1.3 bp a trade, 'too small to clear' costs at a 5 bp round trip. Exact permutation null, frozen holdout.

crypto_evidence_note: The effect is real and rigorously measured, but economically negative even at a 5 bp round trip. At 110 bp it is hopeless.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Up to tens of thousands of 15-minute bets.
fee_sensitivity: The gross edge of 1.3 bp is about 85 times smaller than the 110 bp round trip. Destroyed.
long_only_note: Two-sided as measured; the long-only half (buy after taker-sell bursts) has the same per-trade size problem.
limitations: Edge far below costs
Needs trade and book data
Preprint
priority_reason: Strong evidence that it is too small to trade even at institutional costs. Keep only as a documented negative.

name: Trade-flow imbalance (aggressor / taker buy-sell flow, signed volume)
summary: Signed volume = taker-buy volume minus taker-sell volume over a window, or the taker-buy ratio. Rules go long after strongly positive net taker flow. It is used intraday as a short-horizon predictor, or aggregated daily as a sentiment filter.
data_note: Needs trade-level data with the aggressor side, not plain OHLCV. Coinbase public trades: the 'side' field is the maker side (so taker = opposite), paginated by trade id, slow to backfill. Binance klines carry 'Taker buy base asset volume' and aggTrades carry the 'Was the buyer the maker?' flag. But Binance Vision bulk files are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and forbid 'live proprietary trading execution', so use them for backtesting only.

sources.citation: Silantyev, E. (2019), Order flow analysis of cryptocurrency markets, Digital Finance 1(1), 191-218
sources.finding: [A] BitMEX XBTUSD trades and quotes: trade-flow imbalance explains contemporaneous price changes better than aggregate order-flow imbalance. Thin depth and slow update rates differentiate crypto microstructure.

sources.citation: Makarov, I., Schoar, A. (2020), Trading and arbitrage in cryptocurrency markets, Journal of Financial Economics 135(2), 293-319
sources.finding: [A] Tick data from 34 exchanges: the common component of signed volume 'explains 80% of bitcoin returns'. This is contemporaneous, not predictive.

sources.citation: Kitron, N.A., Wengrowicz, J.M. (2026), Short-horizon mean reversion in cryptocurrency markets: a matched cross-market measurement, arXiv 2608.21888
sources.finding: [A] 15-minute reversal in 183 Binance pairs is concentrated after taker-driven moves and grows with flow intensity. The gross edge peaks near 1.3 bp a trade, too small for a 5 bp round trip.

sources.citation: Binance, Spot API market data endpoints (klines and aggTrades fields)
sources.finding: [FT] Kline index 9 is 'Taker buy base asset volume'; aggTrades include 'm' = 'Was the buyer the maker?'.

sources.citation: Coinbase Developer Platform, Exchange API: Get product trades
sources.finding: [FT] Public endpoint for the latest trades (default limit 1000), paginated with before/after trade-id cursors. 'side' is the maker order's side: buy = down-tick, sell = up-tick.

crypto_evidence_note: Strong contemporaneous link. Predictive power exists at seconds to minutes but is tiny gross, and reverses after taker bursts at 15 minutes. No daily-horizon taker-flow trading study with costs was found.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Intraday use: hundreds to thousands. As a daily filter on a host strategy: fewer than the host's trades.
fee_sensitivity: Intraday edges of about 1 bp against a 110 bp round trip are destroyed. Only a daily veto could avoid added cost, and it has no evidence.
long_only_note: Usable as a long-entry filter; the published predictive uses are two-sided.
limitations: Needs trade-level data
Binance bulk-data terms forbid live-trading use
Coinbase backfill is slow
Predictive horizon far shorter than the fee allows
priority_reason: Documented effects are contemporaneous or at minutes, with gross edges about 85 times smaller than the round trip. Daily use is untested, and the data are partly restricted.

name: VPIN flow toxicity and other microstructure risk measures (Roll spread, Kyle's lambda)
summary: VPIN is the volume-synchronised probability of informed trading: average |buy - sell| volume over volume buckets, with trades classified by bulk volume classification. High VPIN signals toxicity-induced short-term volatility. Proposed here only as a risk or entry-delay filter.
data_note: Bulk volume classification can approximate buy/sell volume from bar price changes, so 1-minute OHLCV suffices for an approximation. Exact VPIN needs trades. Coinbase 1-minute candles are free (300 per request).

sources.citation: Easley, D., López de Prado, M., O'Hara, M. (2012), Flow toxicity and liquidity in a high-frequency world, Review of Financial Studies 25(5), 1457-1493
sources.finding: [A] Defines VPIN, computed in volume time with a bulk volume classification, and shows it 'is a useful indicator of short-term, toxicity-induced volatility' (equity futures).

sources.citation: Easley, D., O'Hara, M., Yang, S., Zhang, Z. (2024), Microstructure and market dynamics in crypto markets, SSRN 4814346 (working paper)
sources.finding: [A] Tests whether standard microstructure measures (Amihud, Kyle's lambda, VPIN, Roll, Roll impact) explain and predict crypto price dynamics with machine learning, Jan 2021 to Jul 2023, including the crypto winter. The PDF could not be parsed here, so no figures are quoted.

crypto_evidence_note: It predicts short-horizon dynamics (volatility, spreads), not return direction. No crypto study uses it as a long-only entry filter with costs.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: No new trades if used as a veto or delay on a host strategy.
fee_sensitivity: No added fees as a veto. Its value would come from avoiding entries just before volatility spikes, which is unproven.
long_only_note: Risk filter only.
limitations: Predicts volatility, not direction
The VPIN flash-crash claims are contested in the literature (not checked here)
The exact form needs trades
priority_reason: Interesting as a risk measure, but its horizon (minutes) is far below the daily strategies the fees allow, and there is no long-only evidence.

name: Order-book imbalance and order-flow imbalance (OFI) from limit-order-book events
summary: OFI sums changes in best-bid and best-ask queue sizes. Depth imbalance = (bid depth - ask depth) / (bid depth + ask depth) over the top levels. Both predict the next mid-price moves over seconds; the price impact is linear in OFI with a slope that falls with depth (Cont et al.).
data_note: Needs a full order-book history (L2 updates). Coinbase gives only a current snapshot (REST) or a live WebSocket, so history must be recorded continuously. No free historical L2 for Coinbase was found.

sources.citation: Cont, R., Kukanov, A., Stoikov, S. (2014), The price impact of order book events, Journal of Financial Econometrics 12(1), 47-88
sources.finding: [A] For 50 US stocks (NYSE TAQ), short-interval price changes are mainly explained by order-flow imbalance at the best quotes, linearly, with a slope inversely related to depth.

sources.citation: Fang, F., Chung, W., Ventre, C., Basios, M., Kanthan, L., Li, L., Wu, F. (2020), Ascertaining price formation in cryptocurrency markets with deep learning, arXiv 2003.00803
sources.finding: [A] Tick-level data from 8 crypto pairs: a 'consistent 78% accuracy' predicting the direction of the next-tick mid-price on live BTC-USD. The horizon is one tick, and no costs are reported.

sources.citation: Bieganowski, B., Ślepaczuk, R. (2026), Explainable patterns in cryptocurrency microstructure, arXiv 2602.00776
sources.finding: [A] Binance Futures 1-second order books and trades, Jan 2022 to Oct 2025, five assets. CatBoost on book and trade features; SHAP links predictability to order-flow imbalance, spread and adverse selection. A 'conservative top-of-book taker backtest' is mentioned, with no figures in the abstract.

crypto_evidence_note: Predictive at tick-to-seconds horizons, where profits are a fraction of a basis point. Irrelevant at 0.55% a side.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Thousands or more as an HFT signal.
fee_sensitivity: Completely destroyed: the per-trade edge is orders of magnitude below 1.10%.
long_only_note: An HFT signal; would need market-making or two-sided taker trading.
limitations: Needs continuous recorded L2 data
Needs low-latency execution
Edge measured in ticks
priority_reason: The evidence is strong but at tick horizons. It needs sub-second execution and a historical order book that is not freely available, and the 0.55% fee rules it out completely.

name: EWMA volatility (RiskMetrics, λ = 0.94 daily)
summary: σ²(t) = λσ²(t-1) + (1-λ)r²(t-1), with λ = 0.94 for daily data in RiskMetrics. Moskowitz et al. size time-series momentum with an exponentially weighted variance with a 60-day centre of mass.
data_note: Daily closes only.

sources.citation: J.P. Morgan/Reuters (1996), RiskMetrics Technical Document, 4th edition (MSCI catalogue page)
sources.finding: [S] Catalogue page only. The 0.94 daily decay is attributed to this document by secondary sources; the original text was not read.

sources.citation: Moskowitz, T.J., Ooi, Y.H., Pedersen, L.H. (2012), Time series momentum, Journal of Financial Economics 104(2), 228-250
sources.finding: [FT] (from A-research-report) Positions sized to 40% annual volatility from an exponentially weighted variance with a 60-day centre of mass.

crypto_evidence_note: No crypto-specific test of EWMA against alternatives was read. Bergsli et al. (HAR beats GARCH) suggest richer models forecast better, but EWMA is the simplest robust choice.

reference_implementations.name: arch: EWMA/RiskMetrics and RiskMetrics 2006 variance models

expected_trades_per_coin_year: None; an input.
fee_sensitivity: As for any sizing input: re-size only beyond a band.
long_only_note: Direction-neutral.
limitations: λ fixed by convention, not fitted to crypto
Reacts slowly to regime breaks at λ = 0.94
priority_reason: The standard, parameter-light estimator for the volatility-sizing tests already planned. Trivial to implement.

name: Realised volatility estimators and volatility clustering (close-to-close, Parkinson, Garman-Klass, Yang-Zhang)
summary: Estimate volatility from returns (close-to-close standard deviation over n days) or from the daily range (Parkinson, Garman-Klass, Rogers-Satchell, Yang-Zhang). Clustering means today's volatility predicts tomorrow's. An input to sizing, stops and regime filters, not a signal on its own.
data_note: Daily OHLC is enough for range estimators. Coinbase 1-minute to 1-day candles are free. 24/7 trading has no overnight gap, so the open-jump component of Yang-Zhang is near zero.

sources.citation: Yang, D., Zhang, Q. (2000), Drift-independent volatility estimation based on high, low, open, and close prices, Journal of Business 73(3), 477-492
sources.finding: [A] A multi-period OHLC estimator that is unbiased, drift-independent and robust to opening jumps, with the smallest variance in its class, a 'dramatic' accuracy gain over close-to-close.

sources.citation: Catania, L., Grassi, S. (2022), Forecasting cryptocurrency volatility, International Journal of Forecasting 38(3), 878-894
sources.finding: [A] 606 cryptocurrencies: a robust volatility filter is 'strongly required'. Long memory and leverage effects are present, and time-varying skewness improves volatility, density and quantile forecasts across horizons.

sources.citation: Bergsli, L.Ø., Lind, A.F., Molnár, P., Polasik, M. (2022), Forecasting volatility of Bitcoin, Research in International Business and Finance 59
sources.finding: [S, via C-evidence.md] HAR on realised variance beats GARCH, most at short horizons: volatility is forecastable, returns much less so.

crypto_evidence_note: Volatility clustering and forecastability are well established for crypto. This is a measurement tool; it carries no return claim.

reference_implementations.name: arch (Kevin Sheppard): volatility models and realised measures
reference_implementations.licence: University of Illinois/NCSA-style permissive licence (LICENSE.md text; name not stated on page)

expected_trades_per_coin_year: None. It is an input.
fee_sensitivity: None directly. If it drives frequent re-sizing, each re-size costs 0.55% of the traded amount, so use bands.
long_only_note: Direction-neutral input.
limitations: Range estimators are biased by discrete sampling and by thin coins' wicks
The daily cut-off time is arbitrary on 24/7 markets
priority_reason: Strong evidence and free data. It is the shared input every sizing, stop and regime test needs, and the repo already has a simple version (signal_fusion volatility).

name: Volatility targeting and inverse-volatility sizing (shrink-only for spot)
summary: Size each position as target_vol / forecast_vol, capped at 100% on spot: Zarattini et al. use min(25%/σ90, 200%); Moskowitz et al. use 40% per position. Re-size only beyond a band; Zarattini et al. used 20%.
data_note: Daily returns.

sources.citation: Grobys, K., Kolari, J.W., Sandretto, D., Shahzad, S.J.H., Äijö, J. (2025), Cryptocurrency momentum has (not) its moments, Financial Markets and Portfolio Management
sources.finding: [A] Weekly data 2016-2023, large-cap coins, equal-weighted momentum portfolios: crypto momentum suffers severe crashes, and 'even a single cryptocurrency can cause insignificant momentum portfolio returns'. Volatility management is 'a useful tool for mitigating cryptocurrency momentum crashes'. A secondary summary adds that tail risk was not significantly changed.

sources.citation: Harvey, C.R., Hoyle, E., Korgaonkar, R., Rattray, S., Sargaison, M., Van Hemert, O. (2018), The impact of volatility targeting, Journal of Portfolio Management 45(1), 14-33
sources.finding: [FT] (from A-research-report) Volatility scaling raises Sharpe ratios for risk assets through the leverage effect, has negligible effect for bonds, FX and commodities, and reduces extreme returns.

sources.citation: Cederburg, S., O'Doherty, M.S., Wang, F., Yan, X. (2020), On the performance of volatility-managed portfolios, Journal of Financial Economics 138(1), 95-117
sources.finding: [A] (from A-research-report) Across 103 equity strategies, volatility-managed portfolios do not systematically outperform, and real-time versions earn less.

sources.citation: Zarattini, C., Pagani, A., Barbon, A. (2025), Catching crypto trends, SSRN 5209907
sources.finding: [FT, via A-research-report.md] Sizing min(25%/σ, 200%). A 20% rebalance band recovered about 100 bp a year at 50 bp costs; volatility sizing 'may also hinder full participation in large trending moves'.

crypto_evidence_note: Crypto: it helps momentum crash risk (Grobys et al.) and is used in the best long-only breakout study (Zarattini et al.). Against it: the repo's own development run (docs/dev/SIG4-REPORT-dev.md, Q3) found no drawdown reduction from the volatility shrink against random sizing (p = 0.69). Equities: contested (Cederburg et al.).
expected_trades_per_coin_year: No new entries. Re-sizing adds partial trades unless banded; size once at entry to add none.
fee_sensitivity: Each re-size pays 0.55% on the traded amount. Size at entry only, or re-size beyond a wide band (20%+).
long_only_note: Shrink-only (cap at 100% of the allocation, no leverage) is natural for spot.
limitations: Spot cannot lever up in calm periods, so only the shrink half is available
Repo development test found no drawdown benefit
Small accounts (£50) hit the ~$1 minimum when shrinking
priority_reason: Moderate evidence, OHLCV only and no added trades if sized at entry. The A-research-report already scheduled it as a sizing policy, but the repo's Q3 result means it must be re-tested on the slow strategies, not assumed.

name: GARCH-family conditional volatility models (GARCH, EGARCH, GJR/TARCH, CGARCH)
summary: Fit GARCH(1,1) or asymmetric and component variants to daily returns and use the one-step forecast for sizing, stop distances or a volatility regime gate. For Bitcoin, Katsiampa found that AR(1)-CGARCH(1,1) fitted best.
data_note: Daily closes. HYPE has under two years of history, which is short for stable GARCH estimates.

sources.citation: Katsiampa, P. (2017), Volatility estimation for Bitcoin: a comparison of GARCH models, Economics Letters 158, 3-6
sources.finding: [A] Among GARCH-type models, AR-CGARCH fits Bitcoin best, which shows the importance of short- and long-run components of conditional variance. The finding is in-sample goodness of fit.

sources.citation: Darné, O., Charles, A. (2019), Volatility estimation for Bitcoin: replication and robustness, International Economics
sources.finding: [S] The replication finds partly different results and concludes the GARCH-type models seem not appropriate for Bitcoin once robustness checks and jumps are considered.

sources.citation: Catania, L., Grassi, S. (2022), Forecasting cryptocurrency volatility, International Journal of Forecasting 38(3)
sources.finding: [A] Score-driven models with leverage, long memory and time-varying skewness improve forecasts across 606 coins; a robust filter is needed.

sources.citation: Bergsli, L.Ø. et al. (2022), Forecasting volatility of Bitcoin, Research in International Business and Finance 59
sources.finding: [S, via C-evidence.md] HAR on realised variance beats GARCH, most at short horizons.

crypto_evidence_note: Volatility is forecastable, but which GARCH variant is best is unstable (replication disagreed), and HAR on intraday data beat GARCH. No evidence that GARCH sizing beats EWMA sizing for a long-only trend strategy.

reference_implementations.name: arch: GARCH, EGARCH, TARCH, FIGARCH and more

expected_trades_per_coin_year: None; an input.
fee_sensitivity: No direct effect.
long_only_note: Direction-neutral.
limitations: Unstable model ranking
Estimation fragile on short histories (HYPE)
Fat tails and jumps poorly captured
priority_reason: More complex than EWMA, with no evidence that it improves trading decisions. Test only if EWMA sizing shows value.

name: HAR-RV realised-volatility forecasting
summary: Regress tomorrow's realised variance on daily, weekly (5-day) and monthly (22-day) averages of realised variance computed from intraday returns (Corsi 2009).
data_note: Needs intraday candles (for example, 5-minute) to build daily realised variance. Coinbase 5-minute candles are free, but 300 per request means many requests for multi-year history.

sources.citation: Corsi, F. (2009), A simple approximate long-memory model of realized volatility, Journal of Financial Econometrics 7(2), 174-196
sources.finding: [A] The HAR-RV model, an AR-type model on realised volatility over different horizons, reproduces long memory and shows 'remarkably good forecasting performance'.

sources.citation: Bergsli, L.Ø. et al. (2022), Forecasting volatility of Bitcoin, Research in International Business and Finance 59
sources.finding: [S, via C-evidence.md] HAR on realised variance beats GARCH for Bitcoin, most at short horizons.

crypto_evidence_note: Better volatility forecasts for Bitcoin. Its value for long-only trade decisions is untested.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: None; an input.
fee_sensitivity: No direct effect.
long_only_note: Direction-neutral.
limitations: Needs intraday data
Forecast gain may not translate into trading gain
priority_reason: The best-evidenced volatility forecaster for Bitcoin, but it matters only if volatility sizing or gating shows value with simpler estimators first.

name: Implied volatility (Deribit DVOL) and the variance risk premium as a regime signal
summary: DVOL is Deribit's 30-day forward-looking annualised implied-volatility index for BTC and ETH. Candidate rules gate entries on the DVOL level or change, or on the variance risk premium (implied minus realised).
data_note: Derivatives (options) market data, not spot, listed here under cross_exchange. Deribit's public endpoint public/get_volatility_index_data (currency, start/end timestamps, resolution) needs no authentication. It covers BTC and ETH only. History start is not verified (believed 2021). Deribit's Terms were not checked.

sources.citation: Deribit API reference, public/get_volatility_index_data
sources.finding: [S] Public method with currency, start_timestamp, end_timestamp and resolution parameters. The docs conflict on the resolution parameter's name. The same docs are mirrored on Coinbase's developer site.

sources.citation: Almeida, C., Grith, M., Miftachov, R., Wang, Z. (2024), Risk premia in the Bitcoin market, arXiv 2410.15195
sources.finding: [A] Bitcoin has a larger variance risk premium than the S&P 500, with two volatility regimes. The abstract does not test whether the premium predicts returns.

crypto_evidence_note: No verified study shows that DVOL or the Bitcoin variance risk premium predicts spot returns. Practitioner claims exist but were not verified.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: A gate: removes some host entries. Applies only to BTC and ETH, or to all coins through BTC as the market proxy.
fee_sensitivity: None as a veto.
long_only_note: Uses derivatives data only as information; trading stays spot long-only.
limitations: BTC and ETH only
Short history
No return-predictability evidence
Third-party venue terms not reviewed
priority_reason: Free but derivatives-only data, a short history, BTC and ETH only, and no evidence that it predicts returns.

name: Volatility (range) breakout: open +/- k x prior range, Larry Williams style
summary: Enter long when price exceeds today's open plus k x yesterday's range (k = 0.25 in the broker version read; k = 0.5 is common in crypto scripts). Exit at a target or stop of 2 x the range, or at the end of the session.
data_note: OHLCV. Crypto has no session open, so a UTC daily open must be chosen.

sources.citation: WH SelfInvest, Trading strategy: Larry Williams volatility break-out
sources.finding: [S] Range = 0.25 x the previous day's high and low added to and subtracted from the open; long above the upper bound, short below; target and stop at 2x range; positions closed by 21:59. Backtests on index futures were 'variable but none are negative' (chart images only; vendor claim). Works in directional, volatile markets and suffers in sideways ones.

crypto_evidence_note: No peer-reviewed crypto test was found; only community scripts. The closest evidenced relative is the daily channel breakout (STRAT-004; Zarattini et al. 2025).
expected_trades_per_coin_year: About one signal a day as published, so roughly 100-250 round trips a year.
fee_sensitivity: At 100-250 round trips, fees cost 110-275% a year. Destroyed.
long_only_note: The long half works as long-or-cash, but the turnover problem remains.
limitations: Intraday turnover
No crypto evidence
An arbitrary session open on 24/7 markets
priority_reason: Anecdotal evidence and daily turnover that the fees destroy. STRAT-004 already covers the slow breakout idea.

name: Volatility squeeze: Bollinger Band inside Keltner Channel, or band-width minimum, then breakout
summary: When Bollinger Bands (20, 2) contract inside Keltner Channels (20, 1.5 ATR) or the band width hits a six-month minimum, wait for a close outside the band and trade in that direction (TTM squeeze, Bollinger's 'squeeze').
data_note: OHLCV.

sources.citation: Fang, J., Jacobsen, B., Qin, Y. (2014), Popularity versus profitability: evidence from Bollinger Bands, SSRN working paper (CXO Advisory summary)
sources.finding: [S] 14 stock indexes to March 2014, with 1% one-way friction for net returns. The squeeze worked in the full and pre-1983 samples and weakened later: after 2001 the squeeze buy-minus-sell spread was -0.07% against a 0.01% market. The authors read this as market adaptation after the bands became popular.

sources.citation: CXO Advisory (2010), Testing a complex breakout indicator (Bollinger-within-Keltner squeeze on SPY)
sources.finding: [S] SPY, Jan 1993 to Jan 2010: the squeeze held on 19% of days. Breakout direction against the subsequent trend had correlation -0.11 and R-squared 0.01 (86 breakouts). The test 'does not support a belief that breakout indications ... are reliable'.

sources.citation: Lento, C., Gradojevic, N., Wright, C.S. (2007), Investment information content in Bollinger Bands?, Applied Financial Economics Letters 3(4), 263-267
sources.finding: [A] (from A-research-report) After transaction costs, Bollinger Band rules are consistently unable to beat buy-and-hold.

crypto_evidence_note: No crypto study was found. Equity evidence shows the squeeze decaying after it became popular.

reference_implementations.name: TA-Lib BBANDS + ATR (Keltner built from EMA and ATR)

expected_trades_per_coin_year: On daily bars, a few squeezes a year per coin (CXO: 86 separated breakouts in 17 years on SPY, about 5 a year).
fee_sensitivity: About 5 round trips a year cost about 5.5% a year, tolerable if the direction were predictive, but the evidence says it is not.
long_only_note: Long-only: take upside breakouts only.
limitations: Negative or decaying evidence in equities
No crypto evidence
Direction of the breakout not predicted
priority_reason: Low turnover suits the fees, but the evidence on direction is negative, and it adds little over STRAT-004's channel breakout. Keep as a falsification test.

name: Probability calibration and expected-value (cost-threshold) gate
summary: Calibrate any model's scores to probabilities (Platt sigmoid or isotonic regression on held-out data), then trade only when the expected net return p x gain - (1 - p) x loss - 1.10% is positive, and size from the calibrated probability.
data_note: Needs the model's out-of-sample predictions and realised outcomes; no extra market data.

sources.citation: Niculescu-Mizil, A., Caruana, R. (2005), Predicting good probabilities with supervised learning, ICML 2005, 625-632
sources.finding: [A] Boosted trees and SVMs give distorted (sigmoid-shaped) probabilities; Platt scaling or isotonic regression fixes them, after which they give the best probabilities; isotonic regression overfits when calibration data are scarce.

sources.citation: Bysik, Slepaczuk (2026), Machine learning-based Bitcoin trading under transaction costs, arXiv 2606.00060
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence] Trading only when the forecast exceeds a cost threshold turned failing naive sign strategies profitable in selected configurations at 10 bp.

sources.citation: Meyer, M., Barziy, I., Joubert, J.F. (2023), Meta-labeling: calibration and position sizing, Journal of Financial Data Science 5(2)
sources.finding: [S, repository summary] Calibration significantly improves fixed position-sizing methods.

crypto_evidence_note: Calibration is well-established statistics; its trading value in crypto rests on one working paper at 10 bp.
