expected_trades_per_coin_year: Fewer than the underlying model's; it only removes trades whose expected value is below the cost.
fee_sensitivity: This is the mechanism that makes any model respect 1.10% a round trip; it cannot add trades.
long_only_note: Applies to long entries only.
limitations: Needs enough held-out predictions to calibrate (isotonic needs more)
Calibration drifts across regimes
It cannot create an edge the model lacks
priority_reason: Infrastructure every ML or LLM test needs at this cost level; cheap and only removes trades.

name: Meta-labelling with triple-barrier labels on an existing rule
summary: A secondary classifier, trained on triple-barrier outcomes (profit-take, stop-loss, expiry) of a primary rule's own signals (e.g. STRAT-004 or STRAT-005 entries), decides whether to take each signal and how much to stake; the side always comes from the primary rule (Lopez de Prado 2018, ch. 3).
data_note: OHLCV plus the primary rule's signal history.

sources.citation: Lopez de Prado, M. (2018), Advances in Financial Machine Learning, Wiley, ch. 3
sources.finding: [S, via A-classic and B-deep notes] Triple-barrier labelling and meta-labelling: the primary model sets the side with high recall and a secondary classifier decides whether to act; ordinary k-fold cross-validation over-inflates results, so purged CV is required.

sources.citation: Joubert, J.F. (2022), Meta-labeling: theory and framework, Journal of Financial Data Science 4(3), 31-44
sources.finding: [S, repository summary] Splits meta-labelling into three components; a controlled experiment suggests each improves strategy metrics. No numbers read.

sources.citation: Meyer, M., Barziy, I., Joubert, J.F. (2023), Meta-labeling: calibration and position sizing, Journal of Financial Data Science 5(2), 23-40
sources.finding: [S, repository summary] Across six position-sizing methods, calibration significantly improves fixed sizing methods; methods that estimate their sizing function from training data gain nothing significant from calibration.

sources.citation: Gradzki, Wojcik, Lessmann (2025), Algorithmic crypto trading using information-driven bars, triple barrier labeling and deep learning, Financial Innovation 11
sources.finding: [S, via A-classic] The nearest crypto use of triple-barrier labels (with deep learning); no figures read.

crypto_evidence_note: Practitioner framework papers on synthetic or equity data; no crypto meta-labelling test after costs was read.

reference_implementations.name: hudson-and-thames/meta-labeling (JFDS paper code)
reference_implementations.licence: not shown on the repository page

reference_implementations.name: mlfinlab
reference_implementations.licence: all rights reserved (per a fork's statement, via A-classic)

expected_trades_per_coin_year: At most the primary rule's 3-8 round trips (Donchian 20-60 day counts, A report §4); it can only remove trades.
fee_sensitivity: Cannot add turnover; each correctly skipped losing trade saves the 1.10% round trip plus the loss.
long_only_note: Takes the primary long signal or skips it.
limitations: Few labels: 3-8 trades x 4.3 years x 9 coins is roughly 120-310 primary signals in total [R], too few for a rich classifier, so pooling and very simple models are needed
Must beat a random skip at the same rate (the entry_gate baseline)
Every primary-rule change invalidates the labels
priority_reason: Fits the fixed-strategy design exactly (a gate that only removes trades from STRAT-004/005), but evidence is practitioner-only and the label count is small.

name: Gradient-boosted trees (LightGBM / XGBoost / CatBoost / HistGradientBoosting)
summary: Gradient-boosted decision trees on lagged-return and technical features, pooled across coins, predict direction or a barrier label; trade only when the predicted edge exceeds the round-trip cost (Bysik and Slepaczuk's cost threshold).
data_note: OHLCV only for the published crypto tests used here; some studies add on-chain or sentiment features.

sources.citation: Bysik, Slepaczuk (2026), Machine learning-based Bitcoin trading under transaction costs: evidence from walk-forward forecasting, arXiv 2606.00060
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence] Hourly BTC-USDT 2018-2026, 27-fold walk-forward, 10 bp per transaction: naive sign trading fails after costs; trading only when the forecast exceeds a cost threshold restores profit 'in selected configurations'; best was long-only XGBoost at over 65% a year with Sharpe above 1; bootstrap tests do not support XGBoost beating the neural models.

sources.citation: G-Research (2022), Wrapping up the G-Research Crypto Forecasting competition
sources.finding: [S, via C-evidence] 14 coins, minute-level, three months of live scoring: the top three all used LightGBM; G-Research calls it 'low signal, high noise'; one team's cross-validation correlation of 0.073-0.078 fell to about 0.016-0.020 live, roughly 4x shrinkage.

sources.citation: Jaquart, P., Dann, D., Weinhardt, C. (2021), Short-term bitcoin market prediction via machine learning, Journal of Finance and Data Science 7
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence] At 1-60 minutes, gradient boosting and recurrent nets were the best models and beat a random classifier; a long-short strategy made up to 39% a month before costs and was negative after costs.

sources.citation: Makridakis, S., Spiliotis, E., Assimakopoulos, V. (2022), M5 accuracy competition: results, findings, and conclusions, International Journal of Forecasting 38(4)
sources.finding: [A, via A-classic] LightGBM-based global models won a large retail-sales forecasting competition; not finance.

crypto_evidence_note: Forecast skill is small and shrinks live (G-Research); trading profits appear only at 10 bp in selected configurations (Bysik and Slepaczuk) and vanish after costs at short horizons (Jaquart 2021).
expected_trades_per_coin_year: As a gate on a daily base rule: at most the base rule's 3-12 round trips. As a stand-alone hourly classifier: hundreds (Bysik and Slepaczuk trade hourly).
fee_sensitivity: The 10 bp results do not transfer to 0.55% a side: an hourly classifier would need more than 1.10% gross per trade. Viable only as a daily gate with an explicit cost threshold.
long_only_note: The best Bysik and Slepaczuk configuration was long-only; most other published results are long-short.
limitations: Gains reported only 'in selected configurations' (multiple-testing risk)
Live performance shrinks several-fold versus cross-validation
Feature engineering, not model choice, drove competition wins

high_return_claim.claim: Long-only XGBoost over 65% a year with Sharpe above 1, net of 10 bp per transaction
high_return_claim.leverage: not stated in what was read (perpetual-futures data)
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: Walk-forward, but the best of selected configurations; single coin in a strongly rising period

priority_reason: The ML family with the best crypto evidence and already a model-lab contestant (HistGB), but no evidence near 0.55% a side; worth testing only as a cost-thresholded gate on a slow rule.

name: Regularised logistic / linear model on own and cross-coin lagged returns
summary: A regularised logistic (or ridge/LASSO linear) model predicts the next period's sign or return of a coin from its own lagged returns and other coins' lagged returns (e.g. BTC's lag for altcoins); long when the predicted probability clears a threshold, else cash. Guo et al. use adaptive LASSO on daily cross-coin lags.
data_note: Daily OHLCV for all nine coins, aligned to the same close time. OHLCV only. HYPE has under two years of history, so pooling across coins is needed.

sources.citation: Guo, L., Sang, B., Tu, J., Wang, Y. (2024), Cross-cryptocurrency return predictability, Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control 163
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence] Other coins' lagged returns predict a coin's daily return out of sample (adaptive LASSO, Binance data). The working-paper version reports a long-short 2.16% a day after costs, a size C-evidence flags as implausible.

sources.citation: Fischer, T.G., Krauss, C., Deinert, A. (2019), Statistical arbitrage in cryptocurrency markets, Journal of Risk and Financial Management 12(1), 31
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence] Predicting whether each of 40 coins beats the cross-sectional median at 120 minutes: logistic regression earned about 18.8% a year and random forest about 29% (7.1 bp a day), long-short after costs (level unverified), out of sample 18 Jun to 17 Sep 2018 only.

sources.citation: Cakici, N., Shahzad, S.J.H., Bedowska-Sojka, B., Zaremba, A. (2024), Machine learning and the cross-section of cryptocurrency returns, International Review of Financial Analysis 94
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence] Most ML portfolios are profitable after costs, but alphas depend on small, illiquid, volatile coins; model complexity adds little over linear models.

crypto_evidence_note: Positive results are long-short, cross-sectional, short-sample or at fees of 0.25% or less; no long-only test near 1.10% a round trip was found. The repository's model-lab batch 1 (logistic contestant) had too few trades to tell.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: 20-60 round trips if it trades every sign flip of a noisy daily forecast [R]; 4-12 with a cost threshold and a minimum hold [R].
fee_sensitivity: At 20-60 round trips the drag is 22-66% a year, far above any reported edge. Survives only as a cost-thresholded filter on a slow base rule.
long_only_note: Long when the predicted probability is high, else cash. The published gains are mostly long-short.
limitations: Published gains are long-short or cross-sectional
Nine large coins share one strong common factor, so cross-coin lags carry little independent information
Short HYPE history; pooling needed

high_return_claim.claim: Logistic regression about 18.8% a year, random forest about 29% a year, long-short after costs (level unverified)
high_return_claim.period: Out of sample 18 Jun to 17 Sep 2018 (three months), 120-minute horizon, 40 coins
high_return_claim.drawdown: not reported in what was read
high_return_claim.leverage: long-short; the short leg needs borrowing
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: Yes, but three months only; no later replication found

priority_reason: Cheap, already a model-lab contestant, and the right floor for any ML model; but no long-only after-cost crypto evidence, and the published alpha is long-short.

name: Random forest / extremely randomised trees
summary: A random forest on technical and lagged-return features classifies the next day's direction (Gradojevic et al.) or whether a coin beats the cross-sectional median (Fischer et al.); long when the predicted probability is high.
data_note: OHLCV only.

sources.citation: Gradojevic, N., Kukolj, D., Adcock, R., Djakovic, V. (2023), Forecasting Bitcoin with technical analysis: a not-so-random forest?, International Journal of Forecasting 39(1)
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence] Hourly: no model beats the random walk. Daily: a random forest with technical features beats the random walk significantly (forecast test, no trading costs).

sources.citation: Fischer, T.G., Krauss, C., Deinert, A. (2019), Statistical arbitrage in cryptocurrency markets, Journal of Risk and Financial Management 12(1), 31
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence] Random forest on lagged returns: 7.1 bp a day after costs, about 29% a year, long-short, out of sample 18 Jun to 17 Sep 2018 only; authors flag volume limits.

crypto_evidence_note: Daily forecastability beyond a random walk is shown for BTC, but the only trading result is long-short over three months at low costs.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: As a daily gate: at most the base rule's 3-12; stand-alone daily long/flat: 20-60 round trips [R].
fee_sensitivity: Stand-alone daily trading costs 22-66% a year; only a cost-thresholded gate is plausible.
long_only_note: Long or cash; Fischer et al.'s result is long-short.
limitations: Largely duplicates gradient boosting
Forecast tests are not trading tests
Three-month trading sample in Fischer et al.

high_return_claim.claim: About 29% a year (7.1 bp a day) long-short after costs
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: Yes, three months; no replication found

priority_reason: One of the few models shown to beat a random walk on daily BTC out of sample, but no long-only after-cost test; overlaps the HistGB contestant.

name: Stacking and agreement ensembles
summary: Combine several base models (e.g. gradient boosting, logistic regression, random forest, SVC) by averaging, stacking or unanimous agreement; Sebastiao and Godinho trade only when five models agree.
data_note: Sebastiao and Godinho add network (on-chain) features; OHLCV-only versions are possible.

sources.citation: Sebastiao, H., Godinho, P. (2021), Forecasting and trading cryptocurrencies with machine learning under changing market conditions, Financial Innovation 7
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence] Best ensemble traded only when 5 models agreed: 9.62% a year (ETH) and 5.73% (LTC) after a 0.5% round-trip cost, test 13 Apr 2018 to 3 Mar 2019 (a bear market), best of many variants.

sources.citation: Borges, T.A., Neves, R.F. (2020), Ensemble of machine learning algorithms for cryptocurrency investment with different data resampling methods, Applied Soft Computing 90, 106187
sources.finding: [S] Ensemble classifier for trading on crypto exchanges with resampled (non-time) bars; the related book combines gradient tree boosting, logistic regression, random forest and SVC. Results not read.

sources.citation: Thumm, D., Barucca, P., Joubert, J.F. (2022), Ensemble meta-labeling, Journal of Financial Data Science
sources.finding: [S, repository summary] Ensembles appear most useful when data span multiple regimes and are non-linear.

crypto_evidence_note: The closest-cost crypto study (0.5% round trip, about half ours) is positive for ETH and LTC but covers one bear year and reports the best of many variants.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Agreement rules trade less than any member; as a daily gate at most the base rule's 3-12 [R].
fee_sensitivity: Unanimity cuts turnover, which helps at 1.10% a round trip; still needs an explicit cost threshold.
long_only_note: Long or cash.
limitations: Combining weak learners does not create an edge none of them has
More configurations means more trials to correct for
One-year test in the closest study
priority_reason: The only crypto ML study near our cost level used an agreement ensemble; cheap once base contestants exist, but evidence is thin and selection-biased.

name: Bayesian neural networks and Bayesian regression
summary: Bayesian neural networks (or Bayesian linear models) give a posterior predictive distribution for the next return or price; trade when the posterior probability of a gain exceeds a threshold. Jang and Lee add blockchain features.
data_note: Jang and Lee use blockchain supply/demand features in addition to prices; basic on-chain series for BTC are free, coverage for other coins varies.

sources.citation: Jang, H., Lee, J. (2018), An empirical study on modeling and prediction of Bitcoin prices with Bayesian neural networks based on blockchain information, IEEE Access 6, 5427-5437
sources.finding: [A] A BNN with blockchain features predicted Bitcoin log price and volatility well against linear and non-linear benchmarks; a forecasting study with no trading or costs.

sources.citation: Koki, C., Leonardos, S., Piliouras, G. (2022), Exploring the predictability of cryptocurrencies via Bayesian hidden Markov models, Research in International Business and Finance 59
sources.finding: [A] Bayesian HMMs with 2-5 states on BTC, ETH and XRP returns; the four-state non-homogeneous HMM gave the best one-step-ahead forecasts. Forecasting only.

crypto_evidence_note: Forecast-accuracy studies only; no after-cost trading evidence found.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Depends on the threshold; as a daily gate at most the base rule's 3-12 [R].
fee_sensitivity: Same as any daily classifier: only a cost-thresholded gate is plausible. The posterior spread helps set that threshold.
long_only_note: Long or cash.
limitations: Price-level forecasting, not trading
Heavier to fit than calibrated tree models
On-chain features need a data source per coin
priority_reason: No trading evidence; its main benefit (uncertainty estimates) can be had more cheaply through calibrated probabilities.

name: Genetic programming / evolved trading rules
summary: A genetic program searches the space of technical-rule expressions, selecting rules on in-sample (and validation) returns, then trades the best evolved rule out of sample.
data_note: OHLCV only.

sources.citation: Neely, C.J., Weller, P.A. (2001), Intraday technical trading in the foreign exchange market, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis Working Paper 1999-016B
sources.finding: [A] Rules from a genetic program and an optimised linear model: 'When realistic transaction costs and trading hours are taken into account, we find no evidence of excess returns.'

sources.citation: Neely, C.J., Weller, P.A., Dittmar, R. (1996), Is technical analysis in the foreign exchange market profitable? A genetic programming approach, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis Working Paper 96-006
sources.finding: [S, search summary] Daily FX: strong evidence of economically significant out-of-sample excess returns for six exchange rates.

crypto_evidence_note: No crypto GP study with out-of-sample after-cost results was confirmed; FX evidence is positive at daily and negative intraday after costs.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Depends on the evolved rule; unconstrained searches favour active rules [R].
fee_sensitivity: Costs must sit inside the fitness function; otherwise the search selects high-turnover rules that fail at 1.10% a round trip.
long_only_note: Rules can be restricted to long or cash.
limitations: An extreme multiple-testing problem: every evolved expression is a trial
Hard to explain or audit
No crypto evidence
priority_reason: A rule search with an effectively unbounded trial count, against a 4.3-year sample that supports only a few dozen independent configurations (A report §11).

name: k-nearest-neighbour / analog pattern matching
summary: Find the k most similar past price windows and trade in the direction their subsequent moves took (the legacy STRAT-003 neural pattern model works in this spirit).
data_note: OHLCV only.

sources.citation: Vrinceanu, B.-P., Vriscu, M., Paraschiv, L., Bujdei-Tebeica, V. (2026), Machine learning-based algorithmic trading bots: a comparative study of kNN and LVQ models on Bitcoin markets, Proceedings of the International Conference on Business Excellence 20(1)
sources.finding: [A] Hourly BTC/USDT, January 2025 to January 2026, TradingView bots: the kNN bot 'failed to generate positive cumulative returns'; LVQ was more profitable with significantly higher drawdown. Fees not stated; no buy-and-hold benchmark.

crypto_evidence_note: No credible crypto evidence with costs was found (also C-evidence). The repository's own tests found the neural/pattern entry models no better than random entries.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Hourly legacy engine: tens to hundreds of round trips [R, from the repository's hourly results].
fee_sensitivity: Hourly use is destroyed by 1.10% round trips; daily use would still need a cost threshold.
long_only_note: Long or cash.
limitations: Range/level forecasts are mostly volatility forecasts and say little about direction (A-classic)
No peer-reviewed crypto evidence with costs
Repository tests: no edge over random
priority_reason: Already implemented and already shown no better than random in this repository; external evidence is anecdotal and negative.

name: Recurrent neural networks (LSTM / GRU)
summary: An LSTM or GRU reads a window of past bars (optionally pooled across coins) and outputs the probability of an up move or of hitting a profit barrier; long above a threshold.
data_note: OHLCV only in the cited studies, although Jaquart 2021 adds some blockchain and sentiment features.

sources.citation: Jaquart, P., Dann, D., Weinhardt, C. (2021), Short-term bitcoin market prediction via machine learning, Journal of Finance and Data Science 7
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence] GRU/LSTM and boosting beat a random classifier at 1-60 minutes; long-short returns of up to 39% a month before costs became negative after costs.

sources.citation: Jaquart, P., Kopke, S., Weinhardt, C. (2022), Machine learning for cryptocurrency market prediction and trading, Journal of Finance and Data Science 8
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence] Daily relative moves of the top-100 coins: accuracy 52.9-54.1%; long-short LSTM/GRU Sharpe 3.23/3.12 after costs against 1.33 for buy-and-hold.

sources.citation: Fischer, T., Krauss, C. (2018), Deep learning with long short-term memory networks for financial market predictions, European Journal of Operational Research 270(2)
sources.finding: [A, via B-deep] S&P 500 stocks: 0.46% a day before costs, but since 2010 profitability hovers around zero after costs.

sources.citation: Puoti, Pittorino, Roveri (2024/25), Quantifying cryptocurrency unpredictability, arXiv 2502.09079
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence] For BTC, ETH, XRP, BNB and LTC at 1, 7 and 30 days, naive forecasts beat ARIMA, tree models, RNN, LSTM and N-BEATS.

crypto_evidence_note: Positive only long-short across 100 coins (Jaquart 2022); negative after costs at short horizons and beaten by naive forecasts on large coins. The repository's neural entry models showed no edge over random entries.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Intraday as published: hundreds or more; as a daily gate: at most the base rule's [R].
fee_sensitivity: Destroyed at intraday turnover (Jaquart 2021 is already negative at lower fees); a daily gate is the only form that could survive.
long_only_note: The only positive after-cost result is long-short.
limitations: Data-hungry relative to 9 coins x 4.3 years of daily bars
Unstable across seeds
No evidence of beating trees or naive baselines on large coins

high_return_claim.claim: Up to 39% a month before costs (long-short), negative after costs
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: Yes; the gain does not survive costs

priority_reason: Negative or long-short-only evidence, beaten by naive forecasts on large coins, and already no edge in this repository; try only after simpler models on the same harness.

name: Deep reinforcement learning traders and portfolio agents (DQN, PPO, policy gradient)
summary: An RL agent learns a policy mapping recent prices to positions or portfolio weights by maximising simulated reward net of commission; Jiang et al.'s EIIE agent reallocates a crypto portfolio every 30 minutes.
data_note: OHLCV only.

sources.citation: Jiang, Z., Xu, D., Liang, J. (2017), A deep reinforcement learning framework for the financial portfolio management problem, arXiv 1706.10059
sources.finding: [A] Poloniex, 30-minute periods, 0.25% commission: at least 4-fold returns in 50 days in backtests. The authors' repository notes the v2 test span is about 30% shorter than the actual experiment and warns that slippage and market impact may badly affect live results.

sources.citation: Gort, B., Liu, X.-Y., et al. (2022), Deep reinforcement learning for cryptocurrency trading: practical approach to address backtest overfitting, arXiv 2209.05559 (ACM ICAIF 2022)
sources.finding: [A] Earlier DRL trading papers report inflated backtest profits from overfitting; rejecting agents with a high estimated probability of overfitting gave better results on 10 coins from 1 May to 27 Jun 2022 than overfitted agents, an equal-weight portfolio and the S&P DBM index.

crypto_evidence_note: Headline results are short backtests at high turnover; the main crypto RL paper on method finds the literature's profits are mostly overfitting.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Hundreds to thousands of rebalances at 30-minute steps [R]; even daily agents re-weight constantly unless penalised.
fee_sensitivity: Continuous re-weighting is ruinous at 0.55% a side; only an agent constrained to rare, large moves could survive, which removes most of RL's flexibility.
long_only_note: Portfolio agents with non-negative weights are long-only by construction.
limitations: Severe backtest overfitting (Gort et al.)
Short test windows
Reward and environment design choices act as hidden parameters

high_return_claim.claim: At least 4-fold returns in 50 days after 0.25% commission
high_return_claim.period: Poloniex backtests, 50-day test windows (dates not read)
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: Backtest only; the authors' repository says the reported test span is shorter than the experiment and warns live results may differ badly

priority_reason: High turnover, documented overfitting and short tests; no after-cost evidence at retail fees.

name: Support vector machine classifier
summary: An SVM classifier predicts next-period direction from technical features; long on an 'up' prediction. Akyildirim et al. found it the most accurate of four classifiers on 12 liquid coins.
data_note: OHLCV only.

sources.citation: Akyildirim, E., Goncu, A., Sensoy, A. (2021), Prediction of cryptocurrency returns using machine learning, Annals of Operations Research 297
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence] SVM was the best of four classifiers, with 55-65% average direction accuracy on 12 liquid coins at daily and minute frequencies; no after-cost trading result was verified.

sources.citation: scikit-learn developers, sklearn.svm.SVC documentation
sources.finding: [FT, via A-classic] SVC fit time scales at least quadratically with sample count and may be impractical beyond tens of thousands of samples; its probability option is deprecated in favour of calibration.

crypto_evidence_note: Accuracy above 50% reported, but no trading-after-cost result; accuracy alone does not imply profit at 1.10% a round trip.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Stand-alone daily: 20-60 round trips [R]; as a gate: at most the base rule's.
fee_sensitivity: Daily stand-alone use costs 22-66% a year; needs a cost threshold and calibrated probabilities.
long_only_note: Long on 'up', else cash.
limitations: No calibrated probabilities without extra work
Scales poorly to pooled hourly data
Accuracy-only evidence
priority_reason: Accuracy-only evidence, poor scaling and no probability output; gradient boosting covers the same ground better.

name: Temporal convolutional networks (TCN / ModernTCN)
summary: Dilated causal convolutions over a window of past bars forecast the next return or direction; trade on the forecast sign or a threshold.
data_note: OHLCV only.

sources.citation: Saidd (2026), arXiv 2603.16886 (benchmark of 9 deep architectures on hourly OHLCV)
sources.finding: [A, via B-deep] 918 runs, 9 architectures, hourly OHLCV for 12 assets including 4 crypto: ModernTCN was best by RMSE and PatchTST second, yet mean directional accuracy was 50.08%.

crypto_evidence_note: Best-by-error deep models still had coin-flip direction accuracy; no after-cost crypto TCN trading study was found.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Hourly sign trading: hundreds [R]; as a daily gate: at most the base rule's.
fee_sensitivity: No margin at 50% direction accuracy; any turnover is pure cost.
long_only_note: Long or cash.
limitations: Lowest forecast error does not mean useful direction
No crypto trading evidence with costs
priority_reason: Coin-flip direction accuracy in the only multi-architecture test found; no reason to expect more than trees.

name: Transformer forecasters (iTransformer, PatchTST, Informer, Autoformer, TimesNet)
summary: Attention-based sequence models trained on past bars forecast returns or direction; trade on sign or a cost threshold.
data_note: OHLCV only.

sources.citation: Bysik, Slepaczuk (2026), Machine learning-based Bitcoin trading under transaction costs, arXiv 2606.00060
sources.finding: [A, via C-evidence] iTransformer was not shown to beat XGBoost or LSTM on hourly BTC under 10 bp costs (bootstrap tests).

sources.citation: Zeng, A., Chen, M., Zhang, L., Xu, Q. (2023), Are transformers effective for time series forecasting?, arXiv 2205.13504 (AAAI 2023)
sources.finding: [A, via B-deep] Simple linear models (LTSF-Linear) beat the Transformer forecasters on 9 benchmark datasets.

sources.citation: Li, Y., Luo, B., Wang, Q., Chen, N., Liu, X., He, B. (2024), CryptoTrade: a reflective LLM-based agent to guide zero-shot cryptocurrency trading, EMNLP 2024
sources.finding: [FT] Informer, Autoformer, TimesNet and PatchTST were among the daily BTC/ETH/SOL baselines over 2023 test windows; the authors report the LLM agent beat these time-series baselines.

crypto_evidence_note: No crypto study found where a Transformer beats boosting or simple baselines after costs.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Hourly sign trading: hundreds [R]; daily gate: at most the base rule's.
fee_sensitivity: Same as other deep models: only a daily cost-thresholded gate could survive.
long_only_note: Long or cash.
limitations: Heavy dependencies (torch, lightning)
Benchmark wins do not carry to returns
Linear models match them on standard benchmarks
priority_reason: No evidence of an advantage over trees or linear models, at much higher cost to build and run.

name: Pretrained time-series foundation models (Kronos, Chronos-2, TimesFM, TTM)
summary: A pretrained forecaster (zero-shot or fine-tuned) produces a return distribution for the next bars; long when the forecast's upper probability mass clears the cost hurdle. Kronos is pretrained on candles from 45 exchanges.
data_note: OHLCV only; models are downloaded weights.

sources.finding: [A, via B-deep] On daily crypto, zero-shot TimesFM had a Sharpe ratio of -0.03 before costs.

sources.citation: Kronos authors (2025), Kronos, arXiv 2508.02739 (AAAI 2026)
sources.finding: [A, via B-deep] Pretraining data run to June 2024 and tests start July 2024; on 997 Binance pairs, zero-shot Moirai, TimesFM, MOMENT and Chronos showed near-zero or negative crypto IC; a reviewer notes Kronos averages 10 sampled rollouts against single-forecast baselines.

sources.citation: Moghadasi, Ghaderi (2026), arXiv 2609.10357 (post-release holdout of foundation models)
sources.finding: [A, via B-deep] On data published only after each model's release, pretrained models matched seasonal-naive forecasts on daily exchange rates; their wins elsewhere tracked how familiar the domain was from pretraining.

crypto_evidence_note: Zero-shot crypto results are near zero or negative before costs; the one positive (Kronos) is the authors' own and ensembles rollouts.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: As a daily gate: at most the base rule's; hourly sign trading: hundreds [R].
fee_sensitivity: No demonstrated gross edge, so any turnover is a loss at 1.10% a round trip.
long_only_note: Long or cash.
limitations: Pretraining corpora include crypto history, so any test before the model's cut-off is contaminated
Several weights are non-commercial
CPU latency of seconds per forecast for sampled models
priority_reason: Near-zero or negative crypto evidence, leakage risk before each model's cut-off, and licence limits on some weights; B-deep already ranks them as experiments.

name: LLM context interpretation as a veto or confirmation on rule entries
summary: When a rule (e.g. STRAT-004) fires, an LLM reads a point-in-time context pack (price summary, recent headlines) and returns confirm or veto; the entry is taken only on confirm. The app's llm_gate scores this against random vetoes at the same rate.
data_note: Price context is free; headline context needs a news feed; each decision costs an API call.

sources.citation: Glasserman, P., Lin, C. (2023), Assessing look-ahead bias in stock return predictions generated by GPT sentiment analysis, arXiv 2309.17322
sources.finding: [A] The model's own knowledge of a named company distorted its judgement of news (distraction effect); anonymised inputs did better in-sample.

sources.citation: Lopez-Lira, A., Tang, Y., Zhu, M. (2025), The memorization problem: can we trust LLMs' economic forecasts?, arXiv 2504.14765 / SSRN 5217505
sources.finding: [S] Before its cut-off GPT-4o recalled exact S&P 500 levels, unemployment and GDP figures; after the cut-off recall disappears; instructions to respect historical boundaries do not prevent recall-level accuracy; anonymising inputs is proposed.

sources.citation: Li, W., Kim, H., Cucuringu, M., Ma, T. (2025), Can LLM-based financial investing strategies outperform the market in long run? (FINSABER), arXiv 2505.07078
sources.finding: [A] Over two decades and 100+ symbols, reported LLM advantages deteriorate; LLM strategies are overly conservative in bull markets (underperforming passive benchmarks) and overly aggressive in bear markets.

crypto_evidence_note: No study of an LLM veto layer on technical entries was found; the related evidence warns of leakage and of LLM conservatism in bull markets, which is when a trend rule earns most [R].
expected_trades_per_coin_year: At most the base rule's 3-8 round trips; only removes trades. About 30-70 LLM calls a year across nine coins at that rate [R].
fee_sensitivity: Cannot add trading costs; API costs are small at this call rate.
long_only_note: Veto or confirm a long entry.
limitations: Any test before the model's training cut-off is contaminated
Non-deterministic outputs: record every prompt and answer
Few signals per year means years of forward data before a verdict
Model upgrades reset the forward record
priority_reason: Infrastructure already exists (llm_gate with a random-slot baseline) and it can only remove trades, but there is no evidence and a valid test must be forward-only.

name: LLM headline sentiment scores
summary: An LLM rates each new headline about a coin as good, bad or neutral (Lopez-Lira and Tang's prompt); scores are aggregated daily and the coin is held while aggregate sentiment is positive, else cash. The equity studies form next-day long-short portfolios instead.
data_note: Needs a timestamped headline feed per coin; free feeds (e.g. GDELT, RSS) exist, curated feeds (e.g. RavenPack, used by Glasserman and Lin) are paid. Plus API cost per scored headline.

sources.citation: Lopez-Lira, A., Tang, Y. (2023, rev. 2025), Can ChatGPT forecast stock price movements? Return predictability and large language models, arXiv 2304.07619
sources.finding: [A, v6] Using headlines dated after the model's knowledge cut-off, GPT-4 scores significantly predict next-day drift, especially for small stocks and negative news; forecasting ability rises with model size; strategy returns fall as LLM adoption rises. No cost statement in the abstract. An earlier version reported over 500% cumulative long-short returns from October 2021 to December 2022 [S].

sources.citation: Kirtac, K., Germano, G. (2024), Sentiment trading with large language models, Finance Research Letters 62, 105227 (arXiv 2412.19245)
sources.finding: [S, search summary of the preprint] 965,375 US news articles 2010-2023: OPT predicted returns with 74.4% accuracy against 72.2% for FinBERT; an OPT long-short strategy had a Sharpe ratio of 3.05 after 10 bp costs and gained 355% from August 2021 to July 2023; the Loughran-McDonald dictionary managed Sharpe 1.23.

sources.citation: Glasserman, P., Lin, C. (2023), Assessing look-ahead bias in stock return predictions generated by GPT sentiment analysis, arXiv 2309.17322
sources.finding: [A] In-sample, GPT-3.5 headline strategies did better with company names removed: a 'distraction effect' from the model's general knowledge outweighed look-ahead bias, most for large companies; anonymising headlines is proposed for de-biased backtests.

sources.citation: He, S., Lv, L., Manela, A., Wu, J. (2025), Chronologically consistent large language models, arXiv 2502.21206
sources.finding: [A] ChronoBERT/ChronoGPT trained only on text available at each date; their real-time news-based next-day return predictions reach Sharpe ratios comparable to a much larger Llama model; look-ahead bias was modest but depends on model and application.

sources.citation: Sarkar, S.K., Vafa, K. (2024), Lookahead bias in pretrained language models (ICML 2025 poster; NBER version June 2024)
sources.finding: [S] Direct tests, based on events that should be unpredictable from a fixed information set, find look-ahead bias in pretrained models in two settings (risk factors from earnings calls; election winners from biographies); they recommend models whose pretraining text predates the analysis period.

crypto_evidence_note: All return-prediction evidence found is for US equities, next-day, long-short, at 0-10 bp. No crypto study testing LLM news sentiment against returns out of sample was confirmed.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Unsmoothed daily sentiment could switch 20-100 times a year [R]; with multi-day smoothing and a minimum hold, 6-20 [R].
fee_sensitivity: The equity edge is a next-day drift measured at 0-10 bp; at 1.10% a round trip a next-day hold cannot pay. Plausible only as a slow aggregate or as a veto on a trend rule.
long_only_note: Long on positive sentiment, else cash; equity results are long-short and strongest on negative news (the short side).
limitations: Look-ahead and memorisation: only post-cut-off headlines are a valid test
Equity evidence concentrated in small stocks and negative news, neither of which a long-only large-coin book can use
Returns decline as adoption rises (Lopez-Lira and Tang)
API cost and non-deterministic outputs

high_return_claim.claim: [S] OPT sentiment long-short gained 355% (Sharpe 3.05) after 10 bp costs
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: Test window; its relation to OPT's pretraining data was not verified; no independent replication found

priority_reason: The best-evidenced LLM use, but in equities, next-day and long-short; crypto evidence is missing and a clean test needs a post-cut-off forward window and a headline feed.

name: Small finance/crypto sentiment classifiers (FinBERT, CryptoBERT)
summary: A local fine-tuned BERT model (FinBERT for financial news, CryptoBERT for crypto social posts) labels each item bearish, neutral or bullish; daily aggregates feed a signal or veto. No API calls needed.
data_note: The models are free; the text is the bottleneck: social feeds (X, Reddit, StockTwits) have restrictive or paid API terms, news feeds vary (see data_source candidates).

sources.citation: Araci, D. (2019), FinBERT: financial sentiment analysis with pre-trained language models, arXiv 1908.10063
sources.finding: [A] A BERT model further trained on financial text improved every measured metric on two financial sentiment classification datasets; a classification result, not a return test.

sources.citation: Kulakowski, M., Frasincar, F. (2023), Sentiment classification of cryptocurrency-related social media posts, IEEE Intelligent Systems 38(4)
sources.finding: [S] CryptoBERT: BERTweet post-trained on about 3.2 million crypto posts; the released model's head was fine-tuned on 2 million StockTwits posts labelled bearish/neutral/bullish (model card, MIT). No return-prediction test.

sources.citation: Kirtac, K., Germano, G. (2024), Sentiment trading with large language models, Finance Research Letters 62, 105227
sources.finding: [S] On US news 2010-2023, FinBERT predicted returns with 72.2% accuracy against 74.4% for the larger OPT model.

crypto_evidence_note: Classifier accuracy is documented; no study tying these classifiers' crypto outputs to after-cost returns was confirmed. Whether social or news sentiment predicts crypto returns is assessed under the data_source candidates.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Same as the sentiment signal it feeds: 6-20 with smoothing [R]; fewer as a veto.
fee_sensitivity: As for headline sentiment: only slow aggregates or vetoes can survive 1.10% a round trip.
long_only_note: Long or cash.
limitations: Tool, not signal: value depends on the data source
Social posts are noisy and manipulable
StockTwits-style labels are self-reported sentiment, not outcomes
priority_reason: Free, local and deterministic (unlike API LLMs), so cheap to test once a legal text feed exists; no return evidence yet.

name: Autonomous LLM trading agents (single or multi-agent: CryptoTrade, TradingAgents, FinMem, FinAgent)
summary: One or more LLM agents read prices, news and (for CryptoTrade) on-chain data each day and output buy/sell/hold decisions, often with a reflection step that reviews past trades.
data_note: Prices free; news and on-chain inputs vary by source; CryptoTrade's released dataset is CC BY-NC-SA. Heavy API cost (several calls per agent per day).

sources.citation: Li, Y., Luo, B., Wang, Q., Chen, N., Liu, X., He, B. (2024), CryptoTrade: a reflective LLM-based agent to guide zero-shot cryptocurrency trading, EMNLP 2024, 1094-1106
sources.finding: [FT] Daily BTC/ETH/SOL, 2023 test windows. Bull (Oct-Dec 2023): BTC buy-and-hold 39.66% vs GPT-4o agent 28.47%; SOL 176.72% vs 115.18%; ETH 22.59% vs 25.47%. Bear (Apr-Jun 2023): agent lost less on all three coins (e.g. SOL -16.32% vs -36.08%). Fee rate not stated. Tests chosen after GPT-3.5's cut-off; GPT-4/4o cut-offs not stated.

sources.citation: Li, X., Zeng, Y., Xing, X., Xu, J., Xu, X. (2025), Profit mirage: revisiting information leakage in LLM-based financial agents, arXiv 2510.07920
sources.finding: [FT, section 2] FinMem, FinAgent, QuantAgent, FinCON and TradingAgents on GPT-4o (cut-off October 2023), NASDAQ-100: from a pre-cut-off window (Q2-Q3 2021) to a post-cut-off window (Q3-Q4 2024), Sharpe ratios fell 51.48-62.23% and total returns 50.18-71.85%, although market returns were similar (+13.79% vs +13.35%).

sources.citation: ForkLog (2025), Four out of six AI models suffer losses in trading tournament (Alpha Arena season 1, nof1)
sources.finding: [FT] Live, real money, $10,000 each, 18 Oct to 3 Nov 2025. Final balances: Qwen3 Max $12,231, DeepSeek $10,489, Claude Sonnet 4.5 $5,799, Gemini 2.5 Pro $5,445, Grok $4,208, GPT-5 $4,126. Other coverage [S] says the venue was Hyperliquid crypto perpetuals (BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, DOGE, XRP). End balances differ between news reports (other coverage gives GPT-5 about $3,733); the official nof1 leaderboard was not read.

sources.citation: Yu, H., Li, F., You, J. (2025), LiveTradeBench: seeking real-world alpha with large language models, arXiv 2511.03628
sources.finding: [S] 50-day live evaluations of 21 LLMs on US stocks and Polymarket: high LMArena scores do not imply better trading outcomes.

sources.citation: Li, W., Kim, H., Cucuringu, M., Ma, T. (2025), FINSABER, arXiv 2505.07078
sources.finding: [A] Over two decades and 100+ symbols, previously reported LLM-agent advantages deteriorate significantly.

crypto_evidence_note: The crypto agent paper trails buy-and-hold in BTC and SOL bull markets and its tests fall inside GPT-4o's likely training window [R]; the one live crypto contest lost money for four of six models; leakage studies show post-cut-off decay of 50-72%.

reference_implementations.name: CryptoTrade (code and data)
reference_implementations.licence: CC BY-NC-SA (stated for the dataset; LICENSE file not read)

expected_trades_per_coin_year: Daily decisions: 20-100+ position changes a year [R]; Gemini's erratic frequent trading was cited in Alpha Arena coverage [S].
fee_sensitivity: Daily discretionary trading at 1.10% a round trip costs 22-110% a year; the agents shown do not have an edge of that size.
long_only_note: Can be restricted to spot long/cash; Alpha Arena used leveraged perpetuals, which this app cannot.
limitations: Leakage: pre-cut-off backtests overstate results by about half (Profit Mirage)
Non-deterministic, unrepeatable decisions
One 17-day live contest with six models is indistinguishable from luck [R]
High API cost

high_return_claim.claim: Qwen3 Max +22.3% (from $10,000 to $12,231) in a live contest; four of six models lost 42-59%
high_return_claim.drawdown: DeepSeek peaked above $13,000 before ending at $10,489; others not read
high_return_claim.leverage: crypto perpetuals with leverage allowed [S]; level not read
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: Live and after every model's cut-off, but one short run with n = 6

priority_reason: Negative live crypto evidence, documented leakage, high turnover and API cost; the veto form keeps the useful part at a fraction of the risk.

name: LLM hypothesis and alpha-factor generation
summary: LLM agents propose trading hypotheses or factor formulas, which are coded and backtested; AlphaAgent adds originality, hypothesis-alignment and complexity regularisation to fight crowding and decay.
data_note: Uses whatever data the generated factors need; OHLCV in the cited study.

sources.citation: Tang, Z., et al. (2025), AlphaAgent: LLM-driven alpha mining with regularized exploration to counteract alpha decay, arXiv 2502.16789
sources.finding: [S] Three LLM agents (idea, factor, evaluation) with originality, alignment and complexity constraints; on CSI 500 and S&P 500 over four years the authors report an 81% higher effective-factor hit ratio with 30% fewer tokens and more decay-resistant factors.

sources.citation: Arnott, R., Harvey, C.R., Markowitz, H. (2019), A backtesting protocol in the era of machine learning, Journal of Financial Data Science 1(1), 64-74
sources.finding: [A] A seven-step protocol: a prior economic hypothesis, careful multiple-testing adjustment, cross-validation, monitoring of model dynamics, simplicity, and incentives that reward method over backtest results.

crypto_evidence_note: No crypto test found; equity results are the authors' own.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Not a signal; depends on the generated rule.
fee_sensitivity: Generated rules must be scored net of 1.10% a round trip from the start.
long_only_note: Generated rules can be constrained to long or cash.
limitations: Every generated hypothesis is a trial against a budget of a few dozen configurations for 4.3 years (A report §11)
LLMs may regurgitate published anomalies that have already decayed
The research process, not the trading, is what it speeds up
priority_reason: A research aid, not a signal; it multiplies trials faster than the 4.3-year sample can test them honestly.

name: ATR stops: trailing (chandelier) stop and ATR-based stop distance (Turtle 2N)
summary: Trail a stop at price minus k x ATR, raised only upward for longs, and exit on a close below it. Turtle rules use 2 x ATR(20); Bui and Nguyen report a best region of k = 2.0-3.5, centred near 2.5. ATR(n) is the Wilder-smoothed mean true range (n = 14 by convention; the Turtles used N = ATR(20) for stops at 2N and for unit sizing).
data_note: OHLC for ATR. No trade or order-book data needed.

sources.citation: Bui, D., Nguyen, T. (2026), Systematic trend-following with adaptive portfolio construction: enhancing risk-adjusted alpha in cryptocurrency markets, arXiv 2602.11708 (Talyxion Research)
sources.finding: [FT] Long-short (70/30) Binance perpetuals, out of sample Jan 2022-Dec 2024, parameters re-optimised monthly: removing the ATR trailing stop lowers Sharpe from 2.41 to 1.68 and deepens max drawdown from -12.7% to -22.4%. Costs: 4 bp taker, slippage, funding.

sources.citation: Original Turtle Trading Rules (Faith 2003), chapter 5, reproduced on a community blog
sources.finding: [S] N is the 20-day average true range; stops are set 2N from entry, with units sized from N. Secondary reproduction; the A-research-report's Garner (2010) gives the same 2 ATR(20) stops.

sources.citation: Zarattini, C., Pagani, A., Barbon, A. (2025), Catching crypto trends: a tactical approach for Bitcoin and altcoins, SFI Research Paper 25-80, SSRN 5209907
sources.finding: [FT, via A-research-report.md] Volatility sizing min(25%/σ, 200%) with σ from 90 days, and a trailing stop never lowered. It uses volatility sizing and a channel stop rather than ATR.

crypto_evidence_note: Only one crypto ablation, from a practitioner preprint on a tuned long-short perpetuals system at about 1/14 of this account's fees. Its Sharpe arithmetic does not reconcile with its own return and volatility. No study isolates ATR stops against no stop or random stops in long-only spot crypto; OVL-ATR has not been evaluated in the repo.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: As the only exit on daily bars at k = 2-3.5, roughly 2-8 exits per coin-year [R]; beside a Donchian exit it only makes some exits earlier.
fee_sensitivity: Smaller k means more exits and re-entries at 1.10% each. Below about 2 ATR on 1h/4h bars, fees dominate (consistent with the repo's hourly losses).
long_only_note: Long-only form is natural: the stop only rises.
limitations: Single preprint, long-short perpetuals, monthly re-tuning
k is a free parameter
Gaps through the stop
Effect not isolated for long-only spot
Stops can turn trend winners into whipsaw losses
No crypto evidence of value
Weekend gaps do not exist, but wicks on thin coins trigger stops

high_return_claim.claim: Full system: 40.5% a year, Sharpe 2.41, net of 4 bp taker, slippage and funding
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: Walk-forward with monthly grid re-optimisation; preprint, no post-publication record

priority_reason: Already implemented; test as an exit policy on daily strategies at k 2-3.5; evidence weak and from a very different cost setting. (Merged with volatility.atr-stops-and-sizing.)

name: Fixed-fraction sizing with exchange minimums (small accounts)
summary: Risk a fixed fraction of equity per entry, raised to the exchange's notional minimum order and capped per coin. The app uses a 1% entry raised to the exchange minimum, with at most 10% per coin.
data_note: Needs each product's minimum order from the exchange's public product endpoint (no authentication).

sources.citation: Coinbase Developer Platform (2026), Exchange REST API: Get all known trading pairs (products)
sources.finding: [FT] 'The property, min_market_funds, has been repurposed as the notional minimum size for limit orders'. Base-size limits were removed (June 2022). The minimum is per product; the page gives no single figure.

sources.citation: Coinbase Developer Platform (2026), Advanced Trade API: Get Public Product
sources.finding: [FT] quote_min_size is the 'Minimum size that can be represented of quote currency'. The endpoint needs no authentication.

crypto_evidence_note: An execution constraint, not a return source. Account-size effects follow from arithmetic [R], not from a study.

reference_implementations.name: ccxt (market limits: amount/cost minimums per exchange)

expected_trades_per_coin_year: Adds none; it sets the size of the base strategy's trades.
fee_sensitivity: Percentage fees cost the same share at any size. But at GBP 50 a 1% entry (GBP 0.50) is below a ~$1 minimum, so each entry is about 2% of equity or more, and a 10% per-coin cap allows only about 5 minimum orders per coin [R].
long_only_note: Spot only; no leverage.
limitations: The ~$1 minimum is the app's own figure; no official Coinbase page giving a single number was found
At GBP 50 to GBP 200, DCA ladders and multi-tranche entries hit the minimum or the per-coin cap
At GBP 10,000 a 1% entry (GBP 100) is far below any liquidity limit for these coins
priority_reason: Infrastructure every test needs: backtests must apply the same minimum and caps at GBP 50, 200, 500 and 10,000.

name: Ratchet (never-lower) trailing stop
summary: A trailing stop that can only rise: stop(t+1) = max(stop(t), reference(t)). In Zarattini, Pagani and Barbon the reference is the Donchian channel midline, and the position exits on the first close below the stop.
data_note: Daily OHLC only.

sources.citation: Zarattini, C., Pagani, A., Barbon, A. (2025), Catching crypto trends: a tactical approach for Bitcoin and altcoins, Swiss Finance Institute RP 25-80, SSRN 5209907
sources.finding: [FT, per A report] 'we never allow the trailing stop to be updated downward'. The 10-coin long-only book, net of 10 bp, has Sharpe 1.50 and max drawdown 12%. At 50 bp the 5-day model's CAGR falls from 34% to 18%; longer lookbacks are less affected.

sources.citation: CXO Advisory (2025), summary of Zarattini, Pagani and Barbon
sources.finding: [S] Jan 2015 to mid-March 2025: 18% net CAGR and 11% annualised net alpha against Bitcoin buy-and-hold, at 0.10% costs; 0.25% and 0.50% also considered.

crypto_evidence_note: Positive only as part of the whole breakout design; the ratchet's own contribution was not isolated. The paper is a working paper, with settings chosen after exploration.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Same as the entry rule it serves: 3-8 round trips per coin-year at 20-60 day lookbacks (Zarattini et al. Bitcoin counts, per A report).
fee_sensitivity: Neutral by itself: it decides when to exit, not how often to enter. At 3-8 round trips the drag is about 3-9% a year.
long_only_note: Designed for long-only; the long-only book beat long-short in the same paper.
limitations: Not ablated separately in the source
Headline costs are 5.5 times lower than this account's
The source sizes up to 200% with leverage; spot caps at 100%

high_return_claim.claim: Long-only Donchian ensemble with ratchet exit: 18% net CAGR, 11% a year net alpha against BTC; Sharpe 1.50 (10-coin book)
high_return_claim.leverage: Volatility sizing min(25%/sigma, 200%), so up to 2x
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: Backtest on a survivorship-free universe; no post-publication record yet; the portfolio result at 0.50% was not verified

priority_reason: Already implemented and part of the best-evidenced long-only design; test with STRAT-004 exits rather than alone.

name: Stop-loss exit (fixed loss threshold)
summary: Exit a position when its loss from entry passes a preset threshold (Han, Zhou and Zhu test 10%, 15% and 20%), then wait for the base strategy's next entry. Kaminski and Lo model it as moving to a safe asset after a cumulative-loss threshold.
data_note: Daily OHLC is enough: the daily low shows whether the stop was hit. No trade or order-book data needed.

sources.citation: Kaminski, K.M., Lo, A.W. (2014), When do stop-loss rules stop losses?, Journal of Financial Markets 18, 234-254
sources.finding: [A] On index futures, 'at longer sampling frequencies, certain stop-loss policies can increase expected return while substantially reducing volatility'. The open-access MIT copy's summary says stops cannot add value under a random walk and need momentum or regime switching to help [S].

sources.citation: Han, Y., Zhou, G., Zhu, Y. (2016), Taming momentum crashes: a simple stop-loss strategy, SSRN working paper (read via CXO Advisory's summary)
sources.finding: [S] US stocks 1926-2013, long-short momentum, 15% stop: worst month -49.8% to -17.4%; average 0.99% to 1.93% a month; Sharpe 0.17 to 0.40. All gross of costs; stop turnover is higher (winner side 39% to 49%).

sources.citation: Sadaqat, M., Butt, H.A. (2023), Stop-loss rules and momentum payoffs in cryptocurrencies, Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Finance 39, 100833
sources.finding: [A] 147 coins, Jan 2015 to Jun 2022: stop-loss momentum gives 'exceedingly higher returns, the Sharpe ratio, and alphas' than benchmark momentum strategies, in all market states. The abstract gives no cost level and no long/short split.

crypto_evidence_note: One crypto study, read only in abstract, on cross-sectional momentum portfolios, not single-coin long-only trend. Theory says stops help only when returns trend or switch regime.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Adds 0-3 round trips per coin-year to a daily trend strategy, since each stop-out and later re-entry is an extra round trip [R estimate; no crypto count published].
fee_sensitivity: Each stop-out and re-entry costs 1.10%; two extra a year is about 2.2% drag. Stops tighter than about 10% on coins with 60-100% yearly volatility would fire often; only wide stops are plausible.
long_only_note: Natural: sell to cash. The app can check closes rather than rest stop orders on the exchange.
limitations: Equity evidence is long-short and gross of costs
Crypto study read in abstract only
Gap risk: a daily close can fall far through the stop
The threshold is a tuned parameter: count each value as a trial (PBO/DSR)

high_return_claim.claim: US stock momentum with a 15% stop: 1.93% a month against 0.99% without (gross of costs, long-short)
high_return_claim.out_of_sample: Not crypto; gross; CXO warns of data snooping; no post-publication test found

priority_reason: Cheap to test on STRAT-004/005 exits with OHLCV; theory and one crypto study support it; must be wide to avoid fee churn.

name: Re-entry cooldown and time stop
summary: After an exit, block re-entry in that coin for N bars (cooldown). Optionally, exit a position that has made no progress after N bars (time stop).
data_note: Bar timestamps only.

sources.citation: Kaminski, K.M., Lo, A.W. (2014), When do stop-loss rules stop losses?, Journal of Financial Markets 18, 234-254
sources.finding: [A] Frames a stop-loss as a policy that reduces exposure after losses, with value depending on whether returns trend; it does not test the length of a re-entry delay.

crypto_evidence_note: No study of entry cooldowns or time stops was found in this session. The case for a cooldown is fee arithmetic: it can only remove re-entries.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: A cooldown only removes re-entries (zero added trades). A time stop adds exits, perhaps +1-3 per coin-year on daily strategies [R].
fee_sensitivity: A cooldown saves 1.10% for each whipsaw re-entry it blocks. A time stop costs 1.10% for each exit followed by a re-entry.
long_only_note: Natural.
limitations: No published evidence found
The cooldown length is a tuned parameter
It can miss the real breakout after a false one
priority_reason: Already implemented and cheap, but untested in the literature; evaluate as a whipsaw filter on hourly or 4h strategies only.

name: Kelly and fractional Kelly sizing
summary: Size each position at the growth-optimal fraction (for small, roughly normal bets f* is about mu / sigma^2), usually scaled to half Kelly or less because mu and sigma are estimates.
data_note: Needs a reliable estimate of each strategy's expected return per trade, which the app's tests have not yet produced.

sources.citation: MacLean, L.C., Thorp, E.O., Ziemba, W.T. (2011), Good and bad properties of the Kelly criterion, ch. 39 in The Kelly Capital Growth Investment Criterion, World Scientific
sources.finding: [A] Summarises 'the good and bad properties of the Kelly criterion and its variants'. Secondary summaries [S] list the main bad property as large losses in bad scenarios from very large bets, which fractional Kelly reduces at some cost in growth.

sources.citation: Perrenod, S. (n.d.), Kelly criterion for Bitcoin, Substack
sources.finding: [S] A blog estimate of a Kelly allocation between Bitcoin and cash from a few years of monthly data. Illustrative only; figures not checked.

crypto_evidence_note: No peer-reviewed crypto study of Kelly sizing was found. The theory is sound, but it needs a known edge.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Adds none if sized once at entry; re-sizing towards the target fraction would add partial fills.
fee_sensitivity: Size once at entry. Each re-sizing fill costs 0.55% of the amount traded.
long_only_note: Capped at 100% of the allocation on spot, with no leverage. A negative Kelly fraction means no trade, not a short.
limitations: Needs a measured edge, and the app's results show none above random entries so far
Estimation error in mu makes full Kelly dangerous
Fat tails and serial dependence break its assumptions
priority_reason: Only useful once a strategy shows a stable net edge; until then the Kelly fraction is about zero.

name: Profit targets and staged profit lock
summary: Exit at a fixed gain from entry (Oxford Strat test: +2% to +100%), or raise the stop to lock in a share of open profit once set gains are reached (staged profit lock).
data_note: OHLC only.

sources.citation: Oxford Capital Strategies (n.d.), Profit-taking: Perry Kaufman, trading strategy test period 1
sources.finding: [FT] 42 futures, 1980-2011, EMA-turn entries, 6 x ATR(20) stop, 1% fixed-fraction sizing: 'Simple profit targets reduce absolute returns and risk-adjusted returns'. Results are charts only, at $0 and $100 a round turn. The page reports Kaufman's opposite 1995 view from 3 markets.

crypto_evidence_note: No crypto study of profit targets or staged profit locks was found. The only test found is a practitioner futures study, and it is negative for fixed targets in trend following.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: If the base strategy re-enters after a target exit, each target hit adds a round trip: about +1-4 per coin-year [R].
fee_sensitivity: Each early exit and re-entry costs 1.10%. Cutting the right tail removes what trend strategies rely on to pay for many small losses.
long_only_note: Natural.
limitations: Evidence is one practitioner futures test
Staged locks are a trailing-stop variant and untested as such
Several stage levels are several tuned parameters
priority_reason: Already implemented and may be cutting winners; worth a single on/off comparison, not tuning.

name: Averaging-down DCA ladder
summary: Add to a losing position at preset falls, lowering its average cost, and exit at a profit target. The legacy engine adds at -2.5% to -50%, each add at 2x the position's value.
data_note: OHLC only.

sources.citation: Hayley, S. (2014), Dynamic strategy bias of IRR and modified IRR: the case of value averaging, City University London
sources.finding: [A, per A report] Strategies that 'double down' after losses bias the IRR, and value averaging 'is inefficient under any plausible investor risk preferences'.

crypto_evidence_note: No empirical study of averaging down, in crypto or elsewhere, was found (A report). With no edge, the expected value is unchanged: many small wins and rare large losses [R].
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Many adds in falling markets: each ladder step is another 0.55% fill; plus one exit per cycle [R].
fee_sensitivity: Each add costs 0.55%, and the profit target must clear the whole position's entry and exit fees.
long_only_note: Long-only by design, but exposure grows into a falling asset.
limitations: Martingale-like exposure growth
At GBP 50-200, 2x adds hit the per-coin cap after one or two steps
Must be tested over the 2018 and 2022 bear markets
priority_reason: No evidence of value; keep with the legacy engine as a control and test it only over full bear markets.

name: Drawdown control: CPPI and account circuit breaker
summary: Hold risky exposure = m x (equity - floor), with the floor fixed or a percentage of peak equity (max-drawdown CPPI). A simpler variant blocks new entries after an X% account drawdown.
data_note: Account equity series only.

sources.citation: Quantpedia (n.d.), Introduction to CPPI - constant proportion portfolio insurance
sources.finding: [S] Exposure is the multiplier times the cushion above the floor. The drawdown variant sets the floor as a share of peak value. A sharp drop between rebalances can breach the floor, and re-entry after full de-risking is the main drawback. In an equity backtest it lowered drawdowns but did not beat SPY.

crypto_evidence_note: No crypto CPPI or drawdown-control study was found. Crypto's large daily moves make gap risk worse [R].
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Continuous CPPI needs frequent rebalancing; with a 10-20% band, perhaps 4-20 adjustments a year [R]. The circuit-breaker variant adds none.
fee_sensitivity: Each adjustment pays 0.55% on the amount traded, so it needs wide bands. The entry-blocking circuit breaker only removes trades.
long_only_note: Natural: exposure between 0 and 100%.
limitations: Gap risk through the floor
Cash lock after a deep fall
The multiplier and floor are tuned parameters
priority_reason: No crypto evidence and turnover cost; the entry-blocking circuit breaker is a cheap safety control rather than a research candidate.

name: Periodic accumulation (dollar-cost averaging) baseline
summary: Invest a fixed amount at fixed intervals (weekly or monthly) instead of a lump sum. Treat it as an execution policy and a baseline, never as a source of return.
data_note: Daily closes.

sources.citation: Williams, R.E., Bacon, P.W. (1993), Lump-sum beats dollar-cost averaging, Journal of Financial Planning 6(2) (AAII reprint)
sources.finding: [FT, per A report] Lump sum 'outperformed dollar cost averaging nearly two-thirds of the time' (S&P 500, 1926-1991).

sources.citation: Finlay, M., Zorn, J. (2023), Cost averaging: invest now or temporarily hold your cash?, Vanguard
sources.finding: [FT pp. 1-3, per A report] Lump sum beat a 3-month split 68% of the time; the split beat holding cash 69% of the time.

sources.citation: Cho, D.D., Kuvvet, E. (2015), Dollar-cost averaging: the trade-off between risk and return, Journal of Financial Planning 28(10)
sources.finding: [FT, per A report] DCA is a trade of lower risk for lower expected return, not a free gain.

crypto_evidence_note: No peer-reviewed crypto DCA study was found (A report; a 2025 Leiria master's thesis on BTC, ETH and XRP was found but not read).
expected_trades_per_coin_year: 12-52 buys per coin-year and no sells.
fee_sensitivity: Each buy pays 0.55%; splitting is about cost-neutral against one buy, provided every tranche clears the minimum. At GBP 50 over 9 coins, weekly tranches fall below ~$1 [R].
long_only_note: Buys only.
limitations: Not a return source
Equity evidence only
Small accounts cannot split finely
priority_reason: A baseline the research needs (accumulation vs lump sum vs strategy), cheap to compute; not a strategy to trade.

name: Equal-weight (1/N) crypto basket
summary: Hold the coin universe in equal weights, rebalanced on a schedule or when weights drift past a band. The market-cap-weighted (BTC-heavy) basket is the alternative benchmark.
data_note: Daily closes of all coins at one instant.

sources.citation: Platanakis, E., Sutcliffe, C., Urquhart, A. (2018), Optimal vs naive diversification in cryptocurrencies, Economics Letters 171
sources.finding: [A] Four cryptocurrencies: 'very little to select between naive diversification and optimal diversification'.

sources.citation: Liu, W. (2019), Portfolio diversification across cryptocurrencies, Finance Research Letters 29, 200-205
sources.finding: [A] Ten major coins: diversification 'can significantly improve the investment results'; out of sample, 'none of the models can consistently beat the naive 1/N portfolio in Sharpe ratio'.

crypto_evidence_note: 1/N is as good as optimised weights out of sample in two small crypto studies. Neither shows it beats Bitcoin alone, and the coins are highly correlated.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Monthly rebalancing means 12 small partial trades per coin-year; quarterly or a +/-20% band means far fewer [R].
fee_sensitivity: The drag is the share of the portfolio traded x 0.55%. With a wide band it is small; daily rebalancing would not survive.
long_only_note: Natural.
limitations: Highly correlated coins: little diversification in crashes
HYPE has a short history
Small accounts: 9 coins x the minimum order limits rebalancing at GBP 50
priority_reason: Equal-weight buy-and-hold of the same coins is the right benchmark for any multi-coin strategy (A report section 8), and cheap to compute.

name: Mean-variance, minimum-variance and Black-Litterman weights
summary: Set coin weights from estimated means and covariances (Markowitz, minimum variance, maximum utility) or from Black-Litterman with variance-based constraints, without shorting.
data_note: Daily returns of all coins.

sources.citation: Platanakis, E., Urquhart, A. (2019), Portfolio management with cryptocurrencies: the role of estimation risk, Economics Letters 177, 76-80
sources.finding: [A] Black-Litterman with variance-based constraints 'yields superior out-of-sample risk-adjusted returns as well as lower risks', 'robust to the inclusion of transaction costs and short-selling'.

sources.citation: Liu, W. (2019), Portfolio diversification across cryptocurrencies, Finance Research Letters 29
sources.finding: [A] The maximum-utility model wins out-of-sample utility, but no model consistently beats 1/N on Sharpe ratio.

sources.citation: Petukhina, A., Trimborn, S., Hardle, W.K., Elendner, H. (2020), Investing with cryptocurrencies: evaluating their potential for portfolio allocation strategies, arXiv 2009.04461
sources.finding: [A] Mean-variance, risk-parity and maximum-diversification portfolios with daily, weekly or monthly rebalancing: crypto improves risk-return, but the illiquidity of cryptocurrencies may reverse these results (LIBRO liquidity constraint).

crypto_evidence_note: Optimisation helps only with heavy shrinkage or constraints (Black-Litterman); plain mean-variance does not beat 1/N. Samples are short and mostly before 2019.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: 12-52 partial rebalances per coin-year at monthly to weekly schedules; fewer with bands [R].
fee_sensitivity: Estimated weights move often, so turnover is higher than 1/N. At 0.55% a side, monthly or banded rebalancing is the only plausible form.
long_only_note: Use the no-short constraint; the published robustness included short-selling variants.
limitations: Estimation error in means
Short, regime-dominated samples
Correlations jump towards 1 in crashes
priority_reason: Mixed evidence, and it needs a multi-coin interface; 1/N should be beaten first.

name: Rebalancing premium (volatility harvesting)
summary: Rebalance a fixed-weight basket (daily, monthly or past a drift band) so it sells relative winners and buys relative losers, harvesting volatility if coins revert against each other.
data_note: Daily closes of all coins.

sources.citation: Quantpedia (2022), Estimating rebalancing premium in cryptocurrencies
sources.finding: [FT] 27 coins, 31.12.2018 to 29.10.2021: daily and monthly rebalanced equal weights beat the drifting equal-weight basket, with higher cumulative return and lower volatility. Costs are not mentioned, so treat it as gross; the figures are in images not read.

sources.citation: Kashyap, R. (2024), To trade or not to trade: cascading waterfall round robin rebalancing mechanism for cryptocurrencies, arXiv 2407.12150
sources.finding: [A] Proposes band-based rebalancing that accounts for 'gas fee and slippage'; no numerical results in the abstract.

crypto_evidence_note: Positive only gross of costs, over one three-year window. Rebalancing is contrarian, while the A report finds large coins show weekly momentum, which works against it.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: Daily: hundreds of small fills; monthly: 12; a +/-20% band: a few [R].
fee_sensitivity: The premium is second-order (driven by the variance of relative returns); at 0.55% a side only wide-band rebalancing could keep any of it [R].
long_only_note: Natural.
limitations: Gross-only evidence from a vendor
Opposes the momentum found in large coins
Minimum orders block small rebalances at GBP 50-200
priority_reason: Cheap to test with the 1/N benchmark (band vs no rebalancing), but the evidence is weak and the fees are against it.

name: Inverse-volatility and risk-parity weights
summary: Weight coins by 1/sigma (inverse volatility) or for equal risk contribution (risk parity), typically from 60-90 day volatility, rebalanced monthly. This avoids estimating expected returns.
data_note: Daily returns of all coins.

sources.citation: Petukhina, A., Trimborn, S., Hardle, W.K., Elendner, H. (2020), Investing with cryptocurrencies, arXiv 2009.04461
sources.finding: [A] Risk parity is among the strategies tested; crypto improves risk-return, but illiquidity may reverse the results.

sources.citation: QuantConnect community (n.d.), Digital asset stockpile: portfolio construction techniques
sources.finding: [S] A community backtest found inverse-volatility and hierarchical-risk-parity baskets underperformed Bitcoin buy-and-hold on a risk-adjusted basis. Figures not checked.

crypto_evidence_note: Inverse-volatility weighting shifts the basket towards BTC, the least volatile coin. No peer-reviewed long-only test against BTC alone was found.
expected_trades_per_coin_year: 12 partial rebalances per coin-year if monthly; fewer with bands [R].
fee_sensitivity: Volatility estimates move, so weights drift; needs a wide no-trade band at 0.55% a side.
long_only_note: Natural. No leverage, so the portfolio cannot reach a volatility target above its natural level.
limitations: Evidence thin and mostly gross
Overlaps with volatility-target sizing (see the volatility family)
Needs a multi-coin interface
priority_reason: Simple and robust in principle, but weak crypto evidence; test after the 1/N benchmark.
